**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):**

**Tafsir (explanation) of Surat al-Anfal**

It is a Medinan surah. [In (د): "Meccan".] Its verses number seventy-six. [In (د, م): "forty-six"; in (أ): "forty-six".] Its words number one thousand, six hundred and thirty-one. [In (د): "one".] Its letters number five thousand, two hundred and ninety-four. [In (د): "seventy".] And Allah knows best.

**In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful**

* *

Al-Bukhari said: Ibn 'Abbas said, "al-Anfal" means "al-ghana'im" (spoils of war). Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Hushaym informed us: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas, "Surat al-Anfal?" He said, "It was revealed concerning Badr."

As for what he (al-Bukhari) reported in suspended form from Ibn 'Abbas, it was similarly narrated by 'Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "al-Anfal" are the spoils of war, which belonged exclusively to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and no one had any share in them. Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, Qatadah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others than one: they are the spoils of war (al-maghanim).

Al-Kalbi said, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: al-Anfal are the spoils of war. In this regard Labid said: "Indeed the piety of our Lord is the best spoil, and by Allah's permission, delay and haste." [The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (13/366) and Lisan al-'Arab, root (n-f-l).]

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Anas informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard a man asking Ibn 'Abbas about "al-Anfal." Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "The horse is from the nafl (bonus), and the spoils (salab) are from the nafl." Then the man returned to his question, and Ibn 'Abbas said that again. Then the man said: "What are the anfal which Allah mentions in His Book?" Al-Qasim said: He kept asking him until he almost upset him. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do you know what the likes of this man are? They are like Sabigh, whom 'Umar ibn al-Khattab beat." [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/364).]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was asked about something, would say: 'I will not command you, nor will I forbid you.'" Then Ibn 'Abbas said: "By Allah, Allah did not send His Prophet (ﷺ) except as one who restrains, commands, makes lawful, and makes unlawful." Al-Qasim said: Then a man was set upon Ibn 'Abbas, asking him about al-Anfal. Ibn 'Abbas said: "A man would grant (yanfulu) another man's horse and his weapon." The man repeated the question to him, and he gave him the same answer. Then he repeated it again until he angered him, and Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do you know what the likes of this man are? They are like Sabigh, whom 'Umar ibn al-Khattab beat, until blood flowed on his heels, or on his legs." Then the man said: "As for you, Allah has taken vengeance for 'Umar against you." [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/231). Sabigh is "Ibn 'Asal," also said to be "Ibn Sahl" al-Tamimi. See his story in al-Isabah (2/198).]

This is a sound chain (isnad) to Ibn 'Abbas, that he explained the nafl as what the imam grants to certain individuals from the spoils, such as the plunder (salab) or the like, after the principal part of the spoils has been divided. This is what most jurists readily understand from the word nafl. And Allah knows best.

'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman... [No: the next is Ibn Abi Najih]. Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: They asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the one-fifth after the four-fifths, and then this was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war﴾. [Reported by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/365).]

Ibn Mas'ud and Masruq said: There is no nafl on the day of the battle-line (zahf); the nafl is only before the ranks meet. Ibn Abi Hatim reported it from both of them.

Ibn al-Mubarak and others than one narrated, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, concerning ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war﴾: "They ask you about what escapes from the polytheists to the Muslims without fighting, of a beast, a slave, a female slave, or property. It is a nafl for the Prophet (ﷺ), who does with it what he wills."

This indicates that he explained al-anfal as al-fay' (what is taken from the disbelievers without fighting).

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: they are the anfal of the expeditions (sara'a). Al-Harith narrated to me: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Salih ibn Hayy narrated to us, who said: It reached me concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war﴾, that he said: "the expeditions."

This means: what the imam grants to some expeditions over and above their share, along with the rest of the army. Al-Sha'bi explicitly stated this. Ibn Jarir chose that they are the additions over the division. What supports this is what has come in the occasion of revelation of the verse, which Imam Ahmad reported, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us: Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah [in (أ): "'Ubayd Allah"] al-Thaqafi, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: On the day of Badr, my brother 'Umayr was killed, and I killed Sa'id ibn al-'As and took his sword, which was called "Dhu al-Kutayfah." I brought it to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Go and throw it in the spoils (al-qabad)." I returned, and I had in me what none knows except Allah, of the killing of my brother and the taking of my spoils. I had not gone far when Surat al-Anfal was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Go and take your sword." [Al-Musnad (1/180).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us: Abu Bakr informed us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Malik, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah has healed me today from the polytheists, so grant me this sword." He said: "This sword is neither for you nor for me; place it." He said: So I placed it, then I returned, saying: "Perhaps this sword will be given today to someone who does not show my valor!" A man called me from behind me. I said: "Has Allah revealed something concerning me?" He said: "You asked me for the sword, and it is not mine, and it has been granted to me, so it is yours." He said: And Allah revealed this verse: ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils are for Allah and the Messenger﴾.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i reported it through several routes, from Abu [Bakr] [addition from (ك, م, أ)] ibn 'Ayyash, with it. [Al-Musnad (1/178); Sunan Abi Dawud (2740); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (3079); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11196).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Likewise, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi reported: Shu'bah informed us, Simak ibn Harb informed us, who said: I heard Mus'ab ibn Sa'd narrating from Sa'd, who said: Four verses were revealed concerning me. I obtained a sword on the day of Badr, and I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Grant me it as a nafl." He said: "Place it where you took it" twice. Then I returned to him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Place it where you took it." Then this verse was revealed: "They ask you about the spoils of war..." [Musnad al-Tayalisi (208).]

The complete hadith concerns the revelation of: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 8] [In (أ): "ihsanan"], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, wine and gambling﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90], and the verse of the bequest (al-wasiyyah). Muslim reported it in his Sahih, from the hadith of Shu'bah, with it. [Sahih Muslim (1748).]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, from some of Banu Sa'idah, who said: I heard Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabi'ah say: "I obtained the sword of Ibn 'A'idh on the day of Badr, and the sword was called al-Marzuban. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the people to return what was in their hands of the nafl, I came with it and threw it into the nafl. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not refuse anything that was asked of him. Al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam al-Makhzumi saw it, asked the Messenger of Allah [(ﷺ)] [addition from (ك, أ)], and he gave it to him." [Reported by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/374) through Ibn Ishaq with it.]

Ibn Jarir also reported it from another route.

**[Another cause of revelation of the verse]:**

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman, from [in (د): "ibn"] Sulayman ibn Musa, from Makhul, from Abu Umamah, who said: I asked 'Ubadah about al-Anfal, and he said: "It was revealed concerning us, the companions of Badr, when we disputed over the nafl and our characters were bad in it, so Allah took it from our hands and placed it with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who divided it among the Muslims equally" — he means: equally. [Al-Musnad (5/322).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us: Abu [in (م, د): "ibn"] Ishaq informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash [in (أ): "'Abbas"] ibn Abi Rabi'ah, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Abu Salam, from Abu Umamah, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: We went out with the Prophet (ﷺ), and I witnessed Badr with him. The people met, and Allah [exalted is He] [addition from (د, م)] defeated the enemy. A group went in pursuit of them, defeating and killing. Another group turned to the camp, collecting and gathering it. Another group encircled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that the enemy would not catch him unawares. When night came and the people returned to one another, those who had gathered the spoils said: "We collected them, so no one has a share in them." Those who had gone out in pursuit of the enemy said: "You are not more entitled to them than us; we kept the enemy away from them and defeated them." Those who had encircled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are not more entitled than us; we encircled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and we feared that the enemy would catch him unawares, so we were occupied with him." Then this was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils are for Allah and the Messenger; so fear Allah and set right what is between you﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided them among the Muslims. [And when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raided into enemy territory, he would grant a quarter as nafl; when he came back with all the people returning, he would grant a third as nafl. He disliked the anfal and would say: "Let the strong among the believers return to their weak."]

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah reported it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, with something similar to it. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith." Ibn Hibban reported it in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith. [Al-Musnad (5/324); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (1561); Sunan Ibn Majah (2852); Sahih Ibn Hibban (1693) "Mawarid"; al-Mustadrak (2/136).] Al-Hakim said: "Sahih in its chain, according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it."

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh (and the wording is his), Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim reported through several routes, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: On the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does such and such, for him is such and such." So the young men competed in that, while the elders remained beneath the banners. When the spoils came, they came seeking what had been promised to them. The elders said: "Do not take precedence over us, for we were a reserve for you; if you had been routed, you would have turned back to us." They disputed, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers﴾. [Sunan Abi Dawud (2737); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (11197); Tafsir al-Tabari (13/368); al-Mustadrak (2/326).]

Al-Thawri also reported, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: On the day of Badr the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever kills an enemy will receive such-and-such, and whoever brings in a captive will receive such-and-such." Then Abu al-Yasar came with two captives and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you promised us." Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you give these to them, nothing will remain for your Companions. We were not prevented from this out of indifference to reward or cowardice before the enemy. We stood in this position only to protect you, fearing that they might come at you from behind." They then disputed, and the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾. He said: The Qur'an was also revealed: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoil, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Anfal: 41]. [Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, no. 9483, from al-Thawri with this chain.]

Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book al-Amwal al-Shar'iyyah wa Bayan Jihatiha wa Masarifiha: As for al-anfal (spoils, or extra portions), they are the spoils, and every gain that the Muslims obtained from the property of the people of war. The first anfal went to the Prophet (ﷺ), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾. So he distributed them on the day of Badr as Allah willed, without taking a khumus (one-fifth) from them, as we mentioned in the hadith of Sa'd. Then the verse of the khumus was revealed afterwards, and it abrogated the first ruling. [al-Amwal, p. 426.]

I say: This is how 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, in the same wording. Mujahid, Ikrimah and al-Suddi also held this view.

Ibn Zayd said: It is not abrogated; rather, it is muhkam (established, not abrogated).

Abu 'Ubayd said: There are reports on this matter. The word al-anfal originally refers to the collection of ghanaim (spoils of war), except that the khumus of it is specifically assigned to its recipients as revealed in the Book and established by the Sunnah. In the usage of the Arabs, al-anfal means any kindness a person does voluntarily, beyond what is obligatory for him. That is the nafl (extra gift) which Allah permitted to the believers from the property of their enemy. It is something Allah specifically granted them out of generosity after the spoils had been forbidden to the nations before them. Allah granted it to this Ummah, and this is the origin of the nafl.

I say: Evidence for this is in the Two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things that no one before me was given," and he mentioned the hadith until he said: "Spoils were made lawful for me, though they were not lawful for anyone before me," and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [See the takhrij (sourcing) of this hadith at the commentary on verse 43 of Surah al-Nisa'.]

Then Abu 'Ubayd said: For this reason, what the leader (imam) gives to the fighters is called nafl. It is his giving some of the army an extra share beyond their regular portions, according to their service to Islam and their effectiveness against the enemy. There are four types of nafl that a leader may grant, each with a place different from the others:

The first: a nafl from which no khumus is taken, and that is the salab (the spoils stripped from a slain enemy).

The second: a nafl taken from the ghanimah after the khumus has been removed. This is when the leader sends detachments into enemy territory, and they bring back spoils. The detachment receives a quarter or a third of what they brought, after the khumus.

The third: a nafl taken from the khumus itself. This is when the entire ghanimah is collected and then divided into fifths, and when the khumus is in the hands of the leader, he gives a nafl from it according to his judgment.

The fourth: a nafl from the whole ghanimah before any part of it is set aside as khumus. This is when guides, herders of livestock and drivers of the animals are given something. There is disagreement over all of these.

Al-Rabi' said: al-Shafi'i said: The anfal are that nothing be taken from the head of the ghanimah before the khumus except the salab.

Abu 'Ubayd said: The second kind of nafl is something they were given in addition to what was already theirs, and it comes from the khumus of the Prophet (ﷺ), for he had one-fifth of the khumus from every ghanimah. The leader should use his judgment: when the enemy is numerous, their strength is great, and the Muslims facing them are few, he gives a nafl from it, following the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). If that is not the case, he does not give a nafl.

The third kind of nafl: when the leader sends a detachment or an army and says to them before the encounter: "Whoever takes any spoil will have it after the khumus." That belongs to them according to what the leader stipulated, because they fought on that basis and they agreed to it. End of his words. [al-Amwal, p. 431.]

Regarding what preceded in his statement, namely his saying "the spoils of Badr were not subjected to khumus," there is room for review. The hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib about his two she-camels, which he received from the khumus on the day of Badr, refutes it. I have explained this fully in my book on the Sirah. [al-Sirah li-Ibn Kathir, 2/466.] And all praise and grace are due to Allah. [Addition from manuscript A.]

* *

As for Allah's saying: ﴿So fear Allah and set right the relations among yourselves﴾: that is, fear Allah in your affairs, and make peace among yourselves. Do not wrong one another, do not quarrel, and do not dispute. What Allah has given you of guidance and knowledge is better than what you dispute over.

﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger﴾: that is, in his division of the spoils among you, as Allah willed, for he divided them as Allah commanded, with justice and fairness.

Ibn 'Abbas said: This is an admonition from Allah to the believers to fear Allah and to set right the relations among themselves. Mujahid also said this.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿So fear Allah and set right the relations among yourselves﴾ means: do not revile one another.

Here we mention a hadith recorded by the Hafiz Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Muthanna al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, in his Musnad. He said: Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Bakr narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn Shaybah al-Habati narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Anas, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting, we saw him laugh until his molars showed. 'Umar said: "What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah? May my father and mother be your ransom." He said: "Two men from my Ummah knelt before the Lord of Might, blessed and exalted. One of them said: 'O Lord, take for me my wrong from my brother.' Allah the Exalted said: 'Give your brother his wrong.' He said: 'O Lord, no good deeds remain to me.' He said: 'O Lord, then let him bear some of my burdens.'" He said: The eyes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) overflowed with weeping. Then he said: "Indeed that is a great day, a day when people need someone to bear some of their burdens for them." Then Allah the Exalted said to the claimant: "Lift your gaze and look at the Gardens." He raised his head and said: "O Lord, I see cities of silver and palaces of gold, adorned with pearls. For which prophet is this? For which truthful one (siddiq) is this? For which martyr is this?" He said: "This is for whoever pays the price." He said: "O Lord, who can own that?" He said: "You own it." He said: "What, O Lord?" He said: "You pardon your brother." He said: "O Lord, I have pardoned him." Allah the Exalted said: "Take your brother by the hand and enter him into Paradise." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "So fear Allah and set right the relations among yourselves, for Allah the Exalted sets right the relations among the believers on the Day of Resurrection." [Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/576), through 'Abdullah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi with this chain. He said: "Its isnad is sahih, but they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi criticized this, saying: "'Abbad ibn Shaybah al-Habati, from Sa'id, is weak, and his shaykh is unknown."]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verse 2–4:

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Only the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾. He said: The hypocrites, the remembrance of Allah does not enter their hearts when performing His obligations, and they do not believe in any of the signs of Allah, nor do they put their trust (in Him), nor do they pray when they are absent, nor do they pay the zakat of their wealth. So Allah informed that they are not believers. Then He described the believers, saying: ﴿Only the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾, and so they fulfilled His obligations. ﴿And when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith﴾, meaning, in certainty. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾, meaning, they hope for none other than Him.

Mujahid said: ﴿Their hearts tremble﴾ means they are frightened and fearful. Likewise said al-Suddi and others.

This is the description of the true believer, who, when Allah is mentioned, his heart trembles, that is, fears Him, so he carries out His commands and abandons what He has forbidden. Like His words: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who can forgive sins except Allah? — and they do not persist in what they have done while they know﴾ [Al 'Imran: 135]. And like His words: ﴿But as for one who feared the standing before his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] desire, indeed, Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 40-41]. For this reason Sufyan al-Thawri said: I heard al-Suddi say concerning His words: ﴿Only the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾:

He said: It is the man who intends to wrong someone — or he said: who intends to commit a sin — and it is said to him: "Fear Allah," and so his heart trembles. [[In M: "fayuwjal".]]

Al-Thawri also said, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', concerning His words: ﴿Only the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾: She said: The trembling in the heart is like the burning of a palm frond. Do you not feel a shiver from it? He said: Yes. She said to me: When you find that, then call upon Allah at that moment, for supplication removes it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith [and upon their Lord they rely]﴾ [[Addition from K.]] are like His words: ﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, among them are those who say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice﴾ [At-Tawbah: 124].

Al-Bukhari and others among the imams have used this verse and similar ones as evidence for the increase of faith and its variation in hearts, as is the position of the majority of the Ummah. Indeed, more than one of the imams has related consensus on this, such as al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Abu 'Ubayd, as we have explained in detail at the beginning of the commentary on Bukhari, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾, meaning: they hope for none other than Him, intend none but Him, seek refuge only in His presence, ask for their needs only from Him, and desire none but Him. They know that whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be, that He alone disposes of the dominion, has no partner, none can repel His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning. For this reason Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Reliance upon Allah is the sum of faith.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Those who establish prayer and from what We have provided them they spend﴾, by this He draws attention to their actions after mentioning their belief. These actions encompass all kinds of good, and the establishment of prayer is the right of Allah, the Exalted.

Qatadah said: Establishing the prayer is preserving its appointed times, its ablution, its bowing, and its prostration.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Its establishment is preserving its appointed times, perfecting its ablution, completing its bowing and prostration, reciting the Qur'an within it, and the tashahhud and sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ). This is its establishment.

Spending from what Allah has provided includes paying zakat and all other rights owed to His servants, whether obligatory or recommended. All of creation are the dependents of Allah, so the most beloved of them to Allah are the most beneficial to His creation.

Qatadah said concerning His words ﴿and from what We have provided them they spend﴾: Spend from what Allah has given you, for these wealths are loans and deposits with you, O son of Adam, and you are about to part with them.

* *

As for His words ﴿Those are the believers in truth﴾, meaning: those who are characterized by these attributes are the believers in true faith.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us, Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Yazid al-Sakuni, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Jahm, from al-Harith ibn Malik al-Ansari; that he passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said to him: "How have you woken up, O Harith?" He said: I have woken up a true believer. He said: "Look at what you are saying, for every truth has a reality. What is the reality of your faith?" He said: My soul has turned away from this world, so I stay awake through my nights and thirst through my days, and it is as if I am looking at the Throne of my Lord openly, and as if I am looking at the people of Paradise visiting one another therein, and as if I am looking at the people of the Fire crying out therein. He said: "O Harith, you have known, so hold fast to it," three times. [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/266). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/57): "In it is Ibn Lahi'ah, and in it is one who needs to be examined."]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verse 2–4:

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Only the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾. He said: The hypocrites, the remembrance of Allah does not enter their hearts when performing His obligations, and they do not believe in any of the signs of Allah, nor do they put their trust (in Him), nor do they pray when they are absent, nor do they pay the zakat of their wealth. So Allah informed that they are not believers. Then He described the believers, saying: ﴿Only the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾, and so they fulfilled His obligations. ﴿And when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith﴾, meaning, in certainty. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾, meaning, they hope for none other than Him.

Mujahid said: ﴿Their hearts tremble﴾ means they are frightened and fearful. Likewise said al-Suddi and others.

This is the description of the true believer, who, when Allah is mentioned, his heart trembles, that is, fears Him, so he carries out His commands and abandons what He has forbidden. Like His words: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who can forgive sins except Allah? — and they do not persist in what they have done while they know﴾ [Al 'Imran: 135]. And like His words: ﴿But as for one who feared the standing before his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] desire, indeed, Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 40-41]. For this reason Sufyan al-Thawri said: I heard al-Suddi say concerning His words: ﴿Only the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾:

He said: It is the man who intends to wrong someone — or he said: who intends to commit a sin — and it is said to him: "Fear Allah," and so his heart trembles. [[In M: "fayuwjal".]]

Al-Thawri also said, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', concerning His words: ﴿Only the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾: She said: The trembling in the heart is like the burning of a palm frond. Do you not feel a shiver from it? He said: Yes. She said to me: When you find that, then call upon Allah at that moment, for supplication removes it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith [and upon their Lord they rely]﴾ [[Addition from K.]] are like His words: ﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, among them are those who say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice﴾ [At-Tawbah: 124].

Al-Bukhari and others among the imams have used this verse and similar ones as evidence for the increase of faith and its variation in hearts, as is the position of the majority of the Ummah. Indeed, more than one of the imams has related consensus on this, such as al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Abu 'Ubayd, as we have explained in detail at the beginning of the commentary on Bukhari, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾, meaning: they hope for none other than Him, intend none but Him, seek refuge only in His presence, ask for their needs only from Him, and desire none but Him. They know that whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be, that He alone disposes of the dominion, has no partner, none can repel His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning. For this reason Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Reliance upon Allah is the sum of faith.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Those who establish prayer and from what We have provided them they spend﴾, by this He draws attention to their actions after mentioning their belief. These actions encompass all kinds of good, and the establishment of prayer is the right of Allah, the Exalted.

Qatadah said: Establishing the prayer is preserving its appointed times, its ablution, its bowing, and its prostration.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Its establishment is preserving its appointed times, perfecting its ablution, completing its bowing and prostration, reciting the Qur'an within it, and the tashahhud and sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ). This is its establishment.

Spending from what Allah has provided includes paying zakat and all other rights owed to His servants, whether obligatory or recommended. All of creation are the dependents of Allah, so the most beloved of them to Allah are the most beneficial to His creation.

Qatadah said concerning His words ﴿and from what We have provided them they spend﴾: Spend from what Allah has given you, for these wealths are loans and deposits with you, O son of Adam, and you are about to part with them.

* *

He said: I have woken up a true believer. He said: "Look at what you are saying, for every truth has a reality. What is the reality of your faith?" He said: My soul has turned away from this world, so I stay awake through my nights and thirst through my days, and it is as if I am looking at the Throne of my Lord openly, and as if I am looking at the people of Paradise visiting one another therein, and as if I am looking at the people of the Fire crying out therein. [[Al-Musnad (3/61); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3987); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3658); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (96).]]

The commentary of Imam Abu Ja'far al-Tabari (Ibn Jarir): The exegetes differed about the reason that brings in this *kaf* (the particle "like," as, in Arabic *kaf al-tashbih*) in His words: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth﴾. Some of them said: it is compared to it in regard to the good state of the believers: their fear of their Lord, their reconciling among themselves, and their obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

Then he narrated similar to this from 'Ikrimah.

The meaning of this is that Allah, exalted is He, says: Just as you disputed over the spoils and contended about them, and Allah took them away from you and placed them under the distribution of Himself and His Messenger ﷺ [[In manuscripts K, M, A: "may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]], and he divided them with justice and equality, and this was the complete benefit for you; likewise, when you disliked going out to face the enemy, to fight the one with the might (the armed force), who are the *nafir* (the armed reinforcement) that went out to defend their religion and to protect their caravan, then the outcome of your dislike of fighting was that He decreed it for you and gathered you with your enemy without prior appointment, and it became right guidance, victory and triumph, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 216].

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: the meaning of that is: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth﴾ despite the dislike of a group of the believers, so likewise they dislike fighting, and they dispute with you about it after it has become clear to them. He narrated something similar from Mujahid, that he said regarding ﴿As your Lord brought you out﴾: Likewise they dispute with you about the truth.

Al-Suddi said: Allah revealed concerning their going out to Badr and their disputing with him: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth, though a party of the believers were averse﴾ to the pursuit of the polytheists, ﴿they dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾.

Some of them said: They ask you about the spoils (*al-anfal*) in dispute, just as they disputed with you on the day of Badr, saying: "You brought us out for the caravan, and you did not inform us of a battle so that we might prepare for it."

I say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only went out from Madinah seeking the caravan of Abu Sufyan, whose news had reached him that it was coming from al-Sham, carrying great wealth for Quraysh. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called upon the Muslims, those who were light (ready to go), and he went out with three hundred and some ten men, and he sought the coastal direction by the way of Badr. Abu Sufyan learned of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ departure in pursuit of him, so he sent Damdam ibn 'Amr as a warner to Makkah. They rose up, nearly a thousand armed men, between nine hundred and a thousand. Abu Sufyan veered with the caravan toward the seaside and escaped. The *nafir* came and reached the water of Badr. Allah gathered the Muslims and the disbelievers without prior appointment, because of what Allah, exalted is He, intended: the elevation of the word of the Muslims, their victory over their enemy, and the distinguishing between truth and falsehood, as its explanation will come.

The purpose: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received word of the *nafir*'s going out, Allah revealed to him, promising him one of the two groups: either the caravan or the *nafir*. Many of the Muslims preferred the caravan, because it was gain without fighting, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you wished that the one without thorns (the unarmed group) would be yours, but Allah intended to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the roots of the disbelievers﴾.

The hadith master Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his *Tafsir*: Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Tabarani narrated to us, Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Aslam Abi 'Imran, that he heard Abu Ayyub al-Ansari say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said while we were in Madinah: "I have been informed about the caravan of Abu Sufyan, that it is approaching. Would you like us to go out before this caravan, perhaps Allah will grant it to us as spoils?" We said: "Yes." So he went out and we went out. When we had traveled a day or two, he said to us: "What do you think about fighting the people, for they have been informed of your departure?" We said: "No, by Allah, we have no strength for fighting the enemy, but we intended the caravan." Then he said: "What do you think about fighting the people?" We said the same as before. Then al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr said: "Then we will not say to you, O Messenger of Allah, as the people of Musa said to Musa: ﴿So go you and your Lord and fight; we are sitting right here﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 24]." He said: Then we, the Ansar, wished that we had said as al-Miqdad said, which would have been more beloved to us than great wealth. He said: So Allah revealed to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth, though a party of the believers were averse﴾, and he mentioned the rest of the hadith [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/174).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah, similarly.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Badr, until when he was at al-Rawha', he addressed the people and said: "How do you see it?" Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have been informed that they are at such-and-such place." Then he addressed the people again and said: "How do you see it?" 'Umar said the same as Abu Bakr's statement. Then he addressed the people again and said: "How do you see it?" Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it us you mean? By Him who honored you with the truth and revealed the Book to you, I have never traversed this route, nor do I have knowledge of it. If you were to travel with us until you reach Bark al-Ghimad in Dhi Yaman, we would march with you. And we would not be like those who said to Musa: ﴿So go you and your Lord and fight, we are sitting right here﴾. Rather, [we say]: Go you and your Lord and fight, we are with you both, following. Perhaps you went out for a matter, and Allah has revealed to you something else, so look at what Allah has revealed to you and proceed with it. Join the ties of whomever you wish, sever the ties of whomever you wish, be hostile to whomever you wish, make peace with whomever you wish, and take from our wealth what you wish." So the Qur'an descended in agreement with Sa'd's statement: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth, though a party of the believers were averse﴾, and the verses that follow.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: When the Prophet ﷺ consulted (the people) about meeting the enemy, and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said what he said, that being on the day of Badr, he ordered the people to get ready for battle and ordered them with the weapon (*al-shawkah*, the armed force). The believers disliked that, so Allah revealed: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth, though a party of the believers were averse. They dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear, as if they were being driven to death while they watch﴾.

Mujahid said: "They dispute with you concerning the truth": concerning the fighting. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿They dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear, as if they were being driven to death while they watch﴾, meaning: out of aversion to meeting the polytheists, and denial of the march of Quraysh when they were mentioned to them.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿They dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾, meaning: after it had become clear to them that you do nothing except what Allah has commanded you.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: it refers to the polytheists.

Yunus narrated to me, informing us Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿They dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear, as if they were being driven to death while they watch﴾: These are the polytheists, who disputed with him about the truth, ﴿as if they were being driven to death﴾ when they are called to Islam, ﴿while they watch﴾. He said: And this is not a description of the others; this is a description specific to the people of disbelief.

Then Ibn Jarir said: There is no sense in what he said, because what comes before His words ﴿They dispute with you concerning the truth﴾ is a report about the people of faith, and what follows it is a report about them as well. The correct view is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Ishaq, that it is a report about the believers.

This, which Ibn Jarir supported, is the truth, and it is what the context of the speech indicates. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr and 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, both saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he had finished with Badr: "Pursue the caravan, nothing stands in your way." Then al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib called out to him, (and 'Abd al-Razzaq said: he was a captive in his bonds), and then they both agreed: "It is not proper for you." He said: "And why?" He said: "Because Allah, mighty and majestic, only promised you one of the two groups, and He has given you what He promised you" [[Al-Musnad (1/229) from the narration of Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, and (1/314) from the narration of 'Abd al-Razzaq.]].

Its chain is good, but they did not bring it out.

The meaning of His words ﴿And you wished that the one without thorns would be yours﴾: that is, they loved that the group which had no might, no strength, and no fighting, would be theirs, and that is the caravan. ﴿And Allah intended to establish the truth by His words﴾: that is, He intended to bring you together with the group that had the might and the fighting, so that He would grant you victory over them and make you prevail over them, and make His religion manifest, and raise the word of Islam, and make it dominant over the religions. Then Ibn Jarir said: There is no sense in what he said, because what comes before His words ﴿They dispute with you concerning the truth﴾ is a report about the people of faith, and what follows it is a report about them as well. The correct view is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Ishaq, that it is a report about the believers.

This, which Ibn Jarir supported, is the truth, and it is what the context of the speech indicates. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr and 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, both saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he had finished with Badr: "Pursue the caravan, nothing stands in your way." Then al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib called out to him, (and 'Abd al-Razzaq said: he was a captive in his bonds), and then they both agreed: "It is not proper for you." He said: "And why?" He said: "Because Allah, mighty and majestic, only promised you one of the two groups, and He has given you what He promised you" [[Al-Musnad (1/229) from the narration of Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, and (1/314) from the narration of 'Abd al-Razzaq.]].

Its chain is good, but they did not bring it out.

The meaning of His words ﴿And you wished that the one without thorns would be yours﴾: that is, they loved that the group which had no might, no strength, and no fighting, would be theirs, and that is the caravan. ﴿And Allah intended to establish the truth by His words﴾: that is, He intended to bring you together with the group that had the might and the fighting, so that He would grant you victory over them and make you prevail over them, and make His religion manifest, and raise the word of Islam, and make it dominant over the religions. He is the most knowing of the ends of matters, and He is the One who arranged for you by His good management, even though people love the opposite of that as it appears to them, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. [And Allah knows, while you know not]﴾ [[Added from manuscripts M, A.]] [Al-Baqarah: 216].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, and Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others of our scholars, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas. Each of them related to me part of this narration, and their accounts combined into what I have set out concerning the Battle of Badr. They said:

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard that Abu Sufyan was approaching from Syria, he called the Muslims to face them and said: "This is the caravan of Quraysh, carrying their wealth. Go out to it; perhaps Allah will grant it to you as spoils." The people responded to the call. Some went out eagerly and some went out reluctantly, for they did not think that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would encounter a fight. Abu Sufyan, when he drew near to the Hijaz, had sent out scouts, gathering news and questioning whoever he met among the riders, being anxious about the affairs of the people, until he received word from one of the riders that Muhammad had called his companions to face you and your caravan. He became wary at that, so he hired Damdam ibn 'Amr al-Ghifari and sent him to the people of Makkah, instructing him to go to Quraysh, summon them to protect their wealth, and inform them that Muhammad had set out against it with his companions. Damdam ibn 'Amr set out quickly for Makkah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also set out with his companions until he reached a valley called "Dhafiran." He left it until, when he was in part of it, he halted, and news reached him about Quraysh's march to protect their caravan. The Prophet ﷺ consulted the people and informed them about Quraysh. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and spoke well. Then 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and spoke well. Then al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, proceed with what Allah has commanded you, for we are with you. By Allah, we will not say to you what the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are sitting right here﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 24]. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we will fight alongside you both. By Him who sent you with the truth, if you were to lead us to Bark al-Ghimad (meaning the city of Abyssinia), we would strive alongside you against whoever stands in the way until you reach it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said good things to him and invoked goodness upon him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Advise me, O people," meaning the Ansar, because they were the majority of the people. This was because when they pledged allegiance to him at al-'Aqabah, they had said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are free of any obligation to you until you reach our homes. When you arrive among us, you will be under our protection, and we will defend you as we defend our sons and our women." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ feared that the Ansar might not consider their support binding upon them except against an enemy who attacked him in Madinah, and that they were not obliged to march with him against an enemy outside their lands. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said this, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to him: "By Allah, it seems you mean us, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Indeed." Sa'd said: "We have believed in you, affirmed you, and testified that what you have brought is the truth, and we have given you our covenants and pledges to hear and obey. So proceed, O Messenger of Allah, with what you intend. By Him who sent you with the truth, if you were to lead us across this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge in with you; not a single man of us would stay behind. We do not dislike that you meet our enemy with us tomorrow. Indeed, we are steadfast in war and truthful in encounter, and perhaps Allah will show you from us what will delight your eyes. So march with us in the blessing of Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased with Sa'd's words and was energized by them. Then he said: "Proceed in the blessing of Allah and rejoice, for Allah has promised me one of the two groups. By Allah, it is as if I am now looking at the places where the people will fall."

[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/399).]

Al-'Awfi related similar to this from Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise said al-Suddi, Qatadah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and many scholars of the earlier and later generations. We have abridged their statements, being content with the context of Muhammad ibn Ishaq.

The commentary of Imam Abu Ja'far al-Tabari (Ibn Jarir): The exegetes differed about the reason that brings in this *kaf* (the particle "like," as, in Arabic *kaf al-tashbih*) in His words: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth﴾. Some of them said: it is compared to it in regard to the good state of the believers: their fear of their Lord, their reconciling among themselves, and their obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

Then he narrated similar to this from 'Ikrimah.

The meaning of this is that Allah, exalted is He, says: Just as you disputed over the spoils and contended about them, and Allah took them away from you and placed them under the distribution of Himself and His Messenger ﷺ [[In manuscripts K, M, A: "may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]], and he divided them with justice and equality, and this was the complete benefit for you; likewise, when you disliked going out to face the enemy, to fight the one with the might (the armed force), who are the *nafir* (the armed reinforcement) that went out to defend their religion and to protect their caravan, then the outcome of your dislike of fighting was that He decreed it for you and gathered you with your enemy without prior appointment, and it became right guidance, victory and triumph, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 216].

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: the meaning of that is: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth﴾ despite the dislike of a group of the believers, so likewise they dislike fighting, and they dispute with you about it after it has become clear to them. He narrated something similar from Mujahid, that he said regarding ﴿As your Lord brought you out﴾: Likewise they dispute with you about the truth.

Al-Suddi said: Allah revealed concerning their going out to Badr and their disputing with him: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth, though a party of the believers were averse﴾ to the pursuit of the polytheists, ﴿they dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾.

Some of them said: They ask you about the spoils (*al-anfal*) in dispute, just as they disputed with you on the day of Badr, saying: "You brought us out for the caravan, and you did not inform us of a battle so that we might prepare for it."

I say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only went out from Madinah seeking the caravan of Abu Sufyan, whose news had reached him that it was coming from al-Sham, carrying great wealth for Quraysh. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called upon the Muslims, those who were light (ready to go), and he went out with three hundred and some ten men, and he sought the coastal direction by the way of Badr. Abu Sufyan learned of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ departure in pursuit of him, so he sent Damdam ibn 'Amr as a warner to Makkah. They rose up, nearly a thousand armed men, between nine hundred and a thousand. Abu Sufyan veered with the caravan toward the seaside and escaped. The *nafir* came and reached the water of Badr. Allah gathered the Muslims and the disbelievers without prior appointment, because of what Allah, exalted is He, intended: the elevation of the word of the Muslims, their victory over their enemy, and the distinguishing between truth and falsehood, as its explanation will come.

The purpose: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received word of the *nafir*'s going out, Allah revealed to him, promising him one of the two groups: either the caravan or the *nafir*. Many of the Muslims preferred the caravan, because it was gain without fighting, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you wished that the one without thorns (the unarmed group) would be yours, but Allah intended to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the roots of the disbelievers﴾.

The hadith master Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his *Tafsir*: Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Tabarani narrated to us, Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Aslam Abi 'Imran, that he heard Abu Ayyub al-Ansari say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said while we were in Madinah: "I have been informed about the caravan of Abu Sufyan, that it is approaching. Would you like us to go out before this caravan, perhaps Allah will grant it to us as spoils?" We said: "Yes." So he went out and we went out. When we had traveled a day or two, he said to us: "What do you think about fighting the people, for they have been informed of your departure?" We said: "No, by Allah, we have no strength for fighting the enemy, but we intended the caravan." Then he said: "What do you think about fighting the people?" We said the same as before. Then al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr said: "Then we will not say to you, O Messenger of Allah, as the people of Musa said to Musa: ﴿So go you and your Lord and fight; we are sitting right here﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 24]." He said: Then we, the Ansar, wished that we had said as al-Miqdad said, which would have been more beloved to us than great wealth. He said: So Allah revealed to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth, though a party of the believers were averse﴾, and he mentioned the rest of the hadith [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/174).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah, similarly.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Badr, until when he was at al-Rawha', he addressed the people and said: "How do you see it?" Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have been informed that they are at such-and-such place." Then he addressed the people again and said: "How do you see it?" 'Umar said the same as Abu Bakr's statement. Then he addressed the people again and said: "How do you see it?" Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it us you mean? By Him who honored you with the truth and revealed the Book to you, I have never traversed this route, nor do I have knowledge of it. If you were to travel with us until you reach Bark al-Ghimad in Dhi Yaman, we would march with you. And we would not be like those who said to Musa: ﴿So go you and your Lord and fight, we are sitting right here﴾. Rather, [we say]: Go you and your Lord and fight, we are with you both, following. Perhaps you went out for a matter, and Allah has revealed to you something else, so look at what Allah has revealed to you and proceed with it. Join the ties of whomever you wish, sever the ties of whomever you wish, be hostile to whomever you wish, make peace with whomever you wish, and take from our wealth what you wish." So the Qur'an descended in agreement with Sa'd's statement: ﴿As your Lord brought you out from your house with the truth, though a party of the believers were averse﴾, and the verses that follow.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: When the Prophet ﷺ consulted (the people) about meeting the enemy, and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said what he said, that being on the day of Badr, he ordered the people to get ready for battle and ordered them with the weapon (*al-shawkah*, the armed force). Al-Suddi said: ﴿They dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾, meaning: after it had become clear to them that you do nothing except what Allah has commanded you.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verses 9–10 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nuh Qurad narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Simak al-Hanafi Abu Zumayl narrated to us, Ibn 'Abbas [[In K: "Ibn 'Ayyash".]] narrated to me, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me, saying: When the Day of Badr came, the Prophet ﷺ looked at his Companions, who were three hundred and some, and he looked at the polytheists and found them to be a thousand and more. So the Prophet ﷺ faced the qiblah, then he raised his hands, while his cloak and waistwrapper were on him, and then he said: "O Allah, where is what You promised me? O Allah, fulfil for me what You promised me. O Allah, if this band of the people of Islam is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on the earth ever." He said: He kept calling upon his Lord [Mighty and Majestic] [[Addition from A.]] and supplicating to Him until his cloak fell off. Then Abu Bakr came to him, took his cloak and put it back on him, then embraced him from behind and said: "O Messenger of Allah, your pleading with your Lord is enough, for He will surely fulfil for you what He promised you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ Then when that day came and they met, Allah defeated the polytheists. Seventy men of them were killed and seventy men of them were taken captive. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted Abu Bakr, 'Ali and 'Umar [[In M: "Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Ali".]]. Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are the sons of our uncles, our kinsmen and our brothers, and I think you should take ransom from them, so that what we take from them will be a strength for us against the disbelievers, and perhaps Allah will guide them and they will become a support for us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What do you think, O son of al-Khattab?" He said: I said: "By Allah, I do not see what Abu Bakr sees, but I think you should let me have so-and-so, a relative of 'Umar, and I will strike his neck; and let 'Ali have 'Aqil, and he will strike his neck; and let Hamzah have so-and-so, his brother, and he will strike his neck, so that Allah will know that there is no softness in our hearts towards the polytheists. These are their chieftains, their leaders and their commanders." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ inclined to what Abu Bakr said, and did not incline to what I said, and he took the ransom from them. When the next day came, 'Umar said: I went to the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr, and they were both weeping. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me what makes you and your companion weep. If I find a reason to weep I will weep, and if I do not find a reason I will feign weeping because of your weeping." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Because of what your Companions proposed to me regarding taking the ransom, your punishment has been presented to me, as close as this tree" — a nearby tree. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed [[Addition from D, K, M, A.]]: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has fought intensively in the land﴾
up to His saying: ﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already preceded, a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾ [Al-Anfal: 67–68] of the ransom. Then He made the spoils lawful for them. When the Day of Uhud came, in the year after, they were punished for what they had done on the Day of Badr, by taking the ransom: seventy of them were killed, the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ fled from the Prophet ﷺ, his front tooth was broken, the helmet was smashed on his head, and blood flowed on his face. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed [[Addition from A.]]: ﴿Why, when a calamity struck you, although you had struck (the enemy) with twice as much, did you say: "How is this?" Say: "It is from yourselves." Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 165], because of your taking the ransom.

Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it, through several chains, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, with this same wording. 'Ali ibn al-Madini and al-Tirmidhi graded it sound, and they both said: It is not known except through the narration of 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar al-Yamani. [[Al-Musnad (1/30), Sahih Muslim no. (1763), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2690), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3081), and Tafsir al-Tabari (13/409).]]

In the same way, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that this noble verse, His saying: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord [so He answered you]﴾ [[Addition from A.]], refers to the supplication of the Prophet ﷺ. Likewise Yazid [[In D, M: "Zayd".]] ibn Yuthay', al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj said.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, who said: When the Day of Badr came, the Prophet ﷺ began to plead with his Lord most earnestly, supplicating. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, [you are asking] some of your pleading. By Allah, Allah will surely fulfil for you what He promised you." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/411).]]

Al-Bukhari said in "The Book of Military Campaigns (Kitab al-Maghazi)", chapter on the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: I heard Ibn Mas'ud say: "I witnessed a scene with al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, that for me to have been his companion in it would be more beloved to me than anything else that could be exchanged for it. He came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was supplicating against the polytheists, and said: 'We will not say to you, as the people of Musa said to Musa: ﴿Go, you and your Lord, and fight﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 24]; rather, we will fight on your right and on your left, before you and behind you.'" I saw the face of the Prophet ﷺ brighten and he was pleased by it — meaning his saying [[In A: "Lo naqul laka".]].

For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty﴾, that is, the might belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger and to the believers through them, in this world and the Hereafter, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand, the Day when no excuse will benefit the wrongdoers.﴾ [Ghafir: 51-52] [[Addition from a.]] ﴿Wise﴾ in what He legislated of fighting the disbelievers, while being able to destroy and annihilate them by His power and might, glorified is He and exalted.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verse 11–14 (part 1 of 2):

Allah reminds them of the favour He bestowed upon them by sending down drowsiness (al-nu'as) upon them, as security from the fear that had come upon them due to the great number of their enemy and the smallness of their own number. Allah, exalted is He, did likewise with them on the day of Uhud, as He said: ﴿Then after distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness overcoming a faction of you, while another faction was concerned only for themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 154].

Abu Talhah said: "I was among those who were overcome by drowsiness on the day of Uhud. The sword kept falling from my hand again and again; I would pick it up, and it would fall and I would pick it up. And I looked at them, swaying while they were beneath the shields (al-hujaf)."

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Zuhayr narrated to us, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from Haritha ibn Mudarrib, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "There was no horseman among us on the day of Badr except al-Miqdad. And indeed I saw us, and there was not one of us sleeping except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was praying beneath a tree and weeping until morning."

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Drowsiness in battle is security from Allah, and drowsiness in prayer is from Shaytan."

Qatadah said: "Drowsiness is in the head, and sleep is in the heart."

I say: As for drowsiness, it did befall them on the day of Uhud, and the matter of that is very well known. As for the day of Badr, in this noble verse, it is in the context of the story of Badr, and it indicates that this also occurred. It seems that this was a natural disposition of the believers at the height of severe danger, so that their hearts would be secure and tranquil in the victory of Allah. This is from Allah's grace and mercy towards them and His blessings upon them. As Allah said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾ [Al-Sharh: 5-6]. For this reason it is recorded in the Sahih that when it was the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the 'arish with al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, and they were both supplicating. Drowsiness overtook the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he awoke smiling and said: "Rejoice, O Abu Bakr, this is Jibril, upon his front teeth is the dust." Then he went out from the door of the 'arish, reciting His saying: ﴿The multitude will be put to flight and they will turn their backs﴾ [Al-Qamar: 45].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Prophet ﷺ descended – meaning when he marched to Badr – and the Muslims had between them and the water a sandy dune (ramlah di'sah), and the Muslims suffered severe weakness. Shaytan cast anger into their hearts, whispering among them: "You claim that you are the friends of Allah, and His Messenger is among you, yet the polytheists have overcome you at the water, and you pray in a state of major impurity!" So Allah sent down heavy rain upon them, and the Muslims drank and purified themselves, and Allah removed from them the filth of Shaytan, and the sand became firm when the rain struck it, and people and animals walked upon it, and they advanced to the enemy. Allah strengthened His Prophet ﷺ and the believers with a thousand angels, and Jibril was with five hundred in one flank, and Mika'il with five hundred in one flank.

Similarly al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: When the polytheists of Quraysh came out to defend the caravan and to fight on its behalf, they descended at the water on the day of Badr and overcame the believers at it. He said: "Rather, it is a place I have descended for war and strategy." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is not a suitable place. Rather, march with us until we descend at the nearest water to the enemy, and we block up the wells beyond it, and we draw water into the cisterns, so that we will have water and they will have no water." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marched and did so.

In the Maghazi of al-Umawi, it is recorded that when al-Hubab said that, an angel descended from the sky while Jibril was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that angel said: "O Muhammad, your Lord sends you greetings of peace and says to you: Indeed, the opinion is what al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir has pointed to." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to Jibril, peace be upon him, and said: "Do you know this one?" He looked at him and said: "I do not know all the angels, but he is an angel and not a devil."

The best of what is related in this regard is what Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, author of the Maghazi, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated: Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr who said: Allah sent the sky – and the valley was soft sand – so it fell upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions in a way that packed down the ground for them and did not prevent them from marching, and it befell Quraysh in a way that they could not manage to set out with it.

Mujahid said: Allah sent down the rain upon them before the drowsiness, so the rain extinguished the dust, the ground became packed with it, their souls were content, and their feet were made firm by it.

Ibn Jarir said: Harun ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from Jariyah, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "There fell upon us during the night a light rain – meaning the night whose morning was the battle of Badr – so we went under the trees and the shields to shelter beneath them from the rain. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spent the night supplicating to his Lord: 'O Allah, if You destroy this band, You will not be worshipped on the earth!' When dawn broke, he called out: 'Prayer, servants of Allah!' The people came from under the trees and the shields, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer and urged us to fight."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿to purify you thereby﴾, that is, from minor or major impurity (hadath), and this is the purification of the outward body; ﴿and remove from you the filth of Shaytan﴾, that is, from whispering or an evil thought, and this is the purification of the inward self. As Allah said regarding the people of Paradise: ﴿Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾, and this is the adornment of the outward; ﴿and their Lord will give them a pure drink﴾ [Al-Insan: 21], that is, one purifying them from whatever rancour, envy, or hatred there was, and this is the adornment and purity of the inward.

﴿And that He may strengthen your hearts﴾, that is, through patience and advancing to contend against the enemies, and this is the courage of the inward; ﴿and plant firmly thereby the feet﴾, and this is the courage of the outward. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed"﴾. This is a hidden blessing which Allah, exalted is He, made manifest to them so that they would thank Him for it. It is that He, exalted, sanctified, blessed and glorified is He, revealed to the angels whom He sent down to support His Prophet, His religion and His party of believers, revealing to them, in what was between Him and them, that they should strengthen those who believed.

Ibn Ishaq said: "Support them." Others said: "Fight alongside them." It was said: "They increased their numbers." It was also said: that this happened in that an angel would come to a man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ and say: "I heard these people – meaning the polytheists – saying: 'By Allah, if they charge against us, we will surely be routed,'" so the Muslims would relate that to one another, and their souls would be strengthened thereby. Ibn Jarir related this, and this is his wording exactly.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾, that is: you, the Muslims, be steadfast and strengthen yourselves against your enemies, in obedience to My command to you in that; I will cast terror and humiliation and abasement upon those who opposed My command and denied My messenger. ﴿So strike above the necks and strike from them every fingertip﴾, that is: strike the skulls and split them, cut off the necks and sever them, and cut off the extremities of them, which are their hands and feet.

The commentators differed regarding the meaning of ﴿above the necks﴾. It was said: its meaning is "strike the heads." This was said by 'Ikrimah.

It was also said: its meaning ﴿above the necks﴾ is "upon the necks," meaning the necks themselves. This was said by al-Dahhak and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi.

This meaning is supported by the fact that Allah guided the believers to this in His saying: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, then striking of the necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then tighten the bonds﴾ [Muhammad: 4].

Wakī' said, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Qasim, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was not sent to punish with the punishment of Allah; I was only sent with striking the necks and tightening the bonds."

Ibn Jarir preferred that it may indicate both striking the necks and splitting the skulls.

I say: In the Maghazi of al-Umawi, it is recorded that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pass among the slain on the day of Badr and say: "We split skulls..." Then Abu Bakr would say: "From men dear to us... and they were more disobedient and more unjust," and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would begin with the first half of the verse and ask Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, to recite its last half, because he did not recite poetry well, as Allah said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69].

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: On the day of Badr, the people knew the slain of the angels from those they had killed, by a blow above the necks and on the fingertips, like a mark of fire that had been burned upon them.

As for His saying: ﴿and strike from them every fingertip﴾. Ibn Jarir said: its meaning is: strike them, O believers, of your enemy, every joint and articulation of the extremities of their hands and feet. Al-Suddi said: "al-banan" means the extremities (al-atraf), and it is also said that it means every joint (kull mafsil).

Ikrimah, Atiyyah al-Awfi and al-Dahhak (in another narration) said: "kull mifsal," meaning every joint.

Al-Awza'i, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿And strike every finger-tip of them﴾, said: "Strike him on the face and the eye, and hurl at him a flaming firebrand. When you have seized him, all of that becomes forbidden to you."

I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [them] upon the necks and strike from them every finger-tip﴾. Blessed and exalted is He; there is no deity except Him, and no lord besides Him.

﴿That, so taste it; and [know that] for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire﴾. This is an address to the disbelievers, meaning: taste this punishment and retribution in this world, and know also that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verse 11–14 (part 1 of 2):

Allah reminds them of the favour He bestowed upon them by sending down drowsiness (al-nu'as) upon them, as security from the fear that had come upon them due to the great number of their enemy and the smallness of their own number. Allah, exalted is He, did likewise with them on the day of Uhud, as He said: ﴿Then after distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness overcoming a faction of you, while another faction was concerned only for themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 154].

Abu Talhah said: "I was among those who were overcome by drowsiness on the day of Uhud. The sword kept falling from my hand again and again; I would pick it up, and it would fall and I would pick it up. And I looked at them, swaying while they were beneath the shields (al-hujaf)."

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Zuhayr narrated to us, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from Haritha ibn Mudarrib, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "There was no horseman among us on the day of Badr except al-Miqdad. And indeed I saw us, and there was not one of us sleeping except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was praying beneath a tree and weeping until morning."

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Drowsiness in battle is security from Allah, and drowsiness in prayer is from Shaytan."

Qatadah said: "Drowsiness is in the head, and sleep is in the heart."

I say: As for drowsiness, it did befall them on the day of Uhud, and the matter of that is very well known. As for the day of Badr, in this noble verse, it is in the context of the story of Badr, and it indicates that this also occurred. It seems that this was a natural disposition of the believers at the height of severe danger, so that their hearts would be secure and tranquil in the victory of Allah. This is from Allah's grace and mercy towards them and His blessings upon them. As Allah said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾ [Al-Sharh: 5-6]. For this reason it is recorded in the Sahih that when it was the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the 'arish with al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, and they were both supplicating. Drowsiness overtook the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he awoke smiling and said: "Rejoice, O Abu Bakr, this is Jibril, upon his front teeth is the dust." Then he went out from the door of the 'arish, reciting His saying: ﴿The multitude will be put to flight and they will turn their backs﴾ [Al-Qamar: 45].

* *

Shaytan cast anger into their hearts, whispering among them: "You claim that you are the friends of Allah, and His Messenger is among you, yet the polytheists have overcome you at the water, and you pray in a state of major impurity!" So Allah sent down heavy rain upon them, and the Muslims drank and purified themselves, and Allah removed from them the filth of Shaytan, and the sand became firm when the rain struck it, and people and animals walked upon it, and they advanced to the enemy. Allah strengthened His Prophet ﷺ and the believers with a thousand angels, and Jibril was with five hundred in one flank, and Mika'il with five hundred in one flank.
