Allah the Exalted says, threatening with the Fire those who flee from the battlefield when they do so: "O you who have believed, when you meet those who have disbelieved advancing [in ranks] (zahfan), do not turn your backs to them [in flight]." That is, when you draw close to them and approach them, "do not turn your backs to them," meaning do not flee and abandon your companions.

"And whoever turns his back to them on that day, except in maneuvering for battle (mutaharrifan li-qital)" means: one who retreats before his opponent as a stratagem, so that he shows him that he fears him and he follows him, and then he turns back upon him and kills him; there is no blame on him for that. This is what Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi stated explicitly.

Al-Dahhak said: it means that he advances ahead of his companions in order to see an opening in the enemy and strike it.

"Or joining a company (mutahayyizan ila fi'ah)" means: he withdraws from here to another company of the Muslims, to be helped by them and to help them. This is permissible for him, and even if he was in a detachment (sariyyah) and withdrew to its commander or to the supreme Imam, he falls within this concession.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "I was in one of the detachments of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the people fled in confusion (haysah) — and I was among those who fled. We said: 'How shall we act, since we have fled from the battle and incurred anger?' Then we said: 'If we entered Madinah and stayed the night?' Then we said: 'If we presented ourselves to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); if there is repentance for us, well; otherwise we will go away.' So we came to him before the dawn prayer, and he came out and said: 'Who are the people?' We said: 'We are the fleers (farrarun).' He said: 'No, rather you are the returners ('akkarun). I am your fi'ah, and I am the fi'ah of the Muslims.' He said: So we came to him until we kissed his hand."

Likewise it was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, through several chains from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad. al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan; we do not know it except from his narration."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad with this chain, and he added at its end: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: 'or joining a company.'"

The people of knowledge said: the meaning of his saying "al-'akkarun" is "those who turn back (al-'attafun)." Likewise Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said about Abu Ubayd when he was killed on the bridge in the land of Persia, due to the great number of the army from the side of the Magians: "Had he withdrawn to me, I would have been a fi'ah for him." Thus Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated it from Umar.

In the narration of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi from Umar: when Abu Ubayd was killed, Umar said: "O people, I am your fi'ah."

Mujahid said: Umar said: "I am the fi'ah of every Muslim."

Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr said, from Umar: "O people, let not this verse deceive you, for it was only (revealed) on the day of Badr, and I am a fi'ah for every Muslim."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Hassan ibn Abdullah al-Misri narrated to us, Khallad ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami narrated to us, Nafi' narrated to us: that he asked Ibn Umar, "We are a people who do not stand firm when fighting our enemy, and we do not know who the fi'ah is: our Imam or our army?" He said: "The fi'ah is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." I said: "Allah says: 'When you meet those who have disbelieved advancing, do not turn your backs to them.'" He said: "This verse was only revealed concerning the day of Badr, neither before it nor after it."

Al-Dahhak, regarding his saying "or joining a company," said: the mutahayyiz is one who flees to the Prophet and his companions, and likewise whoever flees today to his commander or his companions.

As for fleeing without any of these reasons, it is forbidden and is one of the major sins (kaba'ir), due to what al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated in their Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins (al-muwbiqat)." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming riba, consuming the property of an orphan, turning back on the day of the battle-line (al-tawalli yawm al-zahf), and slandering chaste, unwary, believing women."

There are corroborating narrations for this hadith from other routes. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: "then he has returned (baa) with anger from Allah, and his refuge is Hell — and what an evil destination." That is, his place of return and his final abode on the day of the promised meeting: "Hell, and wretched is the destination."

Imam Ahmad said: Zakariyya ibn Adi narrated to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Amr al-Raqqi narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, Jabalah ibn Suhaym narrated to us, from Abu al-Muthanna al-Abdi, I heard al-Sadusi — that is, Ibn al-Khasasiyah, whose name is Bashir ibn Ma'bad — say: "I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) to pledge allegiance to him, and he stipulated to me: 'The testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, that you establish the prayer, pay the zakat, perform the Hajj of Islam, fast Ramadan, and strive in the way of Allah.'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, as for two of them, by Allah I cannot bear them: the jihad, for they claim that whoever turns his back has returned with anger from Allah, and I fear that if I attend that, my soul will be humbled and I will dislike death; and the charity, for by Allah I have nothing but a small flock and ten she-camels which are the carriers of my family and their loads." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) closed his hand, then moved his hand, then said: "Then there is no jihad and no charity; by what then will you enter Paradise?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I pledge allegiance to you." So I pledged allegiance to him upon all of them.

This is a hadith that is gharib from this route, and they did not include it in the six books (al-kutub al-sittah).

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Yazid ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, Abu al-Ash'ath narrated to us, from Thawban, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Three things with which no deed benefits: associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, and fleeing from the battle-line." [al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/104): "In it is Yazid ibn Rabi'ah, who is weak."]

This is also a very gharib hadith.

Al-Tabarani also said: al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Asfati narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hafs ibn Umar al-Shanni narrated to us, Amr ibn Murrah narrated to me, who said: I heard Bilal ibn Yasar ibn Zayd, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), say: I heard my father narrate from my grandfather, who said: the Messenger of Allah said: "Whoever says, 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but He, and I repent to Him,' he will be forgiven, even if he has fled from the battle-line."

Likewise Abu Dawud narrated it from Musa ibn Isma'il with this chain. al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, from al-Bukhari, from Musa ibn Isma'il with this chain, and said: "Gharib; we do not know it except from this route."

I say: nothing is known of Zayd, the freedman of the Prophet (ﷺ), from anyone other than this narration.

Some have held that fleeing was forbidden only for the Companions, because jihad at that time was an individual obligation (fard 'ayn) upon them. It was also said that it was specific to the Ansar, because they pledged allegiance upon listening and obedience in ease and in hardship. It was also said that the intended meaning of this verse is specifically the people of Badr; this is narrated from Umar, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, Abu Nadrah, Nafi' the freedman of Ibn Umar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others.

Their argument for this is that there was no group with strength to which they could turn back other than that group of theirs, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, if You destroy this band, You will not be worshipped on the earth." Therefore Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying "And whoever turns his back to them on that day": "That is the day of Badr. As for today: if he withdraws to a company or to a city — I think he said — then there is no blame upon him."

Ibn al-Mubarak also said, from Ibn Lahi'ah: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, who said: Allah the Exalted made the Fire obligatory for whoever fled on the day of Badr. He said: "And whoever turns his back to them on that day, except in maneuvering for battle or joining a company, has returned with anger from Allah." Then when the day of Uhud came after that, He said: "Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned [...]" and "And Allah has already pardoned them" [Al 'Imran: 155]. Then the day of Hunayn came seven years after that, and He said: "then you turned back, retreating" [al-Tawbah: 25], "then Allah will turn in forgiveness after that to whom He wills" [al-Tawbah: 27].

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, the Mustadrak of al-Hakim, the Tafsir of Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, that he said concerning this verse, "And whoever turns his back to them on that day," it was only revealed concerning the people of Badr. All of this does not negate that fleeing from the battle-line is forbidden for others than the people of Badr, even if the occasion of revelation concerned them, as the hadith of Abu Hurayrah mentioned earlier indicates, that fleeing from the battle-line is among the destructive sins, as is the position of the majority. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

Allah the Exalted says, threatening with the Fire those who flee from the battlefield when they do so: "O you who have believed, when you meet those who have disbelieved advancing [in ranks] (zahfan), do not turn your backs to them [in flight]." That is, when you draw close to them and approach them, "do not turn your backs to them," meaning do not flee and abandon your companions.

"And whoever turns his back to them on that day, except in maneuvering for battle (mutaharrifan li-qital)" means: one who retreats before his opponent as a stratagem, so that he shows him that he fears him and he follows him, and then he turns back upon him and kills him; there is no blame on him for that. This is what Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi stated explicitly.

Al-Dahhak said: it means that he advances ahead of his companions in order to see an opening in the enemy and strike it.

"Or joining a company (mutahayyizan ila fi'ah)" means: he withdraws from here to another company of the Muslims, to be helped by them and to help them. This is permissible for him, and even if he was in a detachment (sariyyah) and withdrew to its commander or to the supreme Imam, he falls within this concession.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "I was in one of the detachments of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the people fled in confusion (haysah) — and I was among those who fled. We said: 'How shall we act, since we have fled from the battle and incurred anger?' Then we said: 'If we entered Madinah and stayed the night?' Then we said: 'If we presented ourselves to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); if there is repentance for us, well; otherwise we will go away.' So we came to him before the dawn prayer, and he came out and said: 'Who are the people?' We said: 'We are the fleers (farrarun).' He said: 'No, rather you are the returners ('akkarun). I am your fi'ah, and I am the fi'ah of the Muslims.' He said: So we came to him until we kissed his hand."

Likewise it was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, through several chains from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad. al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan; we do not know it except from his narration."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad with this chain, and he added at its end: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: 'or joining a company.'"

The people of knowledge said: the meaning of his saying "al-'akkarun" is "those who turn back (al-'attafun)." Likewise Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said about Abu Ubayd when he was killed on the bridge in the land of Persia, due to the great number of the army from the side of the Magians: "Had he withdrawn to me, I would have been a fi'ah for him." Thus Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated it from Umar.

In the narration of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi from Umar: when Abu Ubayd was killed, Umar said: "O people, I am your fi'ah."

Mujahid said: Umar said: "I am the fi'ah of every Muslim."

Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr said, from Umar: "O people, let not this verse deceive you, for it was only (revealed) on the day of Badr, and I am a fi'ah for every Muslim."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Hassan ibn Abdullah al-Misri narrated to us, Khallad ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami narrated to us, Nafi' narrated to us: that he asked Ibn Umar, "We are a people who do not stand firm when fighting our enemy, and we do not know who the fi'ah is: our Imam or our army?" He said: "The fi'ah is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." I said: "Allah says: 'When you meet those who have disbelieved advancing, do not turn your backs to them.'" He said: "This verse was only revealed concerning the day of Badr, neither before it nor after it."

Al-Dahhak, regarding his saying "or joining a company," said: the mutahayyiz is one who flees to the Prophet and his companions, and likewise whoever flees today to his commander or his companions.

As for fleeing without any of these reasons, it is forbidden and is one of the major sins (kaba'ir), due to what al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated in their Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins (al-muwbiqat)." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming riba, consuming the property of an orphan, turning back on the day of the battle-line (al-tawalli yawm al-zahf), and slandering chaste, unwary, believing women."

There are corroborating narrations for this hadith from other routes. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: "then he has returned (baa) with anger from Allah, and his refuge is Hell — and what an evil destination." That is, his place of return and his final abode on the day of the promised meeting: "Hell, and wretched is the destination."

Therefore He said: ﴿So you did not kill them, but it was Allah who killed them﴾, meaning: it was not by your power and strength that you killed your enemies, despite their great numbers and your small number. And Allah is with the patient﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 249].

Then He said to His Prophet (ﷺ) also concerning the handful of dust, which he threw at the faces of the polytheists [in A: "the people"] on the day of Badr, when he came out of the shelter after his supplication, his humble pleading and his submission. He threw it at them and said: "May the faces be disfigured." Then he commanded the Companions to charge immediately after it, and they did. So Allah carried those pebbles to the eyes of the polytheists, and none of them remained without being struck by something from them that preoccupied him from his situation. Therefore He said [Ta'ala] [addition from A]: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾, meaning: it was He who delivered that to them and overwhelmed them with it, not you.

Jibril said to him: "Take a handful of dust and throw it into their faces." So he took a handful of dust and threw it into their faces, and no polytheist was left without dust from that handful reaching his eyes, his nostrils and his mouth, and they turned back in retreat.

As-Suddi said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, on the day of Badr: "Give me pebbles from the earth."

He handed him pebbles with dust on them, and he threw them into the faces of the people, and no polytheist remained without some of that dust entering his eyes. Then the believers [in M: "the Muslims"] pursued them, killing and capturing them, and Allah revealed: ﴿So you did not kill them, but it was Allah who killed them, and you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾.

Abu Ma'shar al-Madani narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: When the two sides drew near to one another, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a handful of dust, threw it into the faces of the people, and said: "May the faces be disfigured." It entered all their eyes, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah [(ﷺ)] [addition from M, K, A] came forward killing them and capturing them, and their defeat was at the throw of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah revealed: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said concerning His saying [Ta'ala] [addition from M]: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾: This is the day of Badr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took three pebbles, threw one pebble [into] [in K, M, A: "threw into"] the right wing of the people, one pebble into the left wing of the people, and one pebble among them, and said: "May the faces be disfigured," and they were routed.

This story has been narrated from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah and other leading scholars: that the verse was revealed concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) throw on the day of Badr, although he also did that on the day of Hunayn.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Imran narrated to us, Musa ibn Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Zam'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah, from Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: When it was the day of Badr, we heard a sound fall from the sky, as if it were the sound of a pebble falling into a basin, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) threw that throw, and we were routed.

[This is] strange from this route. There are two other very strange opinions here.

The first: Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Ta'i narrated to me, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Safwan ibn 'Amr narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to us: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on the day of Ibn Abi al-Huqayq at Khaybar, asked for a bow, and a long bow was brought to him, and he said: "Bring me other than it." They brought a short bow, and the Prophet (ﷺ) shot at the fortress, and the arrow came down and killed Ibn Abi al-Huqayq while he was on his bed, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾ [The following narration and the one after it were omitted from Tabari's text, and the editor placed them in the margin (13/446).]

This is strange, and its chain up to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr is sound; perhaps he was mistaken about it, or he intended that the verse encompasses all of this, since the context of the verse in Surat al-Anfal is undoubtedly about the story of Badr. This is something not hidden from the imams of knowledge. And Allah knows best.

The second: Ibn Jarir also narrated, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, with a sound chain, to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhri that they both said: It was revealed concerning the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) throw on the day of Uhud at Ubayy ibn Khalaf with the spear, while he was in his armor; it grazed his collarbone, and he began to fall from his horse repeatedly, until his death came a few days later, in which he suffered a painful torment, connected to the torment of the barzakh, which is linked to the torment of the Hereafter [Mustadrak (2/327)].

This report from these two imams is also very strange, and perhaps they intended that the verse encompasses it by its generality, not that it was revealed specifically concerning it, as has preceded. And Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, concerning His saying: ﴿and that He might test the believers with a good trial from Him﴾, meaning: that He might make the believers recognize His blessing upon them in granting them victory over their enemy despite the enemy's great numbers and their own small number, so that by this they would recognize His right and thank Him for His blessing.

Ibn Jarir also explained it in this way. And in the hadith: "Every trial from Him that He gives us is good."

* *

The first: Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Ta'i narrated to me, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Safwan ibn 'Amr narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to us: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on the day of Ibn Abi al-Huqayq at Khaybar, asked for a bow, and a long bow was brought to him, and he said: "Bring me other than it." They brought a short bow, and the Prophet (ﷺ) shot at the fortress, and the arrow came down and killed Ibn Abi al-Huqayq while he was on his bed, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾ [The following narration and the one after it were omitted from Tabari's text, and the editor placed them in the margin (13/446).]

This is strange, and its chain up to 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr is sound; perhaps he was mistaken about it, or he intended that the verse encompasses all of this, since the context of the verse in Surat al-Anfal is undoubtedly about the story of Badr. This is something not hidden from the imams of knowledge. And Allah knows best.

The second: Ibn Jarir also narrated, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, with a sound chain, to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhri that they both said: It was revealed concerning the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) throw on the day of Uhud at Ubayy ibn Khalaf with the spear, while he was in his armor; it grazed his collarbone, and he began to fall from his horse repeatedly, until his death came a few days later, in which he suffered a painful torment, connected to the torment of the barzakh, which is linked to the torment of the Hereafter [Mustadrak (2/327)].

This report from these two imams is also very strange, and perhaps they intended that the verse encompasses it by its generality, not that it was revealed specifically concerning it, as has preceded. And Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, concerning His saying: ﴿and that He might test the believers with a good trial from Him﴾, meaning: that He might make the believers recognize His blessing upon them in granting them victory over their enemy despite the enemy's great numbers and their own small number, so that by this they would recognize His right and thank Him for His blessing.

Ibn Jarir also explained it in this way. And in the hadith: "Every trial from Him that He gives us is good."

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾, meaning: Hearing of supplication, Knowing of who deserves victory and triumph.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is so, and [that] Allah weakens the plot of the disbelievers﴾. This is another glad tiding alongside the victory that occurred: He informed them, exalted is He, that He will weaken the plots of the disbelievers in what is to come, belittling their affair, and that everything they have is in ruin and destruction. And to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Allah says to the disbelievers: ﴿If you seek a decision﴾, meaning: if you seek victory from Allah, ask Him for judgment, and insist that He decide between you and your enemies, the believers, then the decision has indeed come to you, as you asked. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others narrated, from al-Zuhri, from Abdullah ibn Tha'labah ibn Su'ayr, that Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: "O Allah, whichever of us is more severed from kinship and brings what we do not know, destroy him tomorrow morning." That was his istiftah (a seeking of opening or decision). Then it was revealed: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has come to you﴾ up to the end of the verse.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid (meaning Ibn Harun) narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, al-Zuhri narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Tha'labah, that Abu Jahl said when the two parties met: "O Allah, whichever of us is more severed from kinship and brings what we do not know, destroy him tomorrow morning." So he was the one seeking the opening.

al-Nasa'i included it in his Tafsir from the hadith of Salih ibn Kaysan, from al-Zuhri, with the same chain. al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak through the route of al-Zuhri, with the same chain, and said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." Similar to this has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Yazid ibn Ruman, and others.

al-Suddi said: When the polytheists set out from Makkah toward Badr, they clung to the curtains of the Ka'bah and sought victory from Allah, saying: "O Allah, give victory to the higher of the two armies, the nobler of the two groups, and the better of the two tribes." So Allah said: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has come to you﴾, meaning: We have given victory to what you said, and that is Muhammad ﷺ.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is His saying, reporting about them: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment"﴾ [al-Anfal: 32].

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you desist﴾, meaning: from what you are in of disbelief in Allah and denial of His Messenger, ﴿it is better for you﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter. His saying: ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾ [al-Isra: 8]. Its meaning: if you return to what you were in of disbelief and misguidance, We will return to you with the like of this event.

al-Suddi said: ﴿And if you return﴾, meaning: to seeking victory, ﴿We will return﴾ to granting victory to Muhammad ﷺ, supporting him, and making him triumph over his enemies. The first (interpretation) is stronger.

﴿And your company will not avail you anything, even if it is large﴾, meaning: even if you gathered whatever multitudes you might gather. Indeed, whoever Allah is with, none can overcome him, for Allah is with the believers, and they are the Prophetic party and the chosen Prophetic company.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah al-Anfal 8:20–23:

Allah, the Exalted, commands His believing servants to obey Him and His Messenger, and forbids them from opposing him and from imitating the disbelievers who defied Him and stood in hostility to Him. For this reason He says: ﴿And do not turn away from him﴾, meaning: do not abandon obedience to him, nor comply with his commands, nor refrain from his prohibitions, ﴿while you hear﴾, meaning: after you have come to know what he calls you to.

﴿And do not be like those who say, "We hear," while they do not hear.﴾ It has been said that the intended meaning is the polytheists. This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Ishaq said: They are the hypocrites, for they show that they have heard and responded, but they are not so.

Then Allah, the Exalted, informs that this type of the children of Adam is the worst of creation and of living beings, so He says: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and the dumb who do not reason.﴾

That is: deaf to hearing the truth, ﴿dumb﴾ in understanding it. For this reason He says: ﴿who do not reason﴾. These are the worst of creation, because every creature other than them is obedient to Allah ([Exalted and Majestic]) in what He created it for, whereas these were created for worship and yet they disbelieved. For this reason He likened them to cattle in His saying: ﴿And the example of those who disbelieve is like that of one who shouts to that which does not hear except a call and cry: deaf, dumb, blind, so they do not reason﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 171]. And He said in another verse: ﴿They are like cattle; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 179].

It has also been said that the intended ones here are a group from the Banu 'Abd al-Dar of Quraysh. This is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid, and it is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They are the hypocrites.

I say: There is no contradiction between the polytheists and the hypocrites in this, because each of them is deprived of correct understanding and of the intention to do righteous deeds.

Then Allah, the Exalted, informs that they have no correct understanding and no correct intention, even if it were supposed that they had some understanding. So He says: ﴿And had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear.﴾ That is: He would have made them understand. The sense of the statement is: but there is no good in them, so He did not make them understand, for He knows that ﴿if He had made them hear﴾, meaning: made them understand, ﴿they would have turned away﴾ from it deliberately and stubbornly after understanding it, ﴿while they are refusing.﴾

Al-Bukhari said: "*Istajibu*" means "respond" (ajibu), and "*li-ma yuhyikum*" means "for that which sets you right" (li-ma yuslihukum). Ishaq narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khubayb[[In A: "Habib".]] ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: I heard Hafs ibn Asim narrating from Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla, who said: "I was praying when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me and called me, but I did not come to him until I had finished praying. Then I came to him, and he said: 'What prevented you from coming to me? Did Allah not say: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾?' Then he said: 'I will teach you the greatest surah in the Qur'an before I leave.'" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then set out to leave, and I reminded him [of his promise]. Mu'adh said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khubayb[[In A: "Habib".]] ibn Abd al-Rahman, who heard Hafs ibn Asim, who heard Abu Sa'id, a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, with this [narration]. He said: "It is ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, the seven oft-repeated verses (as-sab' al-mathani)."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4647).]]

This is its wording exactly. The discussion of this hadith, with its various chains, has already been presented at the beginning of the tafsir of al-Fatihah.

Mujahid said, regarding His saying ﴿li-ma yuhyikum﴾: "[It means] the truth."

Qatadah said regarding ﴿li-ma yuhyikum﴾: "It is this Qur'an, in which there is salvation, protection (al-tuqat)[[In K, M: "al-baqa'" (endurance).]] and life."

Al-Suddi said: "﴿li-ma yuhyikum﴾: in Islam is their revival after their death through disbelief."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾: that is, to the war through which Allah the Exalted strengthened you after humiliation, empowered you after weakness, and protected you from your enemy after they had subdued you.

* *

As for His exalted saying ﴿And know that Allah comes between a person and his heart﴾: Ibn Abbas said: "He comes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak as a statement of Ibn Abbas (mawquf), and said: "It is sahih, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it."[[al-Mustadrak (2/328).]] Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through another route as a statement traced to the Prophet ﷺ (marfu'),[[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (4/45).]] but it is not authentic because its chain is weak, and the mawquf version is more authentic. Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id, Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, Atiyyah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and al-Suddi.

In a narration from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿comes between a person and his heart﴾: "until He leaves him unable to reason."

Al-Suddi said: "He comes between a person and his heart, so he cannot believe or disbelieve except by His permission."

Qatadah said: "It is like His saying: ﴿And We are nearer to him than the jugular vein﴾ [Qaf: 16]."

Hadiths have indeed come from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that relate to this verse.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ often used to say: 'O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.'" He said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have believed in you and in what you have brought. Do you fear for us?" He said: "Yes, indeed the hearts are between two fingers of the fingers of Allah the Exalted; He turns them."

Thus al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in the "Book of Qadar" of his Jami', from Hannad ibn al-Sari, from Abu Mu'awiyah Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Darir, from al-A'mash, whose name is Sulayman ibn Mihran, from Abu Sufyan, whose name is Talhah ibn Nafi', from Anas.[[al-Musnad (3/112) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2140).]] Then he said: "Hasan." Likewise it has been narrated from more than one [narrator] from al-A'mash; some narrated it from him, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ. But the hadith of Abu Sufyan from Anas is more authentic.[[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/288) through al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Another hadith: Abd ibn Humayd said in his Musnad: Abd al-Malik ibn Amr narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate: "O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion."

This is a hadith of good chain, except that there is a break (inqita') in it; nevertheless, it meets the conditions of the authors of the Sunan, though they did not record it.[[al-Muntakhab, no. (359).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Jabir say: Busr ibn Abd Allah al-Hadrami narrated to me, that he heard Abu Idris al-Khawlani say: I heard al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Kilabi, may Allah be pleased with him, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "There is no heart except that it is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, Lord of the worlds; if He wills to set it straight, He sets it straight, and if He wills to make it deviate, He makes it deviate." He used to say: "O Turner of the hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion." He said: "And the scale is in the hand of the Most Merciful; He lowers it and raises it."

Likewise narrated al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, and he mentioned something similar.[[al-Musnad (4/182), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (7738), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (199).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yunus narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Mu'alla ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan, that Aisha said: "These are supplications the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to make: 'O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.'" She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you often make this supplication." He said: "Indeed the heart of the son of Adam is between two fingers of the fingers of Allah; if He wills, He makes it deviate, and if He wills, He keeps it firm."[[al-Musnad (6/91).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hashim narrated to us: Abd al-Hamid narrated to us: Shahr narrated to me, I heard Umm Salamah narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to frequently say in his supplication: "O Allah, O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do hearts indeed turn?" He said: "Yes. Allah has not created any of the sons of Adam except that his heart is between two fingers of the fingers of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If He wills, He keeps it firm, and if He wills, He makes it deviate. So we ask Allah, our Lord, that He not make our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to grant us mercy from Himself; indeed He is the Bestower." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you not teach me a supplication to make for myself?" He said: "Yes. Say: 'O Allah, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive my sin, remove the rage of my heart, and protect me from the misleading trials, for as long as You keep me alive.'"[[al-Musnad (6/301), and al-Tirmidhi in the Sunan, no. (3522), through Shahr ibn Hawshab. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: Hayawah narrated to us: Abu Hani informed me that he heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli say that he heard Abd Allah ibn Amr say that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The hearts of the sons of Adam are between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, like one heart, which He turns however He wills." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, Turner of the hearts, turn our hearts to Your obedience."

Muslim alone recorded it among those who transmitted from al-Bukhari; he narrated it together with al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Hayawah ibn Shurayh al-Misri, with the same wording.[[al-Musnad (2/168), Sahih Muslim, no. (2654), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (7861).]]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, commenting on the verse:

Allah, the Exalted, warns His believing servants against ﴿fitnah﴾, meaning a trial and a tribulation, which encompasses the wrongdoer and others besides him. It is not restricted to the people of sins or to those who actually commit the sin, but encompasses both, when it is not averted or removed. As Imam Ahmad said:

Abu Sa'id, the client of Banu Hashim, narrated to us: Shaddad ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ghaylan ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Mutarrif, who said: We said to al-Zubayr: "O Abu 'Abdullah, what brought you here? You failed the caliph who was killed, and then you came seeking his blood?" Al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "We recited during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with them: ﴿And beware of a fitnah which will not afflict those who wronged among you exclusively﴾. We did not think that we were its people until it befell us as it did."

Al-Bazzar also narrated it [[In A: "al-Tirmidhi".]] through the hadith of Mutarrif, from al-Zubayr, and said: "We do not know of Mutarrif narrating from al-Zubayr other than this hadith." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 976.]]

Al-Nasa'i narrated through the hadith of Jarir ibn Hazim, from al-Hasan, from al-Zubayr, something similar to this. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11206.]]

Ibn Jarir narrated: Al-Harith narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Mubarak ibn Fadala narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: Al-Zubayr said: "We were warned by it, meaning His saying [Exalted is He] [[Addition from K.]] ﴿And beware of a fitnah which will not afflict those who wronged among you exclusively﴾, while we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we did not think that we were specifically singled out by it."

Likewise Humayd narrated it from al-Hasan, from al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/474).]]

Dawud ibn Abi Hind said, from al-Hasan, concerning this verse: "It was revealed concerning 'Ali, 'Uthman, [[In D, K, M, A: "'Ammar".]] Talhah and al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them."

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-Salt ibn Dinar, from 'Uqbah ibn Suhban, who said: I heard al-Zubayr say: "I have recited this verse for a time and did not think we were of its people; then, indeed, we are the ones it refers to: ﴿And beware of a fitnah which will not afflict those who wronged among you exclusively, and know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾."

It has been narrated through more than one chain from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam.

Al-Suddi said: "It was revealed specifically concerning the people of Badr, so it afflicted them on the Day of the Camel, and they fought one another."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying [Exalted is He]: ﴿And beware of a fitnah which will not afflict those who wronged among you exclusively﴾, meaning: the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ exclusively.

He also said in another narration from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the interpretation of this verse: "Allah commanded the believers not to allow the evil to persist among them, lest Allah encompass them all with punishment."

This is a very good interpretation. Therefore Mujahid said concerning His saying [Exalted is He]: ﴿And beware of a fitnah which will not afflict those who wronged among you exclusively﴾: "It is also for you." Likewise said al-Dahhak, Yazid ibn Abi Habib, and others.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "There is none among you but that he is encompassed by a fitnah. Indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a fitnah﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15]. So whoever seeks refuge, let him seek refuge in Allah from misleading trials." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

The view that this warning encompasses the Companions and others, even though the address is directed to them, is the correct one. The ahadith that came concerning warning against trials confirm this, and there is a separate book on this subject, which will be clarified, Allah willing, as the scholars did, dedicating separate works to it. Among the most pertinent narrations mentioned here is what Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said:

Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us: 'Abdullah [i.e., Ibn al-Mubarak] informed us: Sayf ibn Abi Sulayman informed us: I heard 'Adi ibn 'Adi al-Kindi say: My client narrated to me that he heard my grandfather, 'Adi ibn 'Umayrah, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not punish the general public for the deeds of the elite until they see evil among them while they are able to change it but do not change it. When they do that, Allah punishes both the elite and the general public." [[Musnad (4/192).]]

In it there is an unnamed man, and none of the authors of the Six Books included it, and Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman al-Hashimi narrated to us: Isma'il [i.e., ibn Ja'far] narrated to us: 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr informed me, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ashhali, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, or Allah will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, then you will supplicate Him and He will not respond to you." [[Musnad (5/388).]]

He also narrated it from Abu Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, and said: "Or Allah will surely send upon you a people, then you will supplicate Him and He will not respond to you." [[In the Musnad (5/388): "Abu Sa'id, client of Banu Hashim, from Sulayman ibn Bilal." Then I checked Atraf al-Musnad of al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar (2/263) and found it as it is in the Musnad.]]

Ahmad said: 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Razin ibn Habib al-Juhani narrated to us, Abu al-Ruqad narrated to me, he said: I went out with my master, and I came to Hudhayfah, and he was saying: "A man would speak a word during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and become a hypocrite, and I hear it from one of you in a single sitting four times: You must enjoin what is good, forbid what is evil, and urge one another to goodness, or Allah will destroy you all with punishment, or your worst among you will be put in authority over you, then your best will supplicate and they will not be answered." [[Musnad (5/390).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from Zakariyya, Amir narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him, delivering a sermon, saying, while pointing with his two fingers to his ears: "The likeness of one who upholds the limits of Allah and one who falls into them, or one who compromises regarding them, is like a people who boarded a ship. Some of them got the lower part, which was narrow and bad, and some got the upper part. Those in the lower part, when they wanted water, passed by those above them and harmed them. They said: 'If we made a hole in our share, we could draw water without harming those above us.' If they are left to their own devices, they will all perish; but if they take hold of their hands, they will all be saved."

Al-Bukhari alone among them transmitted it, not Muslim. He narrated it in "al-Shirkah" and "al-Shahadat", and al-Tirmidhi in "al-Fitan" through more than one route, from Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash, from 'Amir ibn Sharahil al-Sha'bi, with it. [[Musnad (4/269), Sahih al-Bukhari nos. 2493, 2686, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2173.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn narrated to us, Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Layth, from 'Alqamah ibn Martad, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "When sins appear among my ummah, Allah will encompass them with a punishment from Him." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, are there not righteous people among them?" He said: "Yes." She said: "How will those do?" He said: "They will be afflicted with what afflicts the people, then they will go on to forgiveness from Allah and His pleasure." [[Musnad (6/304).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shurayk informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no people among whom sins are committed while among them is a man more honoured and more powerful than them who does not change it, except that Allah will encompass them with punishment" [or: "the punishment will befall them"].

Abu Dawud narrated it from Musaddad, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abu Ishaq, with it. [[Musnad (4/361), Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4339.]]

Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Abu Ishaq narrate, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Jarir, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no people among whom sins are committed, while they are more honoured and more numerous than the one who commits them, and they do not change it, except that Allah will encompass them with punishment." [[Musnad (4/364).]]

He also narrated it from Waki', from Isra'il; and from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar; and from Aswad, from Shurayk and Yunus; all of them from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, with it.

Ibn Majah also narrated it from 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Waki', with it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4009.]]

[Another hadith] Imam Ahmad also said: Sufyan narrated to us, Jami' ibn Abi Rashid narrated to us, from Mundhir, from Hasan ibn Muhammad, from his wife, from 'A'ishah, reaching the Prophet ﷺ: "When evil appears on the earth, Allah sends down His might upon the people of the earth." She said: "And among them are people who obey Allah?" He said: "Yes, then they go on to the mercy of Allah." [[Musnad (6/41).]]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

God, exalted is He, reminds His believing servants of His blessings upon them and His kindness to them. When they were few, He multiplied them. When they were oppressed and afraid, He strengthened them and gave them victory. When they were poor and destitute, He provided for them with good things. He asked them to be grateful, and they obeyed Him and carried out all that He commanded.

This was the condition of the believers during their stay in Makkah: few in number, hiding, compelled, and fearing that people would snatch them away from all corners of God's lands, whether polytheists, Magians or Romans. All of them were enemies to the believers because of their small numbers and lack of strength. This remained their situation until God permitted them to emigrate (hijrah, migration) to Madinah. He gave them shelter there and appointed its people to help them. The people of Madinah gave them shelter and supported them on the day of Badr and other occasions, shared their wealth with them, and gave their lives in obedience to God and His Messenger.

Qatadah ibn Di'amah al-Sadusi (may Allah have mercy on him), commenting on the words of God, exalted is He: ﴿Remember when you were few and oppressed in the land﴾, said: This tribe of the Arabs was the most humiliated of people in abasement, the most wretched in life, the hungriest in their bellies, the most naked in their skins, and the most evidently astray. They were restrained upon a rock, between the two lions, Persia and Rome. By God, there was nothing in their lands at that time for which they could be envied. Whoever lived among them lived in misery, and whoever died among them was thrown into the Fire. They were eaten and did not eat. By God, we know of no tribe among the settled peoples of the earth at that time that was in a worse state than them. Then God brought Islam, and through it He established them in the lands, widened their provision, and made them kings over the necks of people. By Islam God gave you what you see, so be thankful to God for His blessings, for your Lord is the Bestower who loves gratitude, and those who are grateful will be given increase from God [exalted is He].

[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (13/478). This is a great statement from a noble imam, showing that there is no honour except through Islam. It was also reported from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): "We are a people whom Allah has honoured with Islam, so whenever we seek honour through other than Islam, Allah will humiliate us."]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verses 27–28:

'Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him to the Banu Qurayzah so that they would submit to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They consulted him about that, and he gestured to them toward his throat, meaning that it would be slaughter. Then Abu Lubabah realized what he had done and saw that he had betrayed Allah and His Messenger. So he swore that he would not taste any food until he died or Allah accepted his repentance. He went to the Mosque of Madinah and tied himself to one of its pillars, and he remained in that state for nine days, until he would fall unconscious from exhaustion. Then Allah revealed his repentance to His Messenger. People came to give him the good news of Allah's acceptance of his repentance, and they wanted to untie him from the pillar. But he swore that only the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would untie him with his own hand. So he untied him, and Abu Lubabah said: "O Messenger of Allah, I had vowed to give up my wealth as charity." He (ﷺ) said to him: "A third of it will suffice you to give in charity." [Reported by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/481).]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Yunus ibn al-Harith al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah Abu 'Awn al-Thaqafi narrated to us, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the killing of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him: ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse.

Ibn Jarir also said: Al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, Shababah ibn Sawwar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Muharram narrated to us, who said: I met 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, and he narrated to me, saying: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me that Abu Sufyan left Makkah, and Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Abu Sufyan is at such and such a place." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Abu Sufyan is at such and such a place, so go out to him and keep it secret." But a man among the hypocrites wrote to them: "Muhammad intends to attack you, so take your precautions." Then Allah revealed ﴿Do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts﴾ to the end of the verse. [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/480).]

This is a very strange hadith, and both its chain and its context are questionable.

In the two Sahihs there is the story of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, that he wrote to the Quraysh informing them of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) intention toward them in the Year of the Conquest. Allah informed His Messenger of this, so he sent after the letter and retrieved it, and he summoned Hatib, who admitted what he had done. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not strike his neck? He has betrayed Allah, His Messenger and the believers." He (ﷺ) said: "Leave him, for he was present at Badr. What do you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" [See its takhrij at the commentary on verse 9 of this surah.]

I say: The correct view is that the verse is general, even if it is established that it was revealed on a specific occasion. According to the majority of scholars, the ruling is taken from the general wording of the text, not from the specific circumstance. Betrayal (khiyanah) encompasses minor and major sins, those that are inherent and those that affect others.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿and betray your trusts﴾: "The trusts (amanah) are the duties which Allah has entrusted to His servants, meaning the obligations." He said: "Do not betray" means do not break them.

In another narration he said regarding ﴿do not betray Allah and the Messenger﴾: "By abandoning His sunnah and committing His disobedience."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, on the authority of 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, concerning this verse: Do not show Allah any of the truth that He is pleased with from you, and then oppose Him in secret by turning to something else, for that is destruction of your trusts and betrayal of yourselves.

Al-Suddi said: When they betray Allah and the Messenger, they have betrayed their trusts.

He also said: They used to hear the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) and spread it until it reached the polytheists. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd [ibn Aslam] said: He forbade you to betray Allah and the Messenger, as the hypocrites did.

* *

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, meaning a test and an examination from Him for you, since He gave them to you so that He may know whether you will be thankful for them and obey Him concerning them, or whether you will be preoccupied with them to the neglect of Him and exchange Him for them. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15]. He said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya': 35]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, then those are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9]. And He said: ﴿O you who believe, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Taghabun: 14].

* *

His statement: ﴿And that Allah has with Him a great reward﴾, meaning His reward, His bounty and His gardens are better for you than wealth and children. Indeed, among them there may be an enemy, and most of them will not avail you anything. Allah, glorified is He, is the Disposer and Owner of this world and the Hereafter, and with Him is the abundant reward on the Day of Resurrection.

In a narration, Allah, the Exalted, says: "Son of Adam, seek Me and you will find Me. If you find Me, you will find everything. If you lose Me, you lose everything, and I am dearer to you than everything."

In the Sahih, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever possesses three qualities will taste the sweetness of faith: the one for whom Allah and His Messenger are dearer than anything else; the one who loves a person solely for the sake of Allah; and the one who would rather be thrown into the Fire than return to disbelief after Allah has rescued him from it." [Reported by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (43), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Rather, love for His Messenger takes precedence over children, wealth and souls, as is established in the Sahih that he (peace be upon him) said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, none of you truly believes until I am dearer to him than his own self, his family, his wealth and all of mankind." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (14).]
