[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (14).]

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Suddi, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿furqanan﴾ means a way out (makhrajan).

Mujahid added: "in this world and the Hereafter."

In another report from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿furqanan﴾ means salvation (najatan). In another report from him: victory (nasran).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿furqanan﴾ means a distinction (faslan) between truth (al-haqq) and falsehood (al-batil).

This explanation by Ibn Ishaq is more general than those mentioned earlier, and it may encompass all of them. For whoever fears Allah by carrying out His commands and abstaining from what He forbids, is granted the ability to recognize truth from falsehood. That becomes the cause of his victory (in one copy: "his victory"), his deliverance, and his way out of the affairs of this world, and his happiness on the Day of Resurrection, and the expiation of his sins—that is, their erasure—and their concealment (ghafr), meaning covering them from people—as a cause for attaining Allah's abundant reward, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy and will make for you a light by which you will walk and forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Hadid: 28]

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: "liyuthbitoka" means liyuqayyidukā (to bind you, to put you in fetters).

'Ata' and Ibn Zayd said: liyahbisuka (to imprison you).

As-Suddi said: "al-ithbat" is imprisonment and shackling.

This encompasses what these and those said, and it is the collective of the sayings. It is also the usual conduct of one who intends harm to another.

Sunayd narrated from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' said: I heard 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr say: When they plotted against the Prophet ﷺ to confine him, or kill him, or expel him, his paternal uncle Abu Talib said to him: Do you know what they have plotted against you? He said: "They want to imprison me, or kill me, or expel me." He said: Who informed you of this? He said: "My Lord." He said: How excellent a Lord your Lord is. Show him kindness. He said: "Should I show him kindness? Rather, he should show kindness to me." (Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/493).)

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Basri, known as al-Wasawisi, narrated to me: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi Rawwad informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah, that Abu Talib said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: What are your people plotting against you? He said: "They want to imprison me, or kill me, or expel me." He said: Who informed you of this? He said: "My Lord." He said: How excellent a Lord your Lord is; so show him kindness. "He said: Should I show him kindness?! Rather, he should show kindness to me." He said: Then this was revealed: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you﴾ [al-Anfal: 30]... (Tafsir al-Tabari (13/492).)

The mention of Abu Talib in this is very strange, indeed rejected (munkar), because this verse is Madani. Moreover, this story and the gathering of the Quraysh for this plotting and consultation, whether to confine, expel or kill him, took place on the night of the Hijrah, and it was about three years after the death of Abu Talib, when they became bold enough against him after the death of his uncle Abu Talib, who used to protect him, support him and bear his burdens.

The evidence for the correctness of what we have said is what Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, author of "al-Maghazi", narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: al-Kalbi narrated to me, from Badhan, the freedman of Umm Hani', from Ibn 'Abbas, that a group of Quraysh, the nobles of every tribe, gathered to enter the Dar al-Nadwah (the council house). Iblis confronted them in the form of a venerable old man. When they saw him they said: Who are you? He said: A shaykh from Najd. I heard that you had gathered, so I wanted to attend, and my opinion and counsel will not fail you. They said: Yes, enter. So he entered with them and said: Consider the affair of this man. By Allah, he will soon rise against you in your affair with his command. He said: One of them said: Imprison him in fetters, then wait for him to meet the fate of poets, like Zuhayr and al-Nabighah, who died before him; he is just like one of them. He said: The enemy of Allah, the Najdi shaykh, cried out: By Allah, this is not an opinion for you. By Allah, his Lord will bring him out of his confinement to his companions, and they will soon rise against him and take him from your hands and protect him from you, and I fear they will expel you from your lands. He said: Then consider something other than this.

He said: Another of them said: Expel him from among you, and you will be rid of him, for when he leaves, whatever he does will not harm you, wherever he falls. When he is away from you, his harm is gone and you will have rest, and his affair will be with others. The Najdi shaykh said: By Allah, this is not an opinion for you. Do you not see the sweetness of his speech, the charm of his tongue, and how he captures hearts with what you hear of his words? By Allah, if you do that, he will then go among the Arabs, and they will gather against you, then come upon you until he expels you from your lands and kills your nobles. They said: By Allah, he speaks the truth. So consider another way.

He said: Then Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him, said: By Allah, I will give you an opinion that I see no other than it, which you have not yet considered. They said: And what is it? He said: We take from every tribe a young, strong, well-built lad, and each of them is given a sharp sword, then they strike him with one blow as one man, and when they have killed him, his blood will be scattered among all the tribes. Then I do not think the Banu Hashim will be able to fight all of Quraysh. When they see that, they will accept the blood-money, and we will have rest and cut off his harm from us. He said: The Najdi shaykh said: By Allah, this is the opinion. The saying is what the young man said; there is no opinion other than it. He said: So they dispersed upon that, resolved against him.

Then Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and commanded him not to sleep in the bed where he used to sleep, and informed him of the people's scheming.

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not spend that night in his house, and Allah then permitted him to depart. After his arrival in Madinah, Allah revealed al-Anfal, mentioning His blessings upon him and His trial for him: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of planners﴾. Allah also revealed concerning their saying: "Wait for him to meet the fate of poets, like those before him": ﴿Or do they say, "A poet, we await for him the misfortunes of time"?﴾ [al-Tur: 30]. That day was called "the Day of the Crowding" (Yawm al-Zahmah) because of the opinion on which they gathered. (Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/494) through the chain of Ibn Ishaq.)

Similar to this narration is reported from al-Suddi, and Allah revealed concerning their intention to expel him the words of the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, they were about to unsettle you from the land to expel you from it; and then they would not remain after you except a little﴾ [al-Isra': 76].

Similarly al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. And it is reported from Mujahid, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Musa ibn 'Uqbah, Qatadah, Miqsam and others, something similar.

Yunus ibn Bukayr said, from Ibn Ishaq: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained waiting for the command of Allah, until the Quraysh gathered, plotted against him, and intended against him what they intended. Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and commanded him not to sleep in the place where he used to sleep. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and commanded him to sleep in his bed and to wrap himself in his green cloak, and he did so. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the people, who were at his door, carrying a handful of dust, and he began to throw it upon their heads, while Allah took their sight away from His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and he was reciting: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So We covered them, and they cannot see﴾ [Ya-Sin: 1-9].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Something from 'Ikrimah is reported which confirms this.

Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, have related, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Fatimah entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weeping, and he said: "What makes you weep, my little daughter?" She said: O father, why should I not weep, when these chiefs of Quraysh are in al-Hijr making a pact by al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, the third, the other? If they see you, they will rise against you and kill you, and none of them is without knowing his share of your blood. He said: "My daughter, bring me water for ablution." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed wudu', then went out to the mosque. When they saw him they said: "Here he is," and they lowered their heads, and their chins fell upon their chests, and they could not raise their eyes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a handful of dust and threw it at them, saying: "May your faces be disfigured." Not a single pebble of his that struck any man among them failed to kill him as a disbeliever on the day of Badr.

Then al-Hakim said: Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it, and I know of no defect in it. (Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (1691) in Mawarid, and al-Mustadrak (3/157).) Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, 'Uthman al-Jazari informed me, from Miqsam, the freedman of Ibn 'Abbas, who informed him from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the words: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you﴾, he said: The Quraysh consulted one night in Makkah. Some of them said: "When morning comes, restrain him with fetters," meaning the Prophet ﷺ. Some said: "Rather, kill him." Some said: "Rather, expel him." So Allah informed His Prophet of that, and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, spent the night on the bed of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he reached the cave. The polytheists spent the night guarding 'Ali, thinking him to be the Prophet ﷺ. When they woke in the morning they rushed upon him, but when they saw 'Ali, Allah Most High turned back their scheme. They said: "Where is your companion?" He said: "I do not know." So they followed his trail, but when they reached the mountain it became confused for them, so they climbed the mountain and passed by the cave, and they saw spider webs at its entrance. They said: "Had he entered here, there would not be spider webs at its door." He remained in it for three nights. (Al-Musnad (1/348). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/27): "In it is 'Uthman ibn 'Amr al-Jazari, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy while others declared him weak, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih.")

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, concerning the words: ﴿They plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of planners﴾, meaning: "So I plotted against them with My firm scheme, until I delivered you from them."

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 8, verses 31–33 (part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, informs us of the disbelief, insolence, defiance and obstinacy of the Quraysh, and of their false claim, upon hearing His verses when they were recited to them, that they would say: ﴿We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this.﴾ This was merely their saying, not their doing; for they had been challenged more than once to produce a surah like it, and they could find no way to do so. Rather, this was a saying by which they deceived themselves and those who followed them in their falsehood.

It has been said that the one who uttered this was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, may Allah curse him, as Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj and others have stated explicitly. He had travelled to the land of Persia and learned from the stories of their kings, Rustam and Isfandiyar. When he returned, he found that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been sent by Allah and was reciting the Qur'an to the people. Whenever the Messenger ﷺ rose from a gathering, al-Nadr would sit in that same place and narrate to them from the stories of those (kings), then say: "By Allah, which of us tells the better tale, I or Muhammad?" For this reason, when Allah enabled (the Muslims) to overcome him at the Battle of Badr, and he was among the captives, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that his neck be struck, in cold blood, before him, and it was done. All praise is due to Allah. The one who captured him was al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, may Allah be pleased with him, as Ibn Jarir said:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: The Prophet ﷺ killed in cold blood at the Battle of Badr 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, Tu'aymah ibn 'Adi, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Al-Miqdad had captured al-Nadr. When he (the Prophet) ordered his execution, al-Miqdad said: "O Messenger of Allah, (he is) my captive." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He used to say about the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, what he used to say." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered his execution, and al-Miqdad said: "O Messenger of Allah, (he is) my captive." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, enrich al-Miqdad from Your bounty." Al-Miqdad said: "This is what I wanted." He said: And concerning him this verse was revealed: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the myths of the former peoples."﴾

Similarly, Hushaym narrated it from Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyyah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said: "al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi" instead of "Tu'aymah," and this is an error, because al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi was not alive on the day of Badr. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on that day: "If al-Mut'im were alive and then asked me concerning these foul ones (i.e., the captives), I would have given them to him." He was referring to the captives, because al-Mut'im had given protection to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day he returned from Ta'if.

The meaning of ﴿myths of the former peoples﴾ — "asatir" being the plural of "ustura" — is that they are their books which he has borrowed, so he learns from them and recites them to the people. This is pure falsehood, as Allah informed of them in another verse: ﴿And they say, "Myths of the former peoples, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening." Say, "It was sent down by He who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."﴾ [al-Furqan: 5, 6] — meaning, to whoever repents to Him and turns back in devotion; He accepts from him and pardons him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ This is from the abundance of their ignorance, insolence, obstinacy and intense denial, and it is among the things for which they are blamed. It would have been better for them to say: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then guide us to it and enable us to follow it." But instead they asked for victory against themselves, hastened the punishment, and sought its arrival early, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them. And it will surely come to them suddenly while they do not perceive.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 53]; ﴿And they said, "Our Lord, hasten to us our share (of punishment) before the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Sad: 16]; ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment to befall the disbelievers, which none can avert, from Allah, Lord of the ascending stairways.﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1–3]. Likewise the ignorant among the earlier nations spoke, as the people of Shu'ayb said to him: ﴿So cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 187], and these said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.﴾

Shu'bah narrated from 'Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, from Anas ibn Malik who said: It was Abu Jahl ibn Hisham who said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.﴾ So it was revealed: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ — the verse.

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Nadr, both from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh, from his father, from Shu'bah, with this chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4648, 4649]

This Ahmad is Ahmad ibn al-Nadr ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab. This was stated by al-Hakim Abu Ahmad, and al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah al-Nisaburi, and Allah knows best.

Al-A'mash said, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ He said: It was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah. He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment that will befall the disbelievers, which none can avert.﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1–2]. Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi: it was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. 'Ata' added: Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, hasten to us our share (of punishment) before the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Sad: 16] and He said: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 94] and He said: ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment to befall the disbelievers, which none can avert﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1, 2]. 'Ata' said: Some twenty verses of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were revealed concerning him.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Layth narrated to us, Abu Ghassan narrated to us, Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father who said: I saw 'Amr ibn al-'As standing on a horse on the day of Uhud, saying: "O Allah, if what Muhammad says is true, then swallow me and my horse up (into the earth)."

Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You"﴾ — the verse: "This was said by the fools and ignorant ones of this Ummah, and Allah, by His kindness and mercy, overlooked the fools and ignorant ones of this Ummah."

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfah Musa ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, from Abu Zumayl Simak al-Hanafi, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The polytheists used to circumambulate the House saying: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk," and the Prophet ﷺ would say: "Enough, enough!" And they would say: "No partner for You, except a partner who belongs to You, You own him and what he owns." And they would say: "Forgiveness, forgiveness!" So Allah revealed: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: There were two protections among them: the Prophet ﷺ and seeking forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ has departed, and seeking forgiveness remains. [Also narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/511) through Abu Hudhayfah Musa ibn Mas'ud with this chain.]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ruman and Muhammad ibn Qays, who both said: The Quraysh said to one another: "Muhammad, whom Allah has honoured among us": ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.﴾ When evening came, they regretted what they had said, and said: "Forgiveness, O Allah!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿But Allah would not punish them [while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them] while they seek forgiveness﴾ [addition from M], up to His saying: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Anfal: 34].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ means: Allah would not punish a people while their prophets are among them until He brings them out. Then he said: ﴿Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ means: among them are those for whom Allah has already decreed entry into faith, and that is seeking forgiveness — "they seek forgiveness," meaning, "they pray." He means by this the people of Makkah.

The same was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi.

Al-Dahhak and Abu Malik said: ﴿Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ means: the believers who were in Makkah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Dawud narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi [said] narrated to us, Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah placed two protections in this Ummah, so that they will remain safe and shielded from the calamities of punishment as long as they are among them: one protection Allah has taken to Himself, and the other remains among you, namely His saying: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾

Abu Salih 'Abd al-Ghaffar said: One of our companions told me that al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi narrated this hadith to him, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/513).] Likewise it was narrated from Qatadah and Abu al-'Ala' al-Nahwi al-Muqri'.

al-Tirmidhi said: Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from 'Abbad ibn Yusuf, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah sent down to me two protections for my Ummah: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ So when I pass away, I leave among them seeking forgiveness until the Day of Resurrection." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3082. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith, and Isma'il ibn Muhajir is weak in narration."]

What supports this is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Satan said: 'By Your might, my Lord, I will not cease to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they seek forgiveness from Me.'"

Then al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." [Al-Musnad (3/29) and al-Mustadrak (4/261). This is al-Hakim's wording; Ahmad's wording in the Musnad is through Ibn Lahi'ah from Darraj with this chain.]

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Rishdin (that is, Ibn Sa'd) narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Sa'd al-Tujibi narrated to me, from one who narrated to him, from Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The servant is safe from the punishment of Allah for as long as he seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

[[Al-Musnad (6/20).]]

He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment that will befall the disbelievers, which none can avert.﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1–2]. Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi: it was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. 'Ata' added: Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, hasten to us our share (of punishment) before the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Sad: 16] and He said: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 94] and He said: ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment to befall the disbelievers, which none can avert﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1, 2]. 'Ata' said: Some twenty verses of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were revealed concerning him.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Layth narrated to us, Abu Ghassan narrated to us, Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father who said: I saw 'Amr ibn al-'As standing on a horse on the day of Uhud, saying: "O Allah, if what Muhammad says is true, then swallow me and my horse up (into the earth)."

Qatadah said concerning His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You"﴾ — the verse: "This was said by the fools and ignorant ones of this Ummah, and Allah, by His kindness and mercy, overlooked the fools and ignorant ones of this Ummah."

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfah Musa ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, from Abu Zumayl Simak al-Hanafi, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The polytheists used to circumambulate the House saying: "Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk," and the Prophet ﷺ would say: "Enough, enough!" And they would say: "No partner for You, except a partner who belongs to You, You own him and what he owns." And they would say: "Forgiveness, forgiveness!" So Allah revealed: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: There were two protections among them: the Prophet ﷺ and seeking forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ has departed, and seeking forgiveness remains. [Also narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/511) through Abu Hudhayfah Musa ibn Mas'ud with this chain.]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ruman and Muhammad ibn Qays, who both said: The Quraysh said to one another: "Muhammad, whom Allah has honoured among us": ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.﴾ When evening came, they regretted what they had said, and said: "Forgiveness, O Allah!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿But Allah would not punish them [while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them] while they seek forgiveness﴾ [addition from M], up to His saying: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Anfal: 34].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ means: Allah would not punish a people while their prophets are among them until He brings them out. Then he said: ﴿Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ means: among them are those for whom Allah has already decreed entry into faith, and that is seeking forgiveness — "they seek forgiveness," meaning, "they pray." He means by this the people of Makkah.

The same was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi.

Al-Dahhak and Abu Malik said: ﴿Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ means: the believers who were in Makkah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Dawud narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi [said] narrated to us, Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah placed two protections in this Ummah, so that they will remain safe and shielded from the calamities of punishment as long as they are among them: one protection Allah has taken to Himself, and the other remains among you, namely His saying: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾

Abu Salih 'Abd al-Ghaffar said: One of our companions told me that al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi narrated this hadith to him, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/513).] Likewise it was narrated from Qatadah and Abu al-'Ala' al-Nahwi al-Muqri'.

al-Tirmidhi said: Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from 'Abbad ibn Yusuf, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah sent down to me two protections for my Ummah: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ So when I pass away, I leave among them seeking forgiveness until the Day of Resurrection." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3082. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith, and Isma'il ibn Muhajir is weak in narration."]

What supports this is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Satan said: 'By Your might, my Lord, I will not cease to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they seek forgiveness from Me.'"

Then al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." [Al-Musnad (3/29) and al-Mustadrak (4/261). This is al-Hakim's wording; Ahmad's wording in the Musnad is through Ibn Lahi'ah from Darraj with this chain.]

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Rishdin (that is, Ibn Sa'd) narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Sa'd al-Tujibi narrated to me, from one who narrated to him, from Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The servant is safe from the punishment of Allah for as long as he seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

[[Al-Musnad (6/20).]]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 8, verses 31–33 (part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, informs us of the disbelief, insolence, defiance and obstinacy of the Quraysh, and of their false claim, upon hearing His verses when they were recited to them, that they would say: ﴿We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this.﴾ This was merely their saying, not their doing; for they had been challenged more than once to produce a surah like it, and they could find no way to do so. Rather, this was a saying by which they deceived themselves and those who followed them in their falsehood.

It has been said that the one who uttered this was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, may Allah curse him, as Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj and others have stated explicitly. He had travelled to the land of Persia and learned from the stories of their kings, Rustam and Isfandiyar. When he returned, he found that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been sent by Allah and was reciting the Qur'an to the people. Whenever the Messenger ﷺ rose from a gathering, al-Nadr would sit in that same place and narrate to them from the stories of those (kings), then say: "By Allah, which of us tells the better tale, I or Muhammad?" For this reason, when Allah enabled (the Muslims) to overcome him at the Battle of Badr, and he was among the captives, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that his neck be struck, in cold blood, before him, and it was done. All praise is due to Allah. The one who captured him was al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, may Allah be pleased with him, as Ibn Jarir said:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: The Prophet ﷺ killed in cold blood at the Battle of Badr 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, Tu'aymah ibn 'Adi, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. Al-Miqdad had captured al-Nadr. When he (the Prophet) ordered his execution, al-Miqdad said: "O Messenger of Allah, (he is) my captive." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He used to say about the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, what he used to say." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered his execution, and al-Miqdad said: "O Messenger of Allah, (he is) my captive." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, enrich al-Miqdad from Your bounty." Al-Miqdad said: "This is what I wanted." He said: And concerning him this verse was revealed: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the myths of the former peoples."﴾

Similarly, Hushaym narrated it from Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyyah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said: "al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi" instead of "Tu'aymah," and this is an error, because al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi was not alive on the day of Badr. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on that day: "If al-Mut'im were alive and then asked me concerning these foul ones (i.e., the captives), I would have given them to him." He was referring to the captives, because al-Mut'im had given protection to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day he returned from Ta'if.

The meaning of ﴿myths of the former peoples﴾ — "asatir" being the plural of "ustura" — is that they are their books which he has borrowed, so he learns from them and recites them to the people. This is pure falsehood, as Allah informed of them in another verse: ﴿And they say, "Myths of the former peoples, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening." Say, "It was sent down by He who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."﴾ [al-Furqan: 5, 6] — meaning, to whoever repents to Him and turns back in devotion; He accepts from him and pardons him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ This is from the abundance of their ignorance, insolence, obstinacy and intense denial, and it is among the things for which they are blamed. It would have been better for them to say: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then guide us to it and enable us to follow it." But instead they asked for victory against themselves, hastened the punishment, and sought its arrival early, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them. And it will surely come to them suddenly while they do not perceive.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 53]; ﴿And they said, "Our Lord, hasten to us our share (of punishment) before the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Sad: 16]; ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment to befall the disbelievers, which none can avert, from Allah, Lord of the ascending stairways.﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1–3]. Likewise the ignorant among the earlier nations spoke, as the people of Shu'ayb said to him: ﴿So cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 187], and these said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.﴾

Shu'bah narrated from 'Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, from Anas ibn Malik who said: It was Abu Jahl ibn Hisham who said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.﴾ So it was revealed: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ — the verse.

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Ahmad and Muhammad ibn al-Nadr, both from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh, from his father, from Shu'bah, with this chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4648, 4649]

This Ahmad is Ahmad ibn al-Nadr ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab. This was stated by al-Hakim Abu Ahmad, and al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah al-Nisaburi, and Allah knows best.

Al-A'mash said, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ He said: It was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah. He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment that will befall the disbelievers, which none can avert.﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1–2]. Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi: it was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. 'Ata' added: Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, hasten to us our share (of punishment) before the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Sad: 16] and He said: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 94] and He said: ﴿A seeker asked for a punishment to befall the disbelievers, which none can avert﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1, 2]. 'Ata' said: Some twenty verses of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were revealed concerning him.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Layth narrated to us, Abu Ghassan narrated to us, Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father who said: I saw 'Amr ibn al-'As standing on a horse on the day of Uhud, saying: "O Allah, if what Muhammad says is true, then swallow me and my horse up (into the earth)."

* *

So Allah revealed: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: There were two protections among them: the Prophet ﷺ and seeking forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ has departed, and seeking forgiveness remains. [Also narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/511) through Abu Hudhayfah Musa ibn Mas'ud with this chain.]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to me, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ruman and Muhammad ibn Qays, who both said: The Quraysh said to one another: "Muhammad, whom Allah has honoured among us": ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.﴾ When evening came, they regretted what they had said, and said: "Forgiveness, O Allah!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿But Allah would not punish them [while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them] while they seek forgiveness﴾ [addition from M], up to His saying: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Anfal: 34].

Then he said: ﴿Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ means: among them are those for whom Allah has already decreed entry into faith, and that is seeking forgiveness — "they seek forgiveness," meaning, "they pray." Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Dawud narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi [said] narrated to us, Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah placed two protections in this Ummah, so that they will remain safe and shielded from the calamities of punishment as long as they are among them: one protection Allah has taken to Himself, and the other remains among you, namely His saying: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾

Abu Salih 'Abd al-Ghaffar said: One of our companions told me that al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi narrated this hadith to him, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/513).] Likewise it was narrated from Qatadah and Abu al-'Ala' al-Nahwi al-Muqri'.

al-Tirmidhi said: Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from 'Abbad ibn Yusuf, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah sent down to me two protections for my Ummah: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ So when I pass away, I leave among them seeking forgiveness until the Day of Resurrection." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3082. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith, and Isma'il ibn Muhajir is weak in narration."]

What supports this is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Satan said: 'By Your might, my Lord, I will not cease to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they seek forgiveness from Me.'"

Then al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." [Al-Musnad (3/29) and al-Mustadrak (4/261). This is al-Hakim's wording; Ahmad's wording in the Musnad is through Ibn Lahi'ah from Darraj with this chain.]

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Rishdin (that is, Ibn Sa'd) narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Sa'd al-Tujibi narrated to me, from one who narrated to him, from Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The servant is safe from the punishment of Allah for as long as he seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

[[Al-Musnad (6/20).]]

He, may He be exalted, informs us that they deserve to be punished, but He did not inflict that upon them because of the blessing of the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among them. For this reason, when he left their midst, Allah inflicted His might upon them on the Day of Badr, so their leaders were killed and their nobles were taken captive. He, may He be exalted, also guided them to seek forgiveness for the sins they were engaged in, namely shirk and corruption.

Qatadah, as-Suddi and others said: "The people did not seek forgiveness, and had they sought forgiveness they would not have been punished."

Ibn Jarir chose this view: "If it were not for the weak believers among them who sought forgiveness, the punishment that cannot be averted would have befallen them. But it was averted from them because of those believers, just as He, may He be exalted, said regarding the day of al-Hudaybiyah: ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and the offering held back from reaching its place of sacrifice. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and thereby incur blame on account of them without knowledge, [Allah would have permitted you to engage them]. [That is] so that Allah may admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Fath: 25]."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Ibn Abza who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah, and Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾. He said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) left for Madinah, and Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. He said: Those remaining believers who stayed there, seeking forgiveness, meaning in Makkah. When they left, Allah revealed: ﴿But what [reason] do they have that Allah should not punish them while they bar [access to] the Sacred Mosque, and they are not its guardians?﴾. He said: Then Allah permitted the conquest of Makkah, and that is the punishment He had promised them."

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak and others, something similar to this.

It has also been said that this verse abrogates His statement: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, on the understanding that the intended meaning is that the seeking of forgiveness proceeds from them themselves.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: "In al-Anfal, He said: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, then the verse that follows abrogated it: ﴿But what [reason] do they have that Allah should not punish them…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve﴾. They were fought in Makkah, and hunger and harm befell them there."

Similarly, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Tumaylah Yahya ibn Wadih.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij and Uthman ibn Ata, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. Then He excepted the people of shirk, saying [may He be exalted]: ﴿But what [reason] do they have that Allah should not punish them while they bar [access to] the Sacred Mosque﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿But what [reason] do they have that Allah should not punish them while they bar [access to] the Sacred Mosque, and they are not its guardians. Its guardians are none but the God-fearing, but most of them do not know﴾. That is: and how would Allah not punish them while they bar [access to] the Sacred Mosque, which is in Makkah, barring the believers, who are its people, from prayer near it and from circumambulating it? For this reason He said: ﴿and they are not its guardians﴾, meaning: they are not the people of the Sacred Mosque; its people are rather the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves to disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. The mosques of Allah are only maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakah, and fear none but Allah. For those, it is expected that they will be among the guided﴾ [al-Tawbah: 17-18], and He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And [it is] averting [people] from the way of Allah and disbelief in Him and [from] the Sacred Mosque and the expulsion of its people from it that are greater in the sight of Allah. [And fitnah is greater than killing]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217] and the verse [continues].

The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his tafsir of this verse: Sulayman ibn Ahmad, that is al-Tabarani, narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Ilyas ibn Sadaqah al-Misri narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, Nuh ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Who are your family (ali)?" He said: "Every God-fearing person." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Its guardians are none but the God-fearing﴾.

[Note: al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (5002), "Majma' al-Bahrayn", and said: "No one narrated it from Yahya except Nuh, and Nu'aym is alone in it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/269): "In it is Nuh ibn Abi Maryam, who is weak."]

Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Bakr al-Shafi'i narrated to us, Ishaq ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Isma'il ibn Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered Quraysh and said: "Is there among you anyone from outside your own [tribe]?" They said: "Among us is the son of our sister, among us is our ally, and among us is our client." He said: "Our ally is from us, the son of our sister is from us, and our client is from us. Indeed, my guardians from among you are the God-fearing."

Then he said: This hadith is sahih, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it.

Urwah, al-Suddi and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding His saying: ﴿Its guardians are none but the God-fearing﴾: They are Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

Mujahid said: They are the strivers (al-mujahidun), whoever they are and wherever they are.

Then He, may He be exalted, mentioned what they used to do at the Sacred Mosque and how they used to treat it, saying: ﴿And their prayer at the House was not but whistling and clapping﴾.

Al-mukaʼ is whistling, and they were likened to the whistling of birds and the taṣdiyah to clapping.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abu Umar narrated to us, Qurrah narrated to us, from Atiyyah, from Ibn Umar regarding His saying: ﴿And their prayer at the House was not but whistling and clapping﴾: He said: al-Mukaʼ is whistling, and al-Taṣdiyah is clapping. Qurrah said: Atiyyah related to us Ibn Umar's action, so Ibn Umar whistled, tilted his cheek, and clapped his hands.

It is also narrated from Ibn Umar that he said: "They used to place their cheeks on the ground, and they clapped and whistled." Ibn Abi Hatim related it in his tafsir with his chain from him.

Ikrimah said: "They used to circumambulate the House going to the left."

Mujahid said: "They only did that so that they might confuse the Prophet's (ﷺ) prayer."

Al-Zuhri said: "They used to mock the believers."

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd regarding ﴿wa-taṣdiyah﴾: "It is their barring people from the way of Allah, exalted and majestic is He."

His saying: ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve﴾. Al-Dahhak, Ibn Juraij and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It is what befell them on the Day of Badr of killing and captivity. Ibn Jarir chose this and did not mention any other view.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid who said: "The punishment of the people of affirmation (who had accepted the message) is by the sword, and the punishment of the people of denial is by the Scream (al-sayhah) and the earthquake (al-zalzalah)."

He, may He be exalted, informs us that they deserve to be punished, but He did not inflict that upon them because of the blessing of the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among them. For this reason, when he left their midst, Allah inflicted His might upon them on the Day of Badr, so their leaders were killed and their nobles were taken captive. He, may He be exalted, also guided them to seek forgiveness for the sins they were engaged in, namely shirk and corruption.

Qatadah, as-Suddi and others said: "The people did not seek forgiveness, and had they sought forgiveness they would not have been punished."

Ibn Jarir chose this view: "If it were not for the weak believers among them who sought forgiveness, the punishment that cannot be averted would have befallen them. But it was averted from them because of those believers, just as He, may He be exalted, said regarding the day of al-Hudaybiyah: ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and the offering held back from reaching its place of sacrifice. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and thereby incur blame on account of them without knowledge, [Allah would have permitted you to engage them]. [That is] so that Allah may admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Fath: 25]."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Ibn Abza who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah, and Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾. He said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) left for Madinah, and Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. He said: Those remaining believers who stayed there, seeking forgiveness, meaning in Makkah. When they left, Allah revealed: ﴿But what [reason] do they have that Allah should not punish them while they bar [access to] the Sacred Mosque, and they are not its guardians?﴾. He said: Then Allah permitted the conquest of Makkah, and that is the punishment He had promised them."

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak and others, something similar to this.

It has also been said that this verse abrogates His statement: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, on the understanding that the intended meaning is that the seeking of forgiveness proceeds from them themselves.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: "In al-Anfal, He said: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, then the verse that follows abrogated it: ﴿But what [reason] do they have that Allah should not punish them…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve﴾. They were fought in Makkah, and hunger and harm befell them there."

Similarly, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Tumaylah Yahya ibn Wadih.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij and Uthman ibn Ata, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. Then He excepted the people of shirk, saying [may He be exalted]: ﴿But what [reason] do they have that Allah should not punish them while they bar [access to] the Sacred Mosque﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿But what [reason] do they have that Allah should not punish them while they bar [access to] the Sacred Mosque, and they are not its guardians. Its guardians are none but the God-fearing, but most of them do not know﴾. That is: and how would Allah not punish them while they bar [access to] the Sacred Mosque, which is in Makkah, barring the believers, who are its people, from prayer near it and from circumambulating it? For this reason He said: ﴿and they are not its guardians﴾, meaning: they are not the people of the Sacred Mosque; its people are rather the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves to disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. The mosques of Allah are only maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakah, and fear none but Allah. For those, it is expected that they will be among the guided﴾ [al-Tawbah: 17-18], and He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And [it is] averting [people] from the way of Allah and disbelief in Him and [from] the Sacred Mosque and the expulsion of its people from it that are greater in the sight of Allah. [And fitnah is greater than killing]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217] and the verse [continues].

The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said in his tafsir of this verse: Sulayman ibn Ahmad, that is al-Tabarani, narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Ilyas ibn Sadaqah al-Misri narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, Nuh ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Who are your family (ali)?" He said: "Every God-fearing person." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Its guardians are none but the God-fearing﴾.

[Note: al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (5002), "Majma' al-Bahrayn", and said: "No one narrated it from Yahya except Nuh, and Nu'aym is alone in it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/269): "In it is Nuh ibn Abi Maryam, who is weak."]

They said: "Among us is the son of our sister, among us is our ally, and among us is our client." He said: "Our ally is from us, the son of our sister is from us, and our client is from us. Indeed, my guardians from among you are the God-fearing."

Then he said: This hadith is sahih, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it.

Urwah, al-Suddi and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding His saying: ﴿Its guardians are none but the God-fearing﴾: They are Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

Mujahid said: They are the strivers (al-mujahidun), whoever they are and wherever they are.

They spoke to Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb and to those among the Quraysh who had merchandise in that caravan, saying: "O assembly of the Quraysh, Muḥammad has taken your vengeance and killed your best men. He said: Concerning them, as was mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth [to prevent from the way of Allah]﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve, to Hell they will be gathered﴾. [[Narrated also by al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsīr (13/532).]]

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good﴾. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good﴾: that He may distinguish the people of happiness from the people of misery. Al-Suddī said: He distinguishes the believer from the disbeliever. This may refer to a distinction in the Hereafter, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then We will say to those who associated partners, "Stay in your place, you and your partners." Then We will separate them﴾ [Yūnus 10:28]. He also said: ﴿And the Day the Hour is established, that Day they will be separated﴾ [al-Rūm 30:14], and in another verse: ﴿That Day they will be split apart﴾ [al-Rūm 30:43], and He said: ﴿And stand apart today, O criminals﴾ [Yā-Sīn 36:59].

It may also refer to a distinction in this world, by what appears of their deeds to the believers, and the "lām" here indicates cause: that is, We enabled them to have wealth to spend in barring from the way of Allah, so that Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good, meaning who obeys Him by fighting His disbelieving enemies, and who disobeys Him by shrinking from that. As He said: ﴿And what struck you on the day the two hosts met was by permission of Allah, and that He might know the believers, and that He might know those who were hypocrites. And it was said to them, "Come, fight in the way of Allah or repel [the enemy]." They said, "If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you."﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:166–167], and He said: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:179], and He said: ﴿Do you think you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who strove and known the patient?﴾ [Āl ʿImrān 3:142], and its counterpart in Barāʾah as well.

So the meaning of the verse according to this is: We only tested you through the disbelievers who fight you, and We enabled them to spend and expend wealth in that, so that the wicked may be distinguished from the good, and so that the wicked may be piled upon one another, ﴿and [He] heaps it up﴾, meaning He gathers it all together, and this is gathering one thing upon another, as He said about the cloud: ﴿Then He makes it into layers﴾ [al-Nūr 24:43], meaning piled up and layered. ﴿And puts it into Hell. Those are the losers﴾, meaning these are the losers in this world and the Hereafter.

Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease,﴾ meaning from what they are engaged in of disbelief, opposition, obstinacy, and stubbornness, and enter into Islam, submission, and returning (to Allah), ﴿they will be forgiven what has passed,﴾ meaning their disbelief, their sins, and their wrongdoings. This is as has come in the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu Wa'il, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does good in Islam will not be held accountable for what he did in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance), and whoever does evil in Islam will be held accountable for both the earlier and the later (deeds)." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6921), and Sahih Muslim, no. (120).]] Also in the Sahih: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Islam erases what came before it, and repentance erases what came before it."
* *
As for His words, ﴿but if they return,﴾ meaning if they persist in what they are engaged in, ﴿then the way of the former peoples has already passed,﴾ meaning our way with the former peoples has already passed: that when they denied and persisted in their obstinacy, We would hasten punishment and retribution upon them.
* *
As for His words, ﴿then the way of the former peoples has already passed,﴾ meaning concerning the Quraysh on the Day of Badr and others among the nations. Al-Suddi and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: meaning the Day of Badr.
* *
As for His words, ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah,﴾ al-Bukhari said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya narrated to us, Haywah ibn Shurayh narrated to us, from Bakr ibn 'Amr, from Bukayr, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: that a man came to him and said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, do you not hear what Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 9] to the end of the verse? Why do you not fight as Allah mentioned in His Book?" He said: "O my nephew, I would rather be reproached with this verse than fight, than be reproached with the verse where Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ [An-Nisa: 93] to the end of the verse." The man said: "But Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah.﴾" Ibn 'Umar said: "We did that during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) when Islam was few and a man would be tried in his religion: either they would kill him or they would imprison him, until Islam became widespread and there was no more fitnah." When the man saw that he would not agree with him on what he wanted, he said: "Then what is your opinion about 'Ali and 'Uthman?" Ibn 'Umar said: "What is my opinion about 'Ali and 'Uthman? As for 'Uthman, Allah had pardoned him, and you disliked that He pardoned him. As for 'Ali, he is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his son-in-law," and he pointed with his hand, "and this is his daughter, or his (Prophet's) daughter, as you see."
