As for 'Uthman, Allah had pardoned him, and you disliked that He pardoned him. As for 'Ali, he is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his son-in-law," and he pointed with his hand, "and this is his daughter, or his (Prophet's) daughter, as you see."
And Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Bayan narrated to us that Wabarah narrated to him, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, came out to us, or to us, and a man said: "What is your view on fighting in fitnah?" He said: "Do you know what fitnah is? Muhammad (ﷺ) used to fight the polytheists, and entering among them was fitnah. Your fighting is not for kingship."
This entire chain is the wording of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4650, 4651).]]
'Ubayd Allah narrated, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that two men came to him during the fitnah of Ibn al-Zubayr and said: "The people have done what you see, and you are the son of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and the companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What prevents you from going out?" He said: "What prevents me is that Allah has forbidden me the blood of my Muslim brother." They said: "Did not Allah say: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah﴾?" He said: "We fought until there was no more fitnah and religion was entirely for Allah, but you want to fight until there is fitnah and religion is for other than Allah."
Likewise Hammad ibn Salamah narrated it, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Ayyub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Lakhmi, who said: "I was with 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, when a man came to him and said: 'Allah says: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah.﴾' Ibn 'Umar said: 'I and my companions fought until religion was entirely for Allah, shirk departed, and there was no fitnah. But you and your companions fight until there is fitnah and religion is for other than Allah.'" Ibn Mardawayh narrated both of these.
Abu 'Awanah said, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, who said: Dhu al-Butayn, meaning Usamah ibn Zayd, said: "I will never fight a man who says: there is no god but Allah." He said: Sa'd ibn Malik said: "By Allah, I will never fight a man who says: there is no god but Allah." A man said: "Did not Allah say: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah﴾?" They both said: "We fought until there was no more fitnah and religion was entirely for Allah." Ibn Mardawayh narrated this.
Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah,﴾ meaning until there is no more shirk. Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' (from Anas), al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise.
Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It reached me from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others from among our scholars: ﴿until there is no more fitnah﴾ means until no Muslim is tried in his religion.
* *
As for His words, ﴿and religion is entirely for Allah,﴾ al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse, that he said: it means making the tawhid (monotheism) sincerely for Allah.
Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ means that it is said: there is no god but Allah.
Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: it means that tawhid is sincerely for Allah, with no shirk in it, and that what is other than Him of rivals is cast off. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ means that there is no disbelief alongside your religion.
What supports this is what is established in the two Sahihs from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "I have been commanded to fight people until they say: there is no god but Allah. When they say it, they have protected their blood and their property from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (25), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (22), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] And in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about a man who fights out of bravery, fights out of zeal, and fights for show: which of these is in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? He said: "Whoever fights so that the Word of Allah is the highest, he is in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2810), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1904).]]
* *
As for His words, ﴿then if they cease,﴾ meaning from fighting them over what they are engaged in of disbelief, then hold back from them, even if you do not know their inner states, ﴿then Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [At-Tawbah: 5], and in another verse: ﴿then they are your brothers in religion﴾ [At-Tawbah: 11].
And He said: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is for Allah. And if they cease, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 193]. In the Sahih, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Usamah, when he had raised his sword over that man, and the man said: "There is no god but Allah," and he struck him and killed him, and this was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): he said to Usamah: "Did you kill him after he said: there is no god but Allah? What will you do with 'there is no god but Allah' on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, he only said it to seek refuge." He said: "Did you not split open his heart?" And he kept saying and repeating to him: "Who will be your advocate with 'there is no god but Allah' on the Day of Resurrection?" Usamah said: "Until I wished that I had not become Muslim until that day." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4269), and Sahih Muslim, no. (96).]]
* *
As for His words, ﴿And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your Protector; how excellent a Protector and how excellent a Helper,﴾ meaning: and if they persist in opposing you and fighting you, ﴿then know that Allah is your Protector﴾ (your Master, and your Helper against your enemies), so how excellent a Protector and how excellent a Helper He is.

Muhammad ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: He narrated to me, Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad: My father narrated to us, Aban al-Attar narrated to us, Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us, from Urwah: that Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to him asking him about several matters, and Urwah wrote back to him: "Peace be upon you. I praise Allah to you, the One besides whom there is no god. To proceed: you wrote to me asking about the departure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Makkah, and I will inform you of it. There is no power and no strength except with Allah. Concerning the departure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Makkah: Allah gave him prophethood, and what an excellent Prophet, what an excellent leader, and what an excellent kinsman he was. May Allah reward him with good, and may He make us know his face in Paradise, and may He give us life upon his religion, cause us to die upon it, and raise us upon it. When he called his people to the guidance and light that Allah had sent him with, which was revealed to him, they did not at first distance themselves from him when he called them to it, and they nearly listened to him, until he mentioned their idols. Some people from Quraysh who had come from Taif, who had wealth, denounced that, and the people rejected it against him, grew hostile toward him, disliked what he said, and incited against him whoever obeyed them. Thus the common people turned away from him and abandoned him, except those whom Allah protected from among them, and they were few. He remained in that state for as long as Allah had decreed he should remain. Then their leaders conspired to tempt whoever followed him away from the religion of Allah, from among their sons, their brothers and their tribes. So there was a severe trial that shook them greatly, and whoever was tempted was tempted, and Allah preserved whomever He willed of them. When this was done to the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered them to leave for the land of Abyssinia. In Abyssinia there was a righteous king called al-Najashi, under whose rule no one was wronged, and he was praised for this. The land of Abyssinia was a trading place for Quraysh, where they traded, and it was a dwelling for their merchants, where they found abundant provision, security, and good commerce. So the Prophet (ﷺ) directed them there, and most of them went there when they were overpowered in Makkah, and he feared for them the trials. He himself stayed and did not leave. He remained that way for years, while they persecuted whoever among them had embraced Islam. Then Islam spread there, and men of their nobles and their strong ones entered it. When they saw that, they slackened their pressure against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions. The first trial was what drove out those among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who left toward the land of Abyssinia, out of fear of it and in flight from the trials and turmoil they were in. When pressure was eased on them and whoever entered Islam from among them did so, news spread of their slackening toward them, that it had eased toward those among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who were in Makkah, and that they would no longer be tried. So they returned to Makkah, and they nearly felt secure there, and they began to increase and multiply. Also, many people from the Ansar in Madinah embraced Islam, Islam spread in Madinah, and the people of Madinah began to come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makkah. When Quraysh saw that, they conspired to tempt them and to be harsher, so they seized them, and they were eager to tempt them, and great hardship afflicted them. This was the last trial. Thus there were two trials: a trial that drove out those who left for the land of Abyssinia when the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them to go there and permitted them to leave for it, and a trial when they returned and saw those coming to them from the people of Madinah. Then seventy chiefs from Madinah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the leaders of those who had embraced Islam, and they met him during the Hajj and pledged allegiance to him at al-Aqabah, and they gave him their covenants that: 'We are with you and you are with us, and that whoever comes from your companions or you come to us, we will protect you as we protect ourselves.' Quraysh then grew hostile toward them, so the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered his companions to leave for Madinah. This was the last trial, in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drove out his companions, and he himself left, and it is the one about which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and the religion is entirely for Allah﴾."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/539).]]

Then he narrated it from Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad, from his father, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr: that he wrote to al-Walid, meaning the son of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, with this, and he mentioned something similar.

[[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/542).]]

This chain is sound up to Urwah, may Allah have mercy on him.

Almighty God explains the details of what He legislated specifically for this noble Ummah, distinguishing it from all the earlier nations, concerning the lawfulness of spoils (maghanim). The ghanimah (spoils of war) is the wealth taken from the disbelievers through the charging of horses and riding camels. The fay' (property gained without battle) is what is taken from them by other means, such as property they agree to surrender through a peace treaty, or property left by people who die with no heir, as well as the jizyah (poll tax), the kharaj (land tax), and similar revenues. This is the view of Imam al-Shafi'i and a group of scholars of the earlier and later generations.

Some scholars apply the term fay' to what is also called ghanimah, and apply ghanimah to fay' as well. For this reason, Qatadah held that this verse abrogated (naskh) the verse of al-Hashr: ﴿Whatever God has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God, to the Messenger, to the near kin, the orphans, the needy﴾ [al-Hashr: 7]. He said: the verse of al-Anfal abrogated that one, and made the spoils four-fifths for the fighters and one-fifth for those mentioned. But this claim is far-fetched, because this verse was revealed after the Battle of Badr, whereas that verse was revealed concerning the Banu al-Nadir. There is no disagreement among the scholars of the sira (biographies of the Prophet) and the maghazi (military campaigns) in general that the Banu al-Nadir episode came after Badr. This is a matter beyond doubt. Whoever distinguishes between the meaning of fay' and ghanimah says: that verse was revealed about fay' property, and this one about spoils. Whoever holds that the matter of spoils and fay' is referred to the judgment of the ruler says: there is no contradiction between the verse of al-Hashr and the one-fifth division when the ruler sees fit. And God knows best.

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And know that whatever you gain as spoils, a fifth of it belongs to God﴾ is an emphasis on dividing every amount, small or large, even a thread or a needle. God Almighty said: ﴿Whoever defrauds will bring what he defrauded on the Day of Resurrection; then every soul will be paid in full for what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 161].

* *

His saying: ﴿a fifth of it belongs to God and to the Messenger﴾. The commentators differed here. Some said: God has a share of the fifth that is placed in the Ka'bah.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi related from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ would be brought the spoils and would divide them into five parts. Four-fifths went to those who had witnessed the battle. Then he would take the fifth, put his hand into it, and take from it a handful, which he would place for the Ka'bah, and it was God's share. Then he would divide what remained into five shares: one share for the Messenger, one share for the near kin, one for the orphans, one for the needy, and one for the wayfarer. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/550).]

Others said: the mention of God here is an opening phrase of blessing, and his share is for His Messenger, peace be upon him. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that when the Messenger of God ﷺ sent out a detachment and they gained spoils, he would set aside a fifth of the spoils and divide that fifth into five parts. Then he recited: ﴿And know that whatever you gain as spoils, a fifth of it belongs to God and to the Messenger﴾. [He said: and His saying] ﴿a fifth of it belongs to God﴾ is an opening phrase, [for] ﴿To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾. So He made the share of God and the share of the Messenger one.

Likewise said Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Sha'bi, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, 'Abdullah ibn Buraydah, Qatadah, Mughirah, and many others: that the share of God and His Messenger is one.

This is supported by what al-Imam al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi related with a sound chain of narration, from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from a man of Bulqayn, who said: I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was at Wadi al-Qura, and he was showing a horse. I said: O Messenger of God, what do you say about the spoils? He said: "God's share of it is one-fifth, and four-fifths are for the army." I said: Is anyone more entitled to it than anyone else? He said: "No, not even the arrow you draw from your side. You are not more entitled to it than your Muslim brother." [al-Sunan al-Kubra (6/324).]

Al-Tabari said: Ammar ibn Musa narrated to us, 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Aban narrated to us, from al-Hasan who said: Abu Bakr bequeathed a fifth of his wealth, and said: Shall I not be content with my wealth with what God was content with for Himself? [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/550).]

Then those who held this view differed. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The spoils were divided into five parts. Four of them were distributed among those who fought for them, and one fifth was divided into four parts: a quarter for God and His Messenger and the near kin, meaning the kin of the Prophet ﷺ. What belonged to God and the Messenger went to the kin of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ took nothing from the fifth. [The second quarter was for the orphans, the third quarter for the needy, and the fourth quarter for the wayfarer.] [What is between the brackets is from Tafsir al-Tabari.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Ma'mar al-Minqari narrated to us, 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Husayn al-Mu'allim, from 'Abdullah ibn Buraydah concerning His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you gain as spoils, a fifth of it belongs to God and to the Messenger﴾. He said: What belongs to God is for His Prophet, and what belongs to the Messenger is for his wives.

'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman said, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah: The fifth of God and the fifth of the Messenger is one. He takes from it and disposes of it as he wishes, meaning the Prophet ﷺ.

This is more general and comprehensive: the Messenger ﷺ disposes of the fifth that God gave him as he wills, and gives it to his Ummah however he wishes. This is supported by what Imam Ahmad related, where he said:

Ishaq ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Maryam, from Abu Sallam al-A'raj, from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'd Yakrib al-Kindi: that he sat with 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Abu al-Darda', and al-Harith ibn Mu'awiyah al-Kindi, may God be pleased with them, and they discussed the hadith of the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abu al-Darda' said to 'Ubadah: O 'Ubadah, what did the Messenger of God ﷺ say in such-and-such a battle concerning the fifths? 'Ubadah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ led them in prayer during a battle, toward a camel from the booty. When he finished the salam, the Messenger of God ﷺ stood, took a tuft of hair between his fingertips, and said: "This is from your spoils, and I have no share in it except my portion along with you, besides the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you. So render back the thread and the needle, and what is greater or smaller than that, and do not defraud, for defrauding is a fire and a shame upon its perpetrators in this world and the Hereafter. Strive against people in God's cause, the near and the far, and do not fear the blame of any blamer for God's sake. Uphold the limits of God in residence and in travel. Strive in God's way, for jihad is one of the gates of Paradise, through which God rescues from distress and grief." [al-Musnad (5/316).]

This is an excellent good hadith, and I have not found it in any of the Six Books through this chain. However, Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also related, from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said something similar concerning the story of the fifth and the prohibition of defrauding. [al-Musnad (2/184) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2694.]

Also from 'Amr ibn 'Abasah: the Messenger of God ﷺ led them in prayer toward a camel from the booty, and when he finished the salam he took a tuft of hair from that camel, then said: "It is not lawful for me of your spoils, even the like of this, except the fifth, and the fifth is returned among you." Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2755.]

The Prophet ﷺ did have something from the spoils that he would select for himself: a slave, a female slave, a horse, a sword, or something similar, as Muhammad ibn Sirin and 'Amir al-Sha'bi stated, and most scholars followed them in this.

Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi related, and he graded it as hasan, from Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of God ﷺ took as his own the sword Dhu al-Fiqar on the Day of Badr, and it was the sword in which he had seen the vision on the Day of Uhud. [al-Musnad (1/271) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1561.]

From 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, she said: Safiyyah was from the safi (the choice portion). Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2994.]

He also related, with his chain, and al-Nasa'i too, from Yazid ibn 'Abdullah who said: We were at al-Mirbad when a man entered with a piece of leather. We read it, and in it was: "From Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to the Banu Zuhayr ibn Uqaysh: if you bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establish prayer, give zakat, pay the fifth of the spoils, and the share of the Prophet and the share of the safi, then you are secure under the protection of God and His Messenger." We said: Who wrote this for you? He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2994.]

These are good hadiths that indicate this matter is established and confirmed. For this reason, many scholars counted it among the special privileges of the Prophet, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him.

Others said: the fifth is disposed of by the ruler in whatever serves the Muslims, just as he disposes of the fay' property.

Our shaykh, the Imam and great scholar Ibn Taymiyyah, may God have mercy on him, said: This is the view of Malik and most of the earlier scholars, and it is the most correct of the opinions.

Once this is established and known, scholars also differed about what the Prophet ﷺ used to receive from the fifth: what should be done with it after him? Some said: it belongs to whoever governs the affairs after him. This was related from Abu Bakr, 'Ali, and Qatadah, and a group of others, and there is a raised (marfu') hadith about it. [Al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (6/303) through al-Walid ibn Jumay' from Abu al-Tufayl: When Fatimah asked Abu Bakr about the fifth, he said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "When God feeds a prophet a provision and then takes him, it belongs to the one who governs after him." When I took charge, I thought it right to return it to the Muslims.]

Others said: it is spent on the public interests of the Muslims.

Others said: rather, it is returned to the remaining categories: the near kin, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer. This was chosen by Ibn Jarir.

Others said: rather, the share of the Prophet ﷺ and the share of the near kin are returned to the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer.

Ibn Jarir said: This is the view of a group of the people of Iraq.

It was also said: the entire fifth belongs to the near kin, as Ibn Jarir related.

Al-Harith narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, 'Abd al-Ghaffar narrated to us, al-Minhal ibn 'Amr narrated to us, and I asked 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn about the fifth, and they both said: It is ours. I said to 'Ali: But God says: ﴿and the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer﴾. They said: "Our orphans and our needy."

Ibn Kathir's commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 8, verse 41 (part 2 of 2):

Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Nu'aym and Abu Usama related from Qays ibn Muslim, who said: I asked al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, may God have mercy on him, about the words of God the Exalted: ﴿And know that whatever you acquire of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to God and to the Messenger﴾. He said: "This is the key to the matter (miftah kalam), for God's affairs in this world and the Hereafter."

Then people differed about these two shares after the death of the Messenger of God ﷺ. Some said: the share of the Prophet ﷺ goes to the one who succeeds him as caliph. Others said: it goes to the Prophet's relatives (qaraba). Others said: the share of the relatives goes to the relatives of the caliph. Their opinion then converged on using these two shares for horses and equipment in the cause of God, and they remained so during the caliphates of Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both.

Al-A'mash related from Ibrahim, who said: Abu Bakr and 'Umar used to allocate the share of the Prophet ﷺ to horses and weapons. I said to Ibrahim: What did 'Ali say about it? He said: 'Ali (was) the strictest of them concerning it.

This is the view of a large group of scholars, may God have mercy on them.

As for the share of the near kin (dhawi al-qurba), it is given to the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, because the Banu al-Muttalib supported the Banu Hashim in the Jahiliyya [and in the early days of Islam], and entered with them into the Shi'b (the valley of Abu Talib) out of anger for the Messenger of God ﷺ and to protect him. Their Muslims did so in obedience to God and His Messenger, and their disbelievers did so out of tribal loyalty, pride, and obedience to Abu Talib, the uncle of the Messenger of God. As for the Banu 'Abd Shams and the Banu Nawfal, although they were their paternal cousins, they did not agree with them in this; rather they fought against them and broke with them, and they allied with the clans of Quraysh against the Messenger. For this reason, Abu Talib's censure of them in his rhyming qasida (the Lamiyya) was more severe than his censure of others, because of how close they were to him. For this reason he says in the course of his qasida:

May God repay us for 'Abd Shams and Nawfal,
with a swift punishment of evil, not a delayed one,
By a balance of justice that does not cheat the measure,
which has a witness from its own self, not a dependent.
The minds of a people have been made foolish, having exchanged
the sons of Khalaf for us, and the Ghayatil (falsehoods).
We are the pure core of the summit of Hashim,
and the family of Qusayy in the early calamities.

[The verses are in Ibn Hisham's Sira (1/277).]

Jubayr ibn Mut'im ibn 'Adi [ibn Nawfal] said: I and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, meaning the son of Abu al-'As ibn Umayya ibn 'Abd Shams, went to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of God, you gave the Banu al-Muttalib a share of the fifth of Khaybar and left us out, though we and they are in the same position relative to you." He said: "The Banu Hashim and the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib are one and the same thing."

[Narrated by Muslim. (Note: I have not found it in Sahih Muslim, nor did al-Mizzi attribute it to it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf. I do not definitively ascribe the error to the Hafiz here, because al-Zayla'i attributed it to the two Sahihs in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/30). Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih under no. (3140) through the chain of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, may God be pleased with him, in similar wording.] In some versions of this hadith: "They never parted from us in Jahiliyya or in Islam." [Reported in Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/130).]

This is the view of the majority of scholars: that they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: they are the Banu Hashim alone. He then related from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: God knew that among the Banu Hashim there would be poor people, so He assigned them the fifth in place of zakat.

In another report from him he said: They are the relatives of the Messenger of God ﷺ to whom zakat is not permitted.

Then a similar report was related from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: rather, they are all of Quraysh.

Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me: 'Abd Allah ibn Nafi' related to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, who said: Najda wrote to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas asking him about "the near kin," and Ibn 'Abbas wrote back to him: "We used to say: it is us. But our people refused this for us and said: all of Quraysh are kin (dhawu qurba)."

[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/555).]

This hadith is in Sahih Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, through the hadith of Sa'id al-Maqburi from Yazid ibn Hurmuz that Najda wrote to Ibn 'Abbas asking him about the near kin, and he related it up to his words: "But our people refused this for us." [Sahih Muslim no. (1812), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2982), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1556), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/128). It is in Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i through the hadith of al-Zuhri from Yazid.] The addition is from the unique narrations of Abu Ma'shar Najih ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Madani, and there is weakness in him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ibrahim ibn Mahdi al-Misisi related to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from Hanash, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I have preferred for you (to be spared) the washings of hands (from the spoils), because for you there is from the fifth of the fifth what suffices you or is enough for you."

This is a hadith of good chain (hasan al-isnad). Ibrahim ibn Mahdi was declared reliable (thiqa) by Abu Hatim, but Yahya ibn Ma'in said he "brings strange reports" (ya'ti bi-manakir). [See Mizan al-I'tidal of al-Dhahabi (1/68).] And God knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿and the orphans﴾, meaning: the orphans of the Muslims. The scholars differed as to whether this is restricted to poor orphans or includes both rich and poor, on two views.

﴿And the needy (al-masakin)﴾ are the destitute who do not find what would meet their need and humble condition.

﴿And the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil)﴾ is the traveller, or one intending travel, to a distance in which the prayer is shortened, who has nothing to spend on that journey. Its explanation will come in the verse on the alms in Surat Bara'a (al-Tawba), God willing; in Him is trust, and upon Him is reliance.

* *

His words: ﴿If you have believed in God and in what We sent down upon Our servant﴾, meaning: comply with what We have prescribed for you of the fifth in the spoils, if you truly believe in God and the Last Day and in what He sent down to His Messenger. For this reason it is reported in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, in the hadith of the delegation of 'Abd al-Qays, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said to them: "I command you with four and forbid you from four: I command you with faith in God, then he said: Do you know what faith in God is? The testimony that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakat, and that you pay the fifth of the booty..." [the hadith in full]. Thus he made the payment of the fifth part of faith. Al-Bukhari entitled a chapter on this in the Book of Faith of his Sahih, saying: "Chapter: Paying the fifth is part of faith," and then cited this hadith of Ibn 'Abbas. We have expanded on this discussion in our commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari, and to God belongs praise and favour. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (53) and Sahih Muslim no. (17). See also Ibn Hajar's words in Fath al-Bari (1/129-135).]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿And what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of the Criterion (al-Furqan)﴾, meaning: concerning the division (of spoils). His words ﴿on the day the two hosts met, and God is over all things competent﴾ alert to His blessing and His kindness to His creation in that He separated truth from falsehood at Badr. It is called "al-Furqan" because God exalted in it the word of faith over the word of falsehood, manifested His religion, and granted victory to His Prophet and his party.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Day of the Criterion" is the Day of Badr, on which God separated truth from falsehood. Related by al-Hakim.

Likewise said Mujahid, Miqsam, 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, al-Dahhak, Qatada, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others: it is the Day of Badr.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr concerning His words ﴿the Day of the Criterion﴾: the day on which God separated [therein] truth from falsehood, and it is the Day of Badr, the first battle (mashhad) which the Messenger of God ﷺ witnessed. The head of the polytheists was 'Utba ibn Rabi'a. They met on Friday, on the nineteenth or the seventeenth (there is doubt) of Ramadan. The companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ that day were three hundred and some ten men, while the polytheists were between one thousand and nine hundred.

God defeated the polytheists; more than seventy of them were killed, and a similar number were taken captive.

Al-Hakim related in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said concerning the Night of Power: "Seek it on the eleventh of the remaining nights, for its morning is the Day of Badr." And he said: "It is according to their (Bukhari and Muslim's) conditions." [Al-Mustadrak (3/20).]

A similar report was also related from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, through the hadith of Ja'far ibn Burqan, from a man, from him.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd related to us, Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, Yahya ibn Ya'qub Abu Talib related to us, from Ibn 'Awn Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Thaqafi, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali said: "The Night of the Criterion, the day the two hosts met, was the seventeenth night of Ramadan." [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/562)]. This is a good, strong chain.

Ibn Mardawayh related it from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman 'Abd Allah ibn Habib, from 'Ali, who said: "The Night of the Criterion was the night the two hosts met; its morning was the Friday, the seventeenth day that had passed of the month of Ramadan."

This is the sound view according to the people of the military campaigns (maghazi) and biography (siyar).

Yazid ibn Abi Habib, the imam of the people of Egypt in his time, said: "The Day of Badr was a Monday." But this was not followed by anyone, and the view of the majority takes precedence over it. And God knows best.

Allah says, informing about the Day of Criterion (Yawm al-Furqan): ﴿When you were on the nearer side of the valley﴾, that is, when you were encamped on the nearer side of the valley, the one closer to Madinah, ﴿and they were on the farther side﴾, that is, the polytheists were encamped on the far side, the one that is on the Makkan side, ﴿and the caravan was below you﴾, that is, the caravan in which Abu Sufyan was, with what it carried of merchandise, was downstream from you, ﴿toward the coast﴾, that is, on the side of the sea-shore. ﴿Had you made an appointment together, you would have differed about the appointment﴾, that is, you and the polytheists, to a place.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, regarding this verse, saying: Had that been by a prior appointment between you and them, then, when news reached you of their large numbers and your small numbers, you would not have met them. ﴿But that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾, that is, that Allah might accomplish by His power what He willed of exalting Islam and its people and humiliating polytheism and its people, without any gathering from you; so He did what He willed of that by His kindness.

In the hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims set out intending the caravan of Quraysh, until Allah brought them together with their enemy without prior appointment. [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (3951).]

Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub narrated to me, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to me, from Ibn Awn, from Umayr ibn Ishaq, who said: Abu Sufyan came with the caravan from Syria, and Abu Jahl went out to prevent him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions. They met at Badr, neither group aware of the other, until the water-carriers met, and the people advanced upon one another. [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/567).]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in the Sirah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proceeded on his course until, when he was near al-Safra, he sent Basbas ibn Amr and Adi ibn Abi al-Zaghba' al-Juhaniyyan to seek news of Abu Sufyan. They went on until they reached Badr, and made their two camels kneel at a hillock of gravel, and drew water in a waterskin of theirs. They heard two girls quarrelling; one said to her companion: "Pay me my due." The other said: "The caravan is coming tomorrow or the day after, and I will pay you your due." Majdi ibn Amr intervened between them and said: "You have spoken the truth." Basbas and Adi heard that, so they sat on their camels until they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him of the news. Abu Sufyan, when they had turned back, came forward, being wary, ahead of his caravan, and said to Majdi ibn Amr: "Did you sense anyone at this water whom you disliked?" He said: "No, by Allah, except that I saw two riders who made their camels kneel at this hillock, drew water in a waterskin of theirs, then departed." Abu Sufyan came to the place where their camels had knelt, took some of their dung, broke it apart, and found date-stones in it. He said: "By Allah, these are the fodder of Yathrib!" Then he returned quickly, struck the face of his caravan, and set off with it, veering toward the coast; when he saw that he had secured his caravan, he sent to Quraysh saying: "Indeed Allah has saved your caravan, your wealth and your men, so return."

Abu Jahl said: "By Allah, we will not return until we reach Badr—Badr was a market of the Arabs—and remain there three days, slaughter camels there, feed food, give drink of wine, have singing-girls play for us, and the Arabs will hear of us and our march, and they will continue to fear us after that forever."

Al-Akhnas ibn Shariq said: "O assembly of Banu Zuhrah, indeed Allah has saved your wealth and your companion, so return." They obeyed him, and the Banu Zuhrah returned, and they did not witness it, nor did the Banu Adi.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: When he drew near Badr, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ali ibn Abi Talib, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, along with a group of his Companions, to spy out news for him. They captured two water-carriers of Quraysh: a slave of the Banu Sa'id ibn al-As and a slave of the Banu al-Hajjaj. They brought them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was praying. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began asking them: "To whom do you belong?" They said: "We are water-carriers of Quraysh; they sent us to give them water." The people disliked their report and hoped that they belonged to Abu Sufyan, so they beat them. When they were hurt, they said: "We belong to Abu Sufyan." So they left them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed and prostrated twice, then gave the salam and said: "When they tell you the truth you beat them, and when they lie you leave them. They have spoken the truth; by Allah, they are indeed of Quraysh. Tell me about Quraysh." They said: "They are behind this sand-hill you see on the farther side"—and al-Kathib is al-Aqanqal. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "How many are the people?" They said: "Many." He said: "What is their number?" They said: "We do not know." He said: "How many do they slaughter each day?" They said: "One day nine, and one day ten." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people are between nine hundred and a thousand." Then he said to them: "Who among them of the nobles of Quraysh?" They said: "Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham, Hakim ibn Hizam, Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid, al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal, Tu'aymah ibn Adi ibn [Nawfal, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and Umayyah] ibn Khalaf, Nubayh and Munabbih the two sons of al-Hajjaj, Suhayl ibn Amr, and Amr ibn Abd Wudd." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to the people and said: "This is Makkah, which has thrown to you the fruits of its liver." [See the Sirah of Ibn Hisham (1/616).]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm narrated to me that Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the two sides met on the Day of Badr: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not build you a shelter in which you may stay, and make your mounts kneel ready for you, and meet our enemy? If Allah grants us victory over them and honours us, that is what we love. And if the other outcome occurs, you can sit on your mounts and join those behind us of our people. By Allah, groups have stayed behind you who are not more devoted to you than we are; had they known you would face a war, they would not have stayed behind you, and they would love you and support you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ praised him well and prayed good for him. A shelter was built for him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr were in it, with none else beside them. [See the Sirah of Ibn Hisham (1/620).]

Ibn Ishaq said: Quraysh set out in the morning, and when they came forward and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw them descending from al-Aqanqal—which is the sand-hill from which they came down to the valley—he said: "O Allah, these are Quraysh; they have come with their pride and their vanity, opposing You and denying Your Messenger. O Allah, destroy them tomorrow morning." [See the Sirah of Ibn Hisham (1/621).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So that whoever perished might perish upon clear proof, and whoever lived might live upon clear proof﴾, Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: that is, that whoever disbelieved after the proof might disbelieve, having seen the sign and the lesson, and whoever believed might believe on the same basis.

This is a good explanation. Its elaboration is that He, exalted is He, says: He gathered you with your enemy in one place without prior appointment only so that He might grant you victory over them, raise the word of truth above falsehood, so that the matter becomes manifest, the proof decisive, and the evidences radiant, and no one is left with any argument or doubt. Then ﴿whoever perished perishes﴾, that is, whoever persists in disbelief does so with insight into his affair that he is a falsifier, because the proof has been established against him; ﴿and whoever lived lives﴾, that is, whoever believes believes ﴿upon clear proof﴾, that is, with argument and insight. Faith is the life of hearts. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people...﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. And Aisha, in the story of the slander, said: "Concerning me perished whoever perished," meaning: whoever spoke of it of lies, slander and falsehood.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed Allah is All-Hearing﴾, that is, to your supplication, your humility and your appeal to Him, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, that is, of you, and that you deserve victory over your enemies, the disbelieving, stubborn ones.

Mujahid said: Allah showed them to him in his dream as few, and the Prophet ﷺ informed his Companions of that, and it was a source of reassurance for them.

The same was said by Ibn Ishaq and others. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) related from some of them that he saw them with the eye with which he sleeps.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father related to us, Yusuf ibn Musa al-Mudabbir related to us, Abu Qutaybah related to us, from Sahl al-Sarraj, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few﴾, he said: "With your eye."

This statement is strange (gharib), and the dream has been explicitly mentioned here, so there is no need for the interpretation that has no evidence for it.

As for His words ﴿And if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and disputed among yourselves about the matter﴾, meaning: you would have become cowardly toward them and disagreed among yourselves. ﴿But Allah saved [you]﴾, meaning: from that, by showing them to you as few. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: of what the hearts conceal and what the inner parts harbor. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests hide.

* *

As for His words ﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes﴾, this is also from His kindness toward them, for He showed them to them as few in the view of the eye, so that it emboldened them against the enemy and made them eager for them.

Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i related from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "They were made to appear few in our eyes on the Day of Badr, so much so that I said to a man beside me, 'Do you think they are seventy?' He said, 'No, rather they are a hundred.' Then we captured one of them and questioned him, and he said, 'We were a thousand.'" Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir.

* *

As for His words ﴿and He made you appear few in their eyes﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us, Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharit, from Ikrimah regarding ﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes and made you appear few in their eyes﴾: he said, "He urged some of them on against others."

Its chain is sound (isnad sahih).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr related to me, from his father, regarding His words ﴿that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾, meaning: that He might bring about war between them, for the retribution against those He wished to avenge Himself upon, and the bestowal of favor upon those among the people of His allegiance whom He wished to complete His blessing upon.

The meaning of this is that He incited each of the two groups against the other and made each appear few in the eyes of the other, so that each would be eager for the other, and this was at the time of confrontation. When the fighting became intense and Allah supported the believers with a thousand angels following one another, the party of disbelievers continued to see the party of faith as twice their number, as He said: ﴿There has already been for you a sign in two armies which met: one fighting in the way of Allah, and another disbelieving, who saw them [the believers] as twice their number by sight. And Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision﴾ [Al 'Imran: 13]. This is the reconciliation of these two verses, for each of them is true and right, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

This is the teaching of Allah to His believing servants on the etiquette of encounter and the way of courage when facing enemies,[¹] so He said: ﴿O you who believe, when you encounter a company, stand firm﴾.

It is recorded in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn),[²] from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that during some of the days on which he met the enemy, he waited until the sun had declined, then stood among them and said: "O people, do not wish for encounter with the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. But when you meet them, be steadfast, and know that Paradise is under the shade of the swords." Then the Prophet ﷺ stood and said: "O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Mover of the clouds, Defeater of the confederates, defeat them and grant us victory over them."[³]

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Yazid, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not wish for encounter with the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. When you meet them, stand firm, and remember Allah. If they shout and cry out, then keep to silence."[⁴]

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim al-Baghawi narrated to us, Umayya ibn Bistam narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Thabit ibn Zayd narrated to us, from a man, from Zayd ibn Arqam, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah loves silence at three times: at the recitation of the Qur'an, at the battle line (al-zahf), and at the funeral."[⁵]

And in another marfu' hadith, Allah the Exalted says: "Indeed, My servant, every servant of Mine, is one who remembers Me while he is engaged in combat with his opponent,"[⁶] meaning: that situation does not distract him from My remembrance, My supplication, and seeking My help.

Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah said, from Qatadah, concerning this verse: Allah made His remembrance obligatory at the time when you are most occupied, namely at the clash of swords.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: Silence and remembrance become obligatory at the battle line (al-zahf). Then he recited this verse. I said: Should they remember Allah aloud? He said: Yes.

He also said: It was read to Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la: Ibn Wahb informed us, Abdullah ibn Ayyash[⁷] informed me, from Yazid ibn Qawdhar, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, who said: There is nothing more beloved to Allah the Exalted than the recitation of the Qur'an and remembrance. Were it not so, people would not have been commanded to pray and to fight. Do you not see that He commanded people to remember Him at the time of fighting? He said: ﴿O you who believe, when you encounter a company, stand firm, and remember Allah much, that you may succeed﴾.

A poet said: "I remembered you while the spear was moving between us, and the straight-shafted spears had already drunk among us."

And Antarah said: "I remembered you while the lances were shattered among us, and the Indian blades were dripping with my blood. So I wished to kiss the swords, because they gleamed like the flash of your smiling lips."[⁸]

Thus Allah commanded steadfastness when fighting the enemies and patience in facing them, so that they do not flee, do not falter, and do not show cowardice. And that they remember Allah in that state, not forgetting Him, but seeking His help, relying upon Him, and asking Him for victory over their enemies. And that they obey Allah and His Messenger in that state. Whatever Allah the Exalted commanded them, they carried out; whatever He forbade them, they refrained from. And they should not dispute among themselves, lest they differ, which would become a cause of their weakness and failure.

﴿And your strength will depart﴾, meaning: your power, your fervour, and the advantage you had gained. ﴿But be patient; indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾.

The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, excelled in courage and in obeying Allah's commands and following what He guided them to, in a way that no nation or generation before them attained, and none after them will attain. For by the blessing of the Messenger, the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and their obedience to him in what he commanded them, they opened hearts and lands, east and west, in a short period, despite their small number compared to the armies of all other regions: the Romans, Persians, Turks, Slavs, Berbers, Abyssinians, various kinds of Sudanese, Copts, and all the tribes of the sons of Adam. This is the teaching of Allah to His believing servants on the etiquette of encounter and the way of courage when facing enemies,[¹] so He said: ﴿O you who believe, when you encounter a company, stand firm﴾.

It is recorded in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn),[²] from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that during some of the days on which he met the enemy, he waited until the sun had declined, then stood among them and said: "O people, do not wish for encounter with the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. But when you meet them, be steadfast, and know that Paradise is under the shade of the swords." Then the Prophet ﷺ stood and said: "O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Mover of the clouds, Defeater of the confederates, defeat them and grant us victory over them."[³]

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Yazid, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not wish for encounter with the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. When you meet them, stand firm, and remember Allah. If they shout and cry out, then keep to silence."[⁴]

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim al-Baghawi narrated to us, Umayya ibn Bistam narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Thabit ibn Zayd narrated to us, from a man, from Zayd ibn Arqam, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah loves silence at three times: at the recitation of the Qur'an, at the battle line (al-zahf), and at the funeral."[⁵]

And in another marfu' hadith, Allah the Exalted says: "Indeed, My servant, every servant of Mine, is one who remembers Me while he is engaged in combat with his opponent,"[⁶] meaning: that situation does not distract him from My remembrance, My supplication, and seeking My help.

Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah said, from Qatadah, concerning this verse: Allah made His remembrance obligatory at the time when you are most occupied, namely at the clash of swords.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: Silence and remembrance become obligatory at the battle line (al-zahf). Then he recited this verse. I said: Should they remember Allah aloud? He said: Yes.

He also said: It was read to Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la: Ibn Wahb informed us, Abdullah ibn Ayyash[⁷] informed me, from Yazid ibn Qawdhar, from Ka'b al-Ahbar, who said: There is nothing more beloved to Allah the Exalted than the recitation of the Qur'an and remembrance. Were it not so, people would not have been commanded to pray and to fight. Do you not see that He commanded people to remember Him at the time of fighting? He said: ﴿O you who believe, when you encounter a company, stand firm, and remember Allah much, that you may succeed﴾.

A poet said: "I remembered you while the spear was moving between us, and the straight-shafted spears had already drunk among us."

And Antarah said: "I remembered you while the lances were shattered among us, and the Indian blades were dripping with my blood. So I wished to kiss the swords, because they gleamed like the flash of your smiling lips."[⁸]

Thus Allah commanded steadfastness when fighting the enemies and patience in facing them, so that they do not flee, do not falter, and do not show cowardice. And that they remember Allah in that state, not forgetting Him, but seeking His help, relying upon Him, and asking Him for victory over their enemies. And that they obey Allah and His Messenger in that state. Whatever Allah the Exalted commanded them, they carried out; whatever He forbade them, they refrained from. And they should not dispute among themselves, lest they differ, which would become a cause of their weakness and failure.

﴿And your strength will depart﴾, meaning: your power, your fervour, and the advantage you had gained. ﴿But be patient; indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 8, verses 47–49 (part 1 of 2):

Allah says, after commanding the believers to be sincere in fighting in His cause and to remember Him often, forbidding them to imitate the polytheists in their going forth from their homes ﴿insolently﴾, meaning rejecting the truth, ﴿and to be seen by people﴾, which is boasting and arrogance toward them, as Abu Jahl said when it was said to him: "The caravan has escaped, so return." He said: "No, by Allah, we will not return until we reach the water of Badr, slaughter camels, drink wine, have singing girls play for us, and the Arabs will speak of our presence there forever." But this was reversed upon him entirely, for when they reached the water of Badr they were brought to it by death, and they were thrown into the wells of Badr humiliated, abased, wretched, and damned, in a perpetual, everlasting punishment. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾, meaning He is knowing of what they came with and for what purpose, and for this He repaid them with the worst of recompense.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said concerning His words, ﴿And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people﴾: they are the polytheists who fought the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Badr.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: When Quraysh went out from Makkah to Badr, they went out with singing girls and tambourines, so Allah revealed: ﴿And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people, and who averted [others] from the way of Allah; and Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿And [mention] when Satan made their deeds attractive to them and said, "No one among the people can overcome you today, and indeed I am your protector."﴾ (the verse): he beautified for them, may Allah curse him, what they had come for and what they had intended, and he made them hope that no one among the people could overcome them that day, and he removed from them the fear that they might be attacked in their homes by their enemy, the Banu Bakr, so he said: "I am your protector." This was because he appeared to them in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum, chief of the Banu Mudlij, the greatest man of that region. All of this came from him, as Allah the Exalted said about him: ﴿He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ [An-Nisa: 120]

Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said concerning this verse: When the day of Badr came, Iblis marched with his banner and his troops alongside the polytheists, and he cast into the hearts of the polytheists that no one would defeat them, and [said], "I am your protector." But when the two groups met and Satan saw the reinforcement of the angels, ﴿he turned back on his heels﴾; he said: he retreated fleeing, and he said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾ (the verse).

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Iblis came on the day of Badr with a host of devils, with his banner, in the form of a man from the Banu Mudlij, and Satan was in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Mudlaji. Satan said to the polytheists: ﴿No one among the people can overcome you today, and indeed I am your protector.﴾ When the people lined up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a handful of dust and threw it into the faces of the polytheists, and they turned their backs in flight. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to Iblis, and when he saw him—his hand was in the hand of a man among the polytheists—he pulled his hand away and turned back fleeing, he and his party. The man said: "O Suraqah, do you claim that you are our protector?" He said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ That was when he saw the angels.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: al-Kalbi related to me from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Iblis went out with Quraysh in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum. When the fighting came and he saw the angels, he turned back on his heels and said: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you﴾, and al-Harith ibn Hisham seized him, and he struck him in the face and he fell down unconscious. It was said to him: "Woe to you, O Suraqah! In this state you abandon us and disown us?" He said: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Waqidi said: 'Umar ibn 'Uqbah informed me, from Shu'bah, the freed slave of Ibn 'Abbas, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: When the two sides came face to face, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fainted for a moment, then he regained consciousness, and he gave the people good news of Jibril with a host of angels on the right wing of the people, and Mika'il with another host on the left wing of the people, and Israfil with another host of a thousand. Iblis had taken the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Mudlaji, managing the polytheists and informing them that no one would defeat them that day. When the enemy of Allah saw the angels, he turned back on his heels and said: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see.﴾ Al-Harith ibn Hisham seized him, thinking he was Suraqah because of what he had heard of his speech, so he struck al-Harith in the chest, and al-Harith fell, and Iblis set off fleeing, unseen, until he fell into the sea, and he raised his garment and said: "O Lord, [this is] Your promise which You made to me."

In al-Tabarani, from Rifa'ah ibn Rafi', there is something close to this narration and more extensive than it, which we have mentioned in the Sirah.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq also said: Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: When Quraysh resolved to march, they recalled the war that was between them and the Banu Bakr, and that nearly dissuaded them. Then Iblis appeared to them in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Mudlaji—and he was one of the nobles of the Banu Kinanah—and said: "I am your protector that Kinanah will not bring you anything you dislike." So they set out swiftly.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It was related to me that they used to see him at every station in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik, and they did not deny him, until the day of Badr when the two hosts met. The one who saw him when he turned back was al-Harith ibn Hisham—or 'Umayr ibn Wahb—and he said: "Where, where, O Suraqah?" The enemy of Allah vanished and went away. He said: "He led them and then abandoned them." He said: The enemy of Allah saw the hosts of Allah, with which Allah had strengthened His Messenger and the believers, so he turned back on his heels and said: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see.﴾ The enemy of Allah spoke truly, and he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ This is likewise narrated from al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan al-Basri, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others, may Allah have mercy on them.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that he saw Jibril (peace be upon him) descending with the angels, and the enemy of Allah knew that he had no strength against the angels, so he said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah.﴾ The enemy of Allah lied; by Allah, there was no fear of Allah in him, but he knew that he had no power and no protection, and that is the habit of the enemy of Allah toward whoever obeys him and follows him, until when truth and falsehood meet he hands them over to the worst handing-over, and disowns them at that point.

I say: By his habit toward whoever obeys him, he means His words, the Exalted: ﴿Like the example of Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, [Satan] says, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Al-Hashr: 16], and His words, the Exalted: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot be your helper, nor can you be my helper. Indeed, I disbelieved in what you associated [me] with before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment."﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]

Yunus ibn Bukayr said, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq: al-Harith ibn Abi Bakr ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm related to me, from some of the Banu Sa'idah, who said: I heard Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabi'ah, after his sight had been taken away, say: "If I were with you now at Badr and my sight were with me, I would have shown you the ravine from which the angels emerged, without doubt and without disputing."

When the angels descended and Iblis saw them, and Allah revealed to them: "I am with you, so strengthen those who believe," their strengthening was that the angels would come to a man in the form of a man he knew, and say to him: "Rejoice, for they are nothing, and Allah is with you; charge against them." When Iblis saw the angels, he turned back on his heels and said: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see.﴾ He was in the form of Suraqah. Abu Jahl came forward urging his companions and saying: "Let not the abandonment by Suraqah of you terrify you, for he had an agreement with Muhammad and his companions." Then he said: "By al-Lat and al-'Uzza, we will not return until we tie Muhammad and his companions in ropes; do not kill them, but take them captive." This statement from Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him, is like the words of Pharaoh to the magicians when they had believed: ﴿Indeed, this is a plot you have plotted in the city to expel its people from it﴾ [Al-A'raf: 123], and like his words ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71]; it is of the category of slander and fabrication, and for this reason Abu Jahl was the Pharaoh of this Ummah.

Malik ibn Anas said, from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah, from Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Kurayz, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Iblis was never seen on a day in which he is more humiliated, more despised, more repelled, or more enraged than on the Day of 'Arafah, and that is because of what he sees of the descent of mercy and the forgiveness of sins. Except for what he saw on the day of Badr." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what did he see on the day of Badr?" He said: "Indeed, he saw Jibril (peace be upon him) marshaling the angels."

This is a mursal narration by this route.

* *

As for His words: ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say, "Their religion has deluded these"﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse, who said: When the two groups drew near to one another, Allah made the Muslims seem few in the eyes of the polytheists and made the polytheists seem few in the eyes of the Muslims, so the polytheists said: ﴿Their religion has deluded these﴾, and they said that only because of their fewness in their eyes; they thought they would defeat them, having no doubt of that. Then Allah said: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah—indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise.﴾

Qatadah said: They saw a band of believers who were resolute in obedience to Allah's command. It was mentioned to us that when Abu Jahl, the enemy of Allah, looked down upon Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, he said: "By Allah, they will not worship Allah after today," out of harshness and insolence.

Ibn Jurayj said concerning His words: ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say﴾: they were a group of hypocrites in Makkah, and they said this on the day of Badr.

'Amir al-Sha'bi said: Some people of Makkah had professed Islam, then they went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr, and when they saw the small number of the Muslims they said: ﴿Their religion has deluded these.﴾

Mujahid said, regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say, "These people have been deluded by their religion"﴾. He said: A group from Quraysh: [Abu] Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abu Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughira, al-Harith ibn Zam'a ibn al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, Ali ibn Umayya ibn Khalaf, and al-As ibn Munabbih ibn al-Hajjaj. They went out with Quraysh from Makkah while they were in doubt, and their doubt held them back. When they saw the small number of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they said, ﴿These people have been deluded by their religion﴾, until they arrived at what they arrived at, along with the smallness of their own number and the greatness of their enemy.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said the same thing, identically.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding this verse, he said: They are people who did not witness the fighting on the day of Badr, so they were named hypocrites. Ma'mar said: Some of them said: They are people who had professed Islam while they were in Makkah, then they went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr, and when they saw the small number of the Muslims they said, ﴿These people have been deluded by their religion﴾.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah﴾, meaning: whoever depends upon His protection, ﴿then indeed Allah is Almighty﴾, meaning: He is not wronged, whoever seeks refuge in Him, for indeed Allah is Almighty, of inviolable protection, of great authority, All-Wise in His actions, placing them only in their proper places. He gives victory to whoever deserves victory, and forsakes whoever is worthy of being forsaken.

The one who saw him when he turned back was al-Harith ibn Hisham—or 'Umayr ibn Wahb—and he said: "Where, where, O Suraqah?" The enemy of Allah vanished and went away. He said: "He led them and then abandoned them." He said: The enemy of Allah saw the hosts of Allah, with which Allah had strengthened His Messenger and the believers, so he turned back on his heels and said: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see.﴾ The enemy of Allah spoke truly, and he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ This is likewise narrated from al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan al-Basri, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others, may Allah have mercy on them.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that he saw Jibril (peace be upon him) descending with the angels, and the enemy of Allah knew that he had no strength against the angels, so he said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah.﴾ The enemy of Allah lied; by Allah, there was no fear of Allah in him, but he knew that he had no power and no protection, and that is the habit of the enemy of Allah toward whoever obeys him and follows him, until when truth and falsehood meet he hands them over to the worst handing-over, and disowns them at that point.

I say: By his habit toward whoever obeys him, he means His words, the Exalted: ﴿Like the example of Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, [Satan] says, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Al-Hashr: 16], and His words, the Exalted: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot be your helper, nor can you be my helper. Indeed, I disbelieved in what you associated [me] with before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment."﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]

When the angels descended and Iblis saw them, and Allah revealed to them: "I am with you, so strengthen those who believe," their strengthening was that the angels would come to a man in the form of a man he knew, and say to him: "Rejoice, for they are nothing, and Allah is with you; charge against them." When Iblis saw the angels, he turned back on his heels and said: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see.﴾ He was in the form of Suraqah. Abu Jahl came forward urging his companions and saying: "Let not the abandonment by Suraqah of you terrify you, for he had an agreement with Muhammad and his companions." Then he said: "By al-Lat and al-'Uzza, we will not return until we tie Muhammad and his companions in ropes; do not kill them, but take them captive." This is a mursal narration by this route.

Then Allah said: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah—indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise.﴾

They went out with Quraysh from Makkah while they were in doubt, and their doubt held them back. When they saw the small number of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they said, ﴿These people have been deluded by their religion﴾, until they arrived at what they arrived at, along with the smallness of their own number and the greatness of their enemy.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said the same thing, identically.

He gives victory to whoever deserves victory, and forsakes whoever is worthy of being forsaken.

Allah says, after commanding the believers to be sincere in fighting in His cause and to remember Him often, forbidding them to imitate the polytheists in their going forth from their homes ﴿insolently﴾, meaning rejecting the truth, ﴿and to be seen by people﴾, which is boasting and arrogance toward them, as Abu Jahl said when it was said to him: "The caravan has escaped, so return." He said: "No, by Allah, we will not return until we reach the water of Badr, slaughter camels, drink wine, have singing girls play for us, and the Arabs will speak of our presence there forever." But this was reversed upon him entirely, for when they reached the water of Badr they were brought to it by death, and they were thrown into the wells of Badr humiliated, abased, wretched, and damned, in a perpetual, everlasting punishment. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾, meaning He is knowing of what they came with and for what purpose, and for this He repaid them with the worst of recompense.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said concerning His words, ﴿And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people﴾: they are the polytheists who fought the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Badr.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: When Quraysh went out from Makkah to Badr, they went out with singing girls and tambourines, so Allah revealed: ﴿And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people, and who averted [others] from the way of Allah; and Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾

This was because he appeared to them in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum, chief of the Banu Mudlij, the greatest man of that region. All of this came from him, as Allah the Exalted said about him: ﴿He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ [An-Nisa: 120]

Satan said to the polytheists: ﴿No one among the people can overcome you today, and indeed I am your protector.﴾ When the people lined up, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a handful of dust and threw it into the faces of the polytheists, and they turned their backs in flight. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ That was when he saw the angels.

It was said to him: "Woe to you, O Suraqah! In this state you abandon us and disown us?" He said: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

When the enemy of Allah saw the angels, he turned back on his heels and said: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see.﴾ Al-Harith ibn Hisham seized him, thinking he was Suraqah because of what he had heard of his speech, so he struck al-Harith in the chest, and al-Harith fell, and Iblis set off fleeing, unseen, until he fell into the sea, and he raised his garment and said: "O Lord, [this is] Your promise which You made to me."

Ibn Jurayj related from Mujahid: "﴿And their backs﴾ means their posteriors," and he said, "on the day of Badr."

O My servants, these are only your deeds which I record for you; so whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2577]. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said:

Allah the Exalted says: These polytheists, who deny, did to what you have been sent with, O Muhammad, as the denying nations before them did. So We dealt with them as is Our custom (da'b), that is, Our habit and practice (sunnah) regarding their like among the deniers: the people of Pharaoh and those before them of the denying nations who denied the messengers and disbelieved in the signs of Allah.

﴿So Allah seized them for their sins⟩ [i.e., He destroyed them because of their sins; He seized them with the seizing of the Mighty, the All-Powerful] ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong and severe in punishment⟩, that is, no conqueror can overcome Him, and no fugitive can escape Him.

Ibn Kathir says: He, the Exalted, informs us of the perfection of His justice and equity in His judgment, that He, the Exalted, does not change a blessing He has bestowed upon anyone [[In A: "a people".]] except because of a sin that he has committed, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah wills misfortune for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector other than Him.﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 11]

His saying ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾ means: like His treatment of the people of Pharaoh and those like them, when they denied His signs. He destroyed them because of their sins, and stripped them of those blessings He had bestowed upon them: gardens and springs, crops and treasures, a noble station, and a bounty in which they used to take delight. Allah did not wrong them in that; rather, they were the wrongdoers.

And when Allah wills misfortune for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector other than Him.﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 11]

He destroyed them because of their sins, and stripped them of those blessings He had bestowed upon them: gardens and springs, crops and treasures, a noble station, and a bounty in which they used to take delight. Allah did not wrong them in that; rather, they were the wrongdoers.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, the Exalted, informed that the worst of the creatures that crawl upon the face of the earth are those who disbelieve, so they do not believe. They are the ones who, whenever they make a covenant, break it, and whenever they confirm it with oaths, they violate it. ﴿And they do not fear (Allah)﴾, i.e., they do not fear Allah regarding any sin they commit.

﴿So if you gain the upper hand over them in war﴾, i.e., you overcome them and prevail over them in battle, ﴿then deal with them severely so that those behind them may be scattered﴾, i.e., make an example of them. This was said by Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Ata al-Khurasani, and Ibn Uyaynah. Its meaning is: make their punishment severe and inflict heavy slaughter upon them, so that whoever else among the enemies, from the Arabs and others, will fear them and they become a lesson for them, ﴿so that they may take heed﴾.

Al-Suddi said: It means, "so that they may be cautious lest they break (their covenants), and so that what was done to them is done to them (again)."
