God, the Exalted, says to His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people﴾ with whom you have made a covenant [[In A: "may Allah bless him and grant him peace."]] ﴿treachery﴾, meaning a breach of the pacts and covenants between you and them. ﴿Then throw back to them﴾, meaning their covenant, ﴿on equal terms﴾, meaning: inform them that you have annulled their covenant, so that both your knowledge and theirs is that you are at war with them and they are at war with you, and that there is no covenant between you and them. "On equal terms" means that you and they are equal in this. The rajaz poet said: "So strike the faces of the treacherous [enemies] [[Addition from D, M, A, and al-Tabari.]] until they answer you on equal terms." [[The rajaz verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (14/27).]]

It is related from al-Walid ibn Muslim that he said concerning His words ﴿Then throw back to them on equal terms﴾: it means "in a measured way." ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous﴾ means that even with regard to the disbelievers, He does not love this either.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah [[In K: "Sa'id."]] narrated to us from Abu al-Faydh, from Sulaym ibn 'Amir, who said: Mu'awiyah was marching in the land of the Romans, and there was a term [of truce] between him and them. He wanted to draw near to them, so that when the term ended he could attack them. Then he saw an old man on a mount saying: "Allah is greatest! Allah is greatest! [[Addition from D, K, M, and the Musnad.]] [Fulfil] the covenant, not betray it! Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever has a covenant between himself and a people, let him not loosen its knot or tie it until its term has ended, or he throws it back to them on equal terms.'" He said: Mu'awiyah received word of this and turned back, and the old man was 'Amr ibn 'Abasah, may Allah be pleased with him.

This hadith was transmitted by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi from Shu'bah. It was also recorded by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, through various chains from Shu'bah, with the same wording. [[Musnad Ahmad (4/111); Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (1155); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2759); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1580); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (8732).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Zubayri narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Salman, meaning al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him: that he came to a fortress, or a city, and said to his companions: "Leave me to call them as I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ call them." [[In D, K: "the Prophet."]] So he said: "I was only a man from among them [[In D, K, M: "from among you."]], and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, guided me to Islam. If you embrace Islam, you will have what we have and bear what we bear. If you refuse, then pay the jizyah (poll tax) while you are humbled. If you refuse, we will throw back to you [the covenant] on equal terms. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous﴾." They continued doing this for three days. When the fourth day came, the people went out to it and conquered it by the help of Allah. [[Musnad (5/440). Al-Tirmidhi related it in al-Sunan, no. (1548), through the route of Abu 'Awanah, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Bakhtari, similarly, and said: "The hadith of Salman is hasan, and we do not know it except from the hadith of 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib. I heard Muhammad [al-Bukhari] say: Abu al-Bakhtari did not meet Salman, because he did not meet 'Ali, and Salman died before 'Ali."]]

Allah says to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that they have escaped﴾, O Muhammad. That is, they will not be beyond our reach and we cannot seize them; rather, they are under the subjugation of our power and in the grip of our will, so they cannot escape us. As Allah says: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outstrip Us? Evil is what they judge﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 4], that is, what they suppose. And Allah says: ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think that they can escape [Allah] in the land; their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾ [al-Nur: 57]. And Allah says: ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the land deceive you. It is but brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Al 'Imran: 196-197].

Then Allah commands the preparation of the implements of war to fight them, according to one's capacity, ability and power. He says: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾, that is, whatever you are able to do, ﴿and of steeds of war (ribat al-khail)﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu 'Ali Thumamah ibn Shufayy, that he heard 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say while on the minbar: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾. "Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery."

Related by Muslim from Harun ibn Ma'ruf, and Abu Dawud from Sa'id ibn Mansur, and Ibn Majah from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la; all three from 'Abdullah ibn Wahb, with it.

There are other chains for this hadith from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir. Among them is what al-Tirmidhi related from the hadith of Salih ibn Kaysan, from a man, from him. [al-Tirmidhi said: "Salih ibn Kaysan did not meet 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, though he met Ibn 'Umar."]

Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan related from him that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shoot and ride, and that you shoot is better than that you ride."

Imam Malik said, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih al-Sammān, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Horses are of three kinds: for a man, a reward; for a man, a covering; and for a man, a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward, it is a man who tethers it in the way of Allah, and lengthens its tether in a meadow or garden. Whatever it eats from that meadow or garden in its tether is recorded as good deeds for him. And if it breaks its tether and goes a stride or two, its traces and dung are good deeds for him. And if it passes by a river and drinks from it, without its owner intending to water it, that too is recorded as good deeds for him. So for that man it is a reward. And a man who tethers it out of self-sufficiency and restraint, not forgetting Allah's right in its necks and backs, it is for him a covering. And a man who tethers it for pride, showing off and enmity, it is for him a burden." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about donkeys, and he said: "Allah has revealed nothing concerning them to me except this comprehensive, unique verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7-8]."

Related by al-Bukhari, and this is his wording, and Muslim, both from the hadith of Malik. [al-Muwatta' (2/414), and from its route al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih, no. 2371. Muslim related it through the route of Hafs ibn Maysarah from Zayd ibn Aslam from Abu Salih, no. 987.]

Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, Shurayk informed us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi', from al-Qasim ibn Hassan, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Horses are of three kinds: a horse for the Most Merciful, a horse for the Devil, and a horse for the human being. As for the horse of the Most Merciful, it is the one tethered in the way of Allah; its fodder, dung and urine [are rewarded], and he mentioned what Allah willed. As for the horse of the Devil, it is the one wagered upon or bet upon. As for the horse of the human being, it is the horse a man keeps seeking its belly (i.e., its offspring), and it is a covering from poverty."

Most scholars hold that archery is superior to riding horses, while Imam Malik held that riding is superior to archery. The view of the majority is stronger due to the hadith, and Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj and Hisham narrated to us, both saying: Layth narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib informed me, from Ibn Shumasah, that Mu'awiyah ibn Hudayj passed by Abu Dharr while he was standing by a horse of his, and he asked him: "What do you do with this horse of yours?" He said: "I think this horse has had its supplication answered!" He said: "And what is the supplication of a beast among the beasts?" He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, there is no horse but that it supplicates every dawn, saying: 'O Allah, You have made me subject to a servant of Your servants, and made my provision in his hand. So make me more beloved to him than his family and his wealth and his children.'"

He said: And Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, who narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Suwayd ibn Qays, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hudayj, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no Arabian horse but that it is permitted with every dawn to supplicate with two supplications, saying: 'O Allah, You have made me subject to those among the children of Adam whom You have made subject to me, so make me among the most beloved of his family and his wealth to him'" or "the most beloved of his family and his wealth to him."

Related by al-Nasa'i, from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from Yahya al-Qattan, with it. [al-Musnad (5/170) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/223).]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tustari narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to us, al-Mut'im ibn al-Miqdam al-San'ani narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, that he said to Ibn al-Handhaliyyah (meaning Sahl): "Narrate to us a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Good is bound to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection, and their people are helped with them; and whoever ties a horse in the way of Allah, its expenses are upon him, like one who extends his hand with charity that never takes it back.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/98).]

The hadiths about the virtue of tethering horses are many. In Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Urwah ibn Abi al-Ja'd al-Bariqi, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Good is bound to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection: reward and spoils." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2850.]

As for His saying: ﴿you may terrify thereby the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿and others besides them﴾. Mujahid said: they are Qurayzah. al-Suddi said: they are Persia. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Ibn Yaman said: they are the devils who are in the houses. A hadith with similar meaning has been narrated. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu 'Utbah Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Himsi narrated to us, Abu Haywah, meaning Shurayh ibn Yazid al-Muqri', narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Ibn 'Arib, meaning Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Arib, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say concerning His saying: ﴿and others besides them whom you do not know﴾, "They are the jinn."

Al-Tabarani related it from Ibrahim ibn Duhaym, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Sa'id ibn Sinan, from Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Urayb, with it, and he added: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No house in which there is a noble horse is afflicted with madness (yukhbal)." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/188).]

This hadith is munkar; its chain is not sound and its text is not sound.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are the hypocrites.

This is the most similar of the opinions, and his saying supports it: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become adept at hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 101].

Sufyan al-Thawri said: Ibn Yaman said: they are the devils who are in the houses. A hadith with similar meaning has been narrated. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu 'Utbah Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Himsi narrated to us, Abu Haywah, meaning Shurayh ibn Yazid al-Muqri', narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Ibn 'Arib, meaning Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Arib, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say concerning His saying: ﴿and others besides them whom you do not know﴾, "They are the jinn."

Al-Tabarani related it from Ibrahim ibn Duhaym, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Sa'id ibn Sinan, from Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Urayb, with it, and he added: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No house in which there is a noble horse is afflicted with madness (yukhbal)." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/188).]

This hadith is munkar; its chain is not sound and its text is not sound.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: they are the hypocrites.

This is the most similar of the opinions, and his saying supports it: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become adept at hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 101].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾, that is, whatever you spend in jihad, it will be repaid to you in full and completely. For this reason, a hadith related by Abu Dawud came: that the dirham's reward is multiplied in the way of Allah up to seven hundred times. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2498, with the wording: "Indeed prayer, fasting and remembrance are multiplied over spending in the way of Allah by seven hundred times." A similar wording has already preceded at the commentary of verse 261 of Surat al-Baqarah from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn.] As mentioned in His saying: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from his father, al-Ash'ath ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet ﷺ used to command that charity be given only to the people of Islam, until ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be repaid to you﴾ was revealed, and after it he commanded charity to be given to everyone who asks you, of every religion. This too is gharib.

Allah says: "If you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them their covenant on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous." If they persist in waging war against you and in breaking the truce, then fight them. ﴿And if they incline﴾, meaning they turn away, ﴿to peace﴾, meaning to reconciliation, settlement and truce, ﴿then incline to it﴾, meaning turn toward it and accept that from them. For this reason, when the polytheists asked for a peace treaty at al-Hudaybiyah and for the cessation of fighting between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for ten years, he agreed to that, along with the other conditions they stipulated.

Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad narrated: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Sulayman (i.e., al-Numayri) narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Yahya narrated to us, from Iyas ibn Amr al-Aslami, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, there will occur after me a disagreement, or a matter; so if you are able that there be peace, then do it." [Zawa'id al-Musnad (1/90); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/234): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]

Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning the Banu Qurayzah.

This is open to question, because the whole context concerns the Battle of Badr, and its mention surrounds all of this.

The view of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Zayd ibn Aslam, Ata al-Khurasani, Ikrimah, al-Hasan and Qatadah is that this verse is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of the sword in Bara'ah: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29]. This also is open to question, because the verse of Bara'ah contains the command to fight them when that is possible. But when the enemy is numerous, it is permissible to make a truce with them, as this noble verse indicates, and as the Prophet (ﷺ) did on the day of al-Hudaybiyah. So there is no contradiction, no abrogation, and no specification. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And put your trust in Allah﴾, meaning: make peace with them and trust in Allah, for Allah is sufficient for you and your helper, even if they intended by the peace a deception so that they might strengthen themselves and prepare. ﴿Indeed, Allah is sufficient for you﴾, meaning He alone is sufficient for you.

Then He mentioned His favour upon him by what He strengthened him with of the believers, the Emigrants and the Helpers, saying: ﴿It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers, and joined their hearts together﴾, meaning united them upon faith in you, obedience to you, and support and assistance for you. ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts together﴾, meaning because of the enmity and hatred that existed between them. The Helpers had many wars between them in the Jahiliyyah, between the Aws and the Khazraj, and matters that led to an endless cycle of evil, until Allah cut that off with the light of faith, as He said: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He joined your hearts, so you became by His favour brothers; and you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be guided﴾ [Al 'Imran: 103].

In the Two Sahihs, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed the Helpers concerning the spoils of Hunayn, he said to them: "O assembly of the Helpers, did I not find you astray and Allah guided you through me, in need and Allah enriched you through me, and you were divided and Allah united you through me?" Whenever he said something, they replied: "Allah and His Messenger are most gracious." [Sahih al-Bukhari (4330) and Sahih Muslim (1061), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Yazid ibn Asim, may Allah be pleased with him.]

For this reason Allah said: ﴿But Allah joined them together. Indeed, He is Almighty, All-Wise﴾, meaning: Almighty in His dominion, so He does not disappoint the hope of one who relies upon Him; All-Wise in His actions and His rulings.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Ali ibn Bishr al-Sayrafi al-Qazwini informed us in our house, Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Hasan [in all copies "al-Husayn", and the correction is from al-Shu'ab and al-Mizan] al-Qindili al-Istarabadhi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Saffar narrated to us, Maymun ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, Bakr ibn al-Sharud narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas who said: "The ties of kinship are severed, the obligation of a favour is denied, and no one has seen the like of the closeness of hearts; Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts together﴾." And this is found in poetry:

"When a close relative dies in your regard, having deceived you, and became self-sufficient, he is no longer a kinsman.

But the close relative is one who, if you call him, responds, and one who shoots at the enemy you shoot at."

He said: Among that is the saying of the poet:

"I have accompanied people, then tested them, and tried what means of connection they had,

So kinship does not bring close one who severs, and affection is the nearest of means."

Al-Bayhaqi said: I do not know whether this is connected to the words of Ibn Abbas, or whether it is the saying of one of the narrators below him. [Shu'ab al-Iman of al-Bayhaqi (9034).]

Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i said, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that I heard him say: ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts together﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: "They are those who love one another for the sake of Allah." In another narration: "It was revealed concerning those who love one another for the sake of Allah."

Narrated by al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and he said: Sahih. [al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11210) and al-Mustadrak (2/329).]

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas who said: "Indeed the ties of kinship are severed, and indeed the favour is denied, and indeed when Allah brings hearts close together, nothing can move them apart." Then he recited: ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts together﴾.

Narrated by al-Hakim also.

Abu Amr al-Awza'i said: Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah narrated to me, from Mujahid — and I met him, and he took my hand and said: "When two loving ones for the sake of Allah meet, and one of them takes the hand of his companion and smiles at him, their sins fall away like the leaves of a tree." Abdah said: I said to him: "Indeed this is trivial!" He said: "Do not say that, for Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts together﴾!" Abdah said: I knew that he was more learned than I.

[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/46).]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us [in H: "Abu Yaman"; corrected from D, K, M and al-Tabari], from Ibrahim al-Khuzi [in D, K: "al-Jazari"], from al-Walid ibn Abi Mughith, from Mujahid, who said: "When two Muslims meet and shake hands, they are forgiven." I said to Mujahid: "Are they forgiven by a handshake?" Mujahid said: "Have you not heard Him say: ﴿Had you spent everything on earth, you could not have joined their hearts together, but Allah joined them﴾?" Al-Walid said to Mujahid: "You are more knowledgeable than I."

Similarly Talhah ibn Musarrif narrated from Mujahid.

Ibn Awn said, from Umayr ibn Ishaq: "We used to hear that the first thing to be lifted from people is harmony (al-ulfah)."

Abu al-Qasim Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Tabarani, may Allah have mercy on him, said: al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tustari narrated to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us, Salim ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, I heard Ja'd Abu Uthman, Abu Uthman al-Nahdi narrated to me, from Salman al-Farisi: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a Muslim meets his Muslim brother and takes his hand, their sins fall from them as leaves fall from a dry tree on a day of violent wind; and otherwise they are forgiven, even if their sins were like the foam of the seas." [in D, K, A: "al-bahr"] [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/256), where it reads "like the foam of the sea"; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/37): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Salim ibn Ghaylan, who is trustworthy."]

Al-Walid said to Mujahid: "You are more knowledgeable than I."

Similarly Talhah ibn Musarrif narrated from Mujahid.

Ibn Awn said, from Umayr ibn Ishaq: "We used to hear that the first thing to be lifted from people is harmony (al-ulfah)."

Abu al-Qasim Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Tabarani, may Allah have mercy on him, said: al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tustari narrated to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us, Salim ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, I heard Ja'd Abu Uthman, Abu Uthman al-Nahdi narrated to me, from Salman al-Farisi: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a Muslim meets his Muslim brother and takes his hand, their sins fall from them as leaves fall from a dry tree on a day of violent wind; and otherwise they are forgiven, even if their sins were like the foam of the seas." [in D, K, A: "al-bahr"] [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/256), where it reads "like the foam of the sea"; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/37): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Salim ibn Ghaylan, who is trustworthy."]

Allah urges His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and the believers to fight, to engage the enemy in combat, and to face their equals in single combat. He informs them that He is sufficient for them, meaning that He will suffice them, support them, and strengthen them against their enemy, even if their enemies are numerous and their reinforcements continuous, and even if the number of believers is small.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Hakim related to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Shu'dhab [in H and K: "from Ibn Shu'dhab"; the text as established from M, A and al-Tabari], from al-Sha'bi, concerning His words: ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you, and [for] those believers who follow you﴾ he said: "Allah is sufficient for you, and sufficient for those who witnessed [the battle] with you."

He said: It is also narrated from Ata al-Khurasani and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd [ibn Aslam] [addition from A] something similar.

Therefore He said: ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight﴾, meaning: exhort them and incite them to it. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to urge them to fight when they lined up in rows and confronted the enemy, as he said to his Companions on the Day of Badr, when the polytheists approached in their number and their equipment: "Rise up to a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth." Umayr ibn al-Hummam said: "The heavens and the earth?!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes." He said: "Bakh, bakh!" He said: "What prompts you to say 'bakh, bakh'?" He said: "Hoping that I may be one of its people!" He said: "Indeed, you are one of its people." So the man advanced, broke the sheath of his sword, took out some dates and began eating from them. Then he threw away what remained of them from his hand and said: "If I live until I eat them, that would be a long life!" Then he advanced and fought until he was killed, may Allah be pleased with him. [Footnote: Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1901), from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

It has also been narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that this verse was revealed when Umar ibn al-Khattab embraced Islam, and with him the number of men [who had embraced Islam] was completed to forty.

But this requires consideration, because this verse is Madinan, and Umar's conversion took place in Makkah, after the migration to the land of Abyssinia and before the migration to Madinah. And Allah knows best.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, giving glad tidings to the believers and issuing a command: ﴿If there are twenty among you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred among you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieved﴾, each one [to face] ten [of the enemy]. Then this command was abrogated (naskh), while the glad tidings remained.

Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: Jarir ibn Hazim related to us, saying: al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharrit related to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse was revealed: ﴿If there are twenty among you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾, it weighed heavily on the Muslims when Allah made it obligatory upon them that not one of them should flee from ten [of the enemy]. Then relief came, and He said: ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you﴾ up to His words: ﴿they will overcome two hundred﴾. He said: Allah lightened it for them in terms of the number [of enemies to be faced], and reduced the steadfastness required by the same measure by which He lightened it for them.

Al-Bukhari narrated something similar from the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4653).]

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Sufyan related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse, that he said: It was prescribed for them that twenty should not flee from two hundred. Then Allah lightened it for them, saying: ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you, and He knows that among you there is weakness﴾. So it is not proper for a hundred to flee from two hundred.

Al-Bukhari narrated, from Ali ibn Abd Allah, from Sufyan, with the same chain, something similar. [Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4652).]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Ibn Abi Najih related to me, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they considered it great that twenty should fight two hundred, and a hundred [fight] a thousand. So Allah lightened it for them and abrogated it with the other verse, saying: ﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you, and He knows that among you there is weakness﴾, and so forth. Thus, when they were at half the number of their enemy, it was not proper for them to flee from their enemy; and when they were fewer than that, fighting them was not obligatory upon them, and it was permissible for them to withdraw from them.

Ali ibn Abi Talha and al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas something similar to that.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is also narrated from Mujahid, Ata, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Zayd ibn Aslam, Ata al-Khurasani, and al-Dahhak something similar to that.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh related, from the hadith of al-Musayyib ibn Sharik, from Ibn Awn, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, concerning ﴿If there are twenty among you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾, that he said: It was revealed concerning us, the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Then he said: Its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it. [Footnote: al-Mustadrak (2/239).]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verses 67–69:

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted the people about the captives on the day of Badr, and said: "Indeed Allah has granted you power over them." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, strike their necks." The Prophet ﷺ turned away from him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned and said: "O people, indeed Allah has granted you power over them, and they are only your brothers of yesterday." 'Umar stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, strike their necks." The Prophet ﷺ turned away from him. Then the Prophet ﷺ returned and said the same thing to the people. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we think you should pardon them and accept ransom from them." He said: The distress that was on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed, so he pardoned them and accepted ransom from them. He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed: ﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already preceded...﴾ to the end of the verse. [[al-Musnad (3/243).]]

The hadith of Ibn 'Abbas in Sahih Muslim, similar to this, has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

Al-A'mash said, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah: When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What do you say about these captives?" He said: Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your people and your family. Spare them and let them repent, perhaps Allah will accept their repentance." He said: 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, they expelled you and denied you, so bring them forward and strike their necks." He said: 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are in a valley full of firewood, so set the valley ablaze upon them, then throw them into it." [He said: al-'Abbas said: "You have severed your ties of kinship."] [[Addition from D, K, M, al-Musnad and al-Tabari.]] He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell silent and did not answer them at all, then he stood up and entered. Some people said: he will take the view of Abu Bakr. Some people said: he will take the view of 'Umar. Some people said: he will take the view of 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to them and said: "Indeed Allah softens the hearts of some men until they are softer than milk, and indeed Allah hardens the hearts of other men until they are harder than stones. And your example, O Abu Bakr, is like that of Abraham, peace be upon him, who said: ﴿Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Ibrahim: 36]. And your example, O Abu Bakr, is like that of Jesus, peace be upon him, who said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 118]. And your example, O 'Umar, is like that of Moses, peace be upon him, who said: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 88]. And your example, O 'Umar, is like that of Noah, peace be upon him, who said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dwelling-place﴾ [Nuh: 26]. You are dependent, so none of them should escape except by ransom or by striking the neck." Ibn Mas'ud said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, except Suhayl ibn Bayda', for he mentions Islam." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell silent. I have never felt more fearful on any day that stones from the sky would fall upon me than I did on that day, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Except Suhayl ibn Bayda'." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives...﴾ to the end of the verse.

This was narrated by Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, and by al-Hakim in his al-Mustadrak, who said: "Its chain is sahih (authentic), though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." [[al-Musnad (1/383); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3084); al-Mustadrak (3/21). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan (good) hadith, and Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abd Allah did not hear from his father."]] Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also narrated, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, something similar. [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (4/104, 107).]] And there is a related report from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, and the wording is his, and al-Hakim in his al-Mustadrak, from the hadith of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa: Israil narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: When the captives were taken on the day of Badr, al-'Abbas was among those taken captive. A man from the Ansar captured him. He said: The Ansar had threatened that they would kill him. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I did not sleep last night because of my uncle al-'Abbas, and the Ansar claim that they will kill him." 'Umar said to him: "Shall I go to them?" He said: "Yes." So 'Umar went to the Ansar and said to them: "Release al-'Abbas." They said: "No, by Allah, we will not release him." 'Umar said to them: "But if the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is content?" They said: "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is content, then take him." 'Umar took him, and when he was in his hand he said to him: "O 'Abbas, embrace Islam, for by Allah, your becoming Muslim is more beloved to me than that al-Khattab should become Muslim, and that is only because I saw that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is pleased by your Islam." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr said: "They are your kinsmen; release them." Then he consulted 'Umar, and he said: "Kill them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then ransomed them, and Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a great slaughter upon the land...﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sahih (authentic), though they did not record it." [[al-Mustadrak (2/329). al-Dhahabi said: "On the condition of Muslim."]]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Hisham (that is, Ibn Hassan), from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Badr and said: "Give your companions the choice regarding the captives: if they wish, they may take ransom, or if they wish, they may kill them, on condition that a number of them equal to them be killed in the future." They said: "Ransom, and some of us will be killed."

This was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, from the hadith of al-Thawri, with this chain. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1567); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (8662). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib (rare) hadith from the hadith of al-Thawri; we only know it from the hadith of Ibn Abi Za'idah."]] This is an extremely gharib hadith.

Ibn 'Awn [from Muhammad ibn Sirin] [[Addition from al-Mustadrak and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah.]] said, from 'Ubaydah, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the captives of the day of Badr: "If you wish, you may kill them; and if you wish, you may take ransom from them and benefit from the ransom, and then some of you will be martyred equal to their number." He said: The last of the seventy was Thabit ibn Qays, who was killed on the day of al-Yamamah, may Allah be pleased with him. [[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/140) and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/139), by the route of Ibrahim ibn 'Ar'arah who said: Azhar informed us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, from 'Ubaydah, from 'Ali. Ibn 'Ar'arah said: "I objected to Azhar about this, but he insisted on saying: 'Ubaydah from 'Ali.' " Al-Hakim declared it sahih and said: "On the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim)."]]

Among them are those who narrated this hadith from 'Ubaydah as mursal (a report in which a successor omits the companion from the chain). [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/67) by the route of Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Ibn 'Awn, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, as mursal.]] Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives...﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿a great punishment﴾. He said: The spoils of Badr, before Allah made them lawful for them. He said: The distress that was on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed, so he pardoned them and accepted ransom from them. He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed: ﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already preceded...﴾ to the end of the verse. [[al-Musnad (3/243).]]

The hadith of Ibn 'Abbas in Sahih Muslim, similar to this, has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

Al-A'mash said, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah: When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What do you say about these captives?" He said: Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your people and your family. Spare them and let them repent, perhaps Allah will accept their repentance." He said: 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, they expelled you and denied you, so bring them forward and strike their necks." He said: 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are in a valley full of firewood, so set the valley ablaze upon them, then throw them into it." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good﴾ to the end of the verse. Similarly al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Something similar was narrated from Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas'ud, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, and al-A'mash also, that the meaning of ﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already preceded﴾ is the decree for this Ummah concerning the permissibility of the spoils. This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him.

This view is supported by what al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given five things that none of the prophets before me was given: I was made victorious through terror (in the hearts of enemies) a distance of one month's journey; the earth was made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification; the spoils were made lawful for me, though they were not lawful for anyone before me; I was given the intercession; and every prophet was sent only to his own people, but I was sent to all of mankind." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (335); Sahih Muslim no. (521).]]

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The spoils were not made lawful for the black-headed ones (mankind) other than us." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (3085), by the route of Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr, from Za'idah, from al-A'mash with this wording similar. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith from the hadith of al-A'mash."]]

For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good, and fear Allah. Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. At that point they took ransom from the captives.

Imam Abu Dawud also narrated in his Sunan: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak al-'Ayshi narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-'Anbas, from Abu al-Sha'tha', from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set the ransom of the people of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period) on the day of Badr at four hundred. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2691).]]

The ruling concerning captives has been settled, according to the majority of the scholars, that the leader (imam) has a choice regarding them: if he wishes, he may kill them, as he did with the Banu Qurayzah; and if he wishes, he may release them for wealth, as he did with the captives of Badr; or he may release them in exchange for those of the Muslims who were captured, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did with that slave woman and her daughter, who were among the captives of Salamah ibn al-Akwa', when he returned them and took in exchange for them some of the Muslims who had been with the polytheists; and if he wishes, he may enslave whoever he has taken captive. This is the position of Imam al-Shafi'i and a group of scholars. There is another difference of opinion among the imams on this question, which is established in its proper place in the books of jurisprudence (fiqh).

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verse 70–71:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Al-Abbas ibn Abdullah ibn Mughaffal narrated to me, from some of his family, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of Badr: "I have come to know that some men from Banu Hashim and others have been taken out unwillingly; they have no need to fight us. So whoever among you encounters any of them—meaning from Banu Hashim—let him not kill him, and whoever encounters Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham, let him not kill him, and whoever encounters al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, let him not kill him, for he was only taken out under compulsion." Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah said: "Shall we kill our fathers, our sons, our brothers and our clans, and leave al-Abbas? By Allah, if I meet him, I will bridle him with the sword!" News of this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: "O Abu Hafs—" Umar said: By Allah, it was the first day that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me by that kunyah—"Is the face of the uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to be struck with the sword?" Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me, and I will strike his neck. By Allah, he has indeed become a hypocrite." Abu Hudhayfah would say after that: "By Allah, I do not feel safe from that word which I said, and I remain fearful of it, unless Allah expiates it for me through martyrdom." He was then killed as a martyr on the day of al-Yamamah, may Allah be pleased with him.

And with the same chain, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered the evening of the day of Badr, while the captives were held in bonds, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stayed awake for the first part of the night. His companions said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, why do you not sleep?" — and a man from the Ansar had captured al-Abbas — and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I heard the groaning of my uncle al-Abbas in his bonds." So they released him, and he fell silent, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slept.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The largest number of captives on the day of Badr who were ransomed was al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, because he was a wealthy man, so he ransomed himself for one hundred uqiyyah of gold.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Musa ibn Uqbah, Ibn Shihab said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that some men of the Ansar asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "Permit us to leave the ransom of our nephew al-Abbas." He said: "No, by Allah, you will not leave a single dirham of it." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4026)

Yunus ibn Bukayr said, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Urwah—and from al-Zuhri, from a group he named—who said: Quraysh sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the ransom of their captives, and every people ransomed their captive with what they agreed upon. Al-Abbas said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was indeed a Muslim!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah knows best about your Islam. If it is as you say, then Allah will reward you. But as for your outward appearance, it was against us, so ransom yourself and your two nephews: Nawfal ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and Aqil ibn Abi Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and your ally Utbah ibn Amr, brother of Banu al-Harith ibn Fihr." He said: "That is not with me, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "Then where is the wealth which you and Umm al-Fadl buried? You said to her: 'If I am struck down on this journey of mine, this wealth is for Bani al-Fadl, Abdullah, and Qutham.'" He said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I know that you are the Messenger of Allah; this is something no one knew except me and Umm al-Fadl. So reckon for me, O Messenger of Allah, what you have taken from me: twenty uqiyyah of wealth that was with me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No, that is something Allah the Exalted has given us from you." So he ransomed himself, his two nephews and his ally, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning him: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives: If Allah knows of any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and will forgive you, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Al-Abbas said: "Then Allah gave me, in place of the twenty uqiyyah, in Islam, twenty slaves, each of whom has wealth in his hand that he trades with, besides what I hope for of the forgiveness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Ibn Ishaq also narrated, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse, something similar to what preceded.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakih narrated to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us [from Ibn Ishaq], from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Abbas said: "It was concerning me that this was revealed: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted slaughter upon the land﴾." So I informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of my Islam and asked him to reckon with me the twenty uqiyyah that he had taken from me, but he refused, so Allah replaced them for me with twenty slaves, each of whom is a merchant, and my wealth is in his hand.

Ibn Ishaq also said: Al-Kalbi narrated to me, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, from Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Ri'ab, who said: Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib used to say: "By Allah, it was concerning me that this was revealed, when I mentioned my Islam to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)," and then he mentioned something similar to the preceding narration.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives﴾ refers to al-Abbas and his companions. He said: They said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We believe in what you have brought, and we testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, and we will indeed advise you concerning our people." So Allah revealed: ﴿If Allah knows of any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you﴾—faith and affirmation—"He will replace for you something better than what was taken from you" ﴿and will forgive you﴾ the polytheism you were upon. He said: Al-Abbas used to say: "I do not wish that this verse had not been revealed concerning us, and that I had the whole world, for He said: ﴿He will give you better than what was taken from you,﴾ and He has given me better than what was taken from me a hundredfold, and He said: ﴿and will forgive you,﴾ and I hope that I have been forgiven."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas, concerning this verse: Al-Abbas was taken captive on the day of Badr, and he ransomed himself for forty uqiyyah of gold. When this verse was recited, al-Abbas said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given us two things, and I would not wish to have the whole world in exchange for them: I was taken captive on the day of Badr and ransomed myself for forty uqiyyah, and He gave me forty slaves; and I hope for the forgiveness which Allah, His praise is exalted, has promised us."

Qatadah said in the explanation of this verse: It has been related to us that when the wealth of Bahrain, eighty thousand, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he had performed ablution for the noon prayer. On that day he gave to no one who was silent and withheld from no one who asked, and he did not pray that day until he had distributed it. He commanded al-Abbas to take from it and to fill his garment, and he took. He said: Al-Abbas would say: "This is better than what was taken from us, and I hope for forgiveness."

Ya'qub ibn Sufyan said: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, who said: Ibn al-Hadrami sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Bahrain eighty thousand; no wealth had ever come to him more abundant than it, neither before nor after. He said: It was spread upon a mat, and the call to prayer was made. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and stood over the wealth, and the people of the mosque came, and on that day there was no counting and no weighing; it was only handfuls. He said: Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib came carrying it in a cloak he wore, and he tried to rise but could not. He said: So he raised his head to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, lift it onto me." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled until his molars [or his canine teeth] showed, and said to him: "Take out some of the wealth, and stand up with what you can bear." He said: So he did, and al-Abbas began to say as he departed: "As for one of the two things Allah promised us, we have received it, and we do not know what He will do with the other." Then the verse: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives﴾ to the end of the verse, then he said: "This is better than what was taken from us, and I do not know what Allah will do in the Hereafter." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued leaning over that wealth until not a dirham of it remained, and he did not send any of it to his family, then he went to the prayer and prayed.

Another hadith on this: The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Tayyib Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Sa'idi informed me, Mahmash ibn Isam narrated to us, Hafs ibn Abdullah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to us, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Wealth from Bahrain was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Scatter it in the mosque."

He said: It was the largest wealth ever brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He went out to the prayer without looking at it, and when he had finished the prayer he came and sat beside it. He did not see anyone except that he gave to him. Then al-Abbas came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, give to me, for I ransomed myself and ransomed Aqil." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Take." So he scooped into his garment, then tried to lift it but could not, and said: "Command someone to lift it onto me." He said: "No." He said: "Then you lift it onto me." He said: "No." So he scattered some of it and then carried it on his shoulder and departed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to follow him with his gaze until he was out of sight, marveling at his greed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not rise while a single dirham of it remained.

Al-Bukhari narrated it in several places of his Sahih as a mu'allaq report in the form of certainty, saying: "Ibrahim ibn Tahman said," and he related it; and in some of its contexts it is more complete than this.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if they intend to betray you﴾, meaning in what they have shown you of words, ﴿then they have already betrayed Allah before﴾, meaning before Badr, by disbelieving in Him, ﴿so He gave you power over them﴾, meaning by their capture on the day of Badr, ﴿and Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: Knowing of what He does, Wise in it.

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh, the scribe, when he apostatized and joined the polytheists.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas: It was revealed concerning al-Abbas and his companions, when they said: "We will indeed advise you concerning our people."

As-Suddi explained it in a general sense, and that is more comprehensive and apparent, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verse 72:

Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the categories of the believers and divided them into Muhajirun (emigrants), who left their homes and their wealth, came seeking the victory of Allah and His Messenger and the establishment of His religion, and expended their wealth and their lives in that cause; and into Ansar (helpers), who were the Muslims of Madinah at that time, who sheltered their emigrant brothers in their homes, shared their wealth with them, and supported Allah and His Messenger by fighting alongside them. So "some of them are allies of others" means that each of them has a greater right to the other than anyone else. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established brotherhood (mu'akhah) between the Muhajirun and the Ansar, every two men being brothers, so they used to inherit from one another by this bond, a inheritance given precedence over blood relations, until Allah abrogated (naskh) that by the rules of inheritance. This is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn 'Abbas [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6747)]. Al-'Awfi and 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related it from him [al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/78)]. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others also said it.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sharik, from 'Asim, from Abu Wa'il, from Jarir — he is Ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Muhajirun and the Ansar are allies of one another, and the freed captives (tulaqa') of Quraysh and the freed slaves ('utaqa') of Thaqif are allies of one another until the Day of Resurrection." Ahmad alone related it [al-Musnad (4/363)].

And the Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Shaiban narrated to us, 'Ikrimah — meaning Ibn Ibrahim al-Azdi — narrated to us, 'Asim narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Muhajirun and the Ansar, and the freed captives of Quraysh and the freed slaves of Thaqif, are allies of one another in this world and the Hereafter." Thus he related it in the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud [Musnad Abi Ya'la (8/446), in which is 'Ikrimah ibn Ibrahim, weak].

Allah and His Messenger have praised the Muhajirun and the Ansar in more than one verse of His Book. He said: "And the foremost of the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them in goodness — Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow" — to the end of the verse [at-Tawbah: 100]. He said: "Allah has certainly turned in mercy to the Prophet and the Muhajirun and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship" — to the end of the verse [at-Tawbah: 117]. And Allah, exalted is He, said: "For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth, seeking bounty from Allah and approval, and supporting Allah and His Messenger; those are the truthful. And those who were settled in the abode and in faith before them love those who emigrate to them and find not in their breasts any need for what they have been given, and prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves are in poverty" — to the end of the verse [al-Hashr: 8–9].

The best that has been said concerning His words "and find not in their breasts any need for what they have been given" is that they do not envy them for the excess of what Allah gave them because of their emigration. The apparent meaning of the verses is that the Muhajirun are given precedence over the Ansar, and this is a matter on which the scholars agree; they do not differ concerning it. For this reason, the Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave me the choice between emigration (hijrah) and support (nusrah), and I chose emigration [Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2718), Kashf al-Astar, in which is 'Ali ibn Zayd, weak].

Then he said: "We do not know it except from this route."

* *

As for His words: "And those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of protection toward them until they emigrate" [Hamzah read "wilayatihim" with a kasrah, while the rest read it with a fathah; both are the same, like al-dilalah and al-dalalah] — this is the third category of the believers: those who believed but did not emigrate, rather remained in their dwellings. For these there is no share in the spoils, nor in its fifth, except what they were present for in fighting. As Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed a commander over a detachment or an army, he would enjoin him concerning his own person to fear Allah, and concerning the Muslims with him to do good, and he said: "Make war in the name of Allah, in the way of Allah. Fight those who disbelieve in Allah. When you meet your enemy from among the polytheists, invite them to one of three matters — or: qualities — and whichever of them they answer you with, accept it from them and refrain from them: invite them to Islam; if they respond, accept from them and refrain from them. Then invite them to move from their land to the land of the Muhajirun, and inform them that if they do so, they will have what the Muhajirun have and will bear what the Muhajirun bear. If they refuse and choose their own land, inform them that they will be like the Bedouin Muslims, the ruling of Allah applying to them as it applies to the believers, and they will have no share in the fay' and the spoils, unless they fight with the Muslims. If they refuse, invite them to pay the jizyah. If they respond, accept from them and refrain from them. If they refuse, seek help from Allah and fight them."

Muslim alone related it, and he has additional narrations [Musnad (5/352) and Sahih Muslim no. (1731)].

* *

As for His words: "And if they seek your help in religion, then it is incumbent upon you to help, except against a people between you and whom there is a treaty; and Allah is Seeing of what you do" — Allah, exalted is He, says: If these Bedouins, who did not emigrate, seek your help in a religious fight against an enemy of theirs, then help them, for it is obligatory upon you to help them, because they are your brothers in religion — except if they seek your help against a people of the disbelievers "between you and whom there is a treaty" (mithaq), i.e., a truce for a fixed period; so do not break your covenant, nor violate your oaths with those with whom you have made a pact. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.

When He, exalted is He, mentioned that the believers are allies of one another, He severed the bond of allegiance between them and the disbelievers, as al-Hakim said in his *Mustadrak*:

Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Hani narrated to us: Abu Sa'd (in all the copies "Abu Sa'id," corrected from the books of biographical evaluation) Yahya ibn Mansur al-Harawi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Aban narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yazid and Sufyan ibn Husayn narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Usama, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The people of two religions do not inherit from each other, a Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, and a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim." Then he recited: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others. If you do not do that, there will be turmoil in the land and great corruption.﴾ Then al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound, but the two (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it."[[al-Mustadrak (2/240).]]

I say: The hadith is in the *Sahihayn* (the two Sahih collections, of Bukhari and Muslim), narrated by Usama ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor does a disbeliever inherit from a Muslim."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6764), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1614).]] In the *Musnad* and the *Sunan* (collections), from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of two different religions do not inherit from each other."[[al-Musnad (2/195) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2911). I did not find it in Sunan al-Tirmidhi; rather, he referred to it at the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd, and Allah knows best.]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and sound).

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Muhammad narrated to us, [from Muhammad ibn Thawr][[Addition from M, A, and al-Tabari.]] from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a pledge from a man who had entered Islam, saying: "You establish the prayer, give the zakat, perform the pilgrimage to the House, fast Ramadan, and that you do not see the fire of a polytheist except that you are at war with him."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/82).]]

This is a *mursal* (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain) through this route. It has been narrated connected (*muttasil*) by another route from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "I am free of every Muslim who dwells among the polytheists," then he said: "Their fires should not be visible to each other."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (2645), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (1604), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (8/36), from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Abu Dawud said at the end of the Book of Jihad: Muhammad ibn Dawud ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Yahya ibn Hassan informed me: Sulayman ibn Musa Abu Dawud informed us: Ja'far ibn Sa'd ibn Samura ibn Jundub narrated to us, [Khubayb ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from his father Sulayman ibn Samura][[Addition from D, K, M, and Abu Dawud.]] from Samura ibn Jundub: "To proceed: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever mingles with the polytheist and dwells with him, then he is like him.'"[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2787).]]

The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh mentioned, from the hadith of Hatim ibn Isma'il, from 'Abd Allah ibn Hurmuz, from Muhammad and Sa'id, the two sons of 'Ubayd, from Abu Hatim[[In A: "Hazim."]] al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If there comes to you one whose religion and character you are pleased with, then marry him to her. If you do not do so, there will be turmoil in the land and widespread corruption." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, even if he is...?" He said: "If there comes to you one whose religion and character you are pleased with, then marry him," three times.[[In K: "tafʿaluh."]]

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, from the hadith of Hatim ibn Isma'il, with the same meaning.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Maraasil, no. (224), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (1085).]]

Then it was narrated from the hadith of 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Sulayman, from Ibn[[In A: "Abi."]] 'Ajlan, from Ibn Wathima al-Nasri[[In A: "Ibn Abi Wathima al-Nasri."]], from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If there comes to you one whose character and religion you are pleased with, then marry him. If you do not do so, there will be turmoil in the land and widespread corruption."[[Also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (1084), by the route of 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Sulayman with it, and he said: "The hadith of Abu Hurayra was opposed by 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Sulayman in this hadith; al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated it from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a mursal (report). Then he said: The hadith of al-Layth is more likely (correct), and he did not consider the hadith of 'Abd al-Hamid to be preserved (mahfuz)."]]

The meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you do not do that, there will be turmoil in the land and great corruption﴾ is: if you do not keep away from the polytheists and take the believers as allies, then turmoil will occur among the people, which is the confusion of the matter and the mixing of the believer with the disbeliever, so widespread corruption, far-reaching and extensive, will befall the people.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 8, verse 74–75:

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the ruling concerning the believers in this world, He followed it with mention of what is theirs in the Hereafter. He informed about them with the reality of faith, as has preceded at the beginning of the surah, and that He will reward them with forgiveness and pardon for their sins, if they had any, and with generous provision (rizq karim), which is good, abundant, pure and noble, lasting and continuous forever, never cut off nor coming to an end, and never tiring nor becoming wearisome, because of its goodness and variety.

Then He mentioned that the followers (al-atba') have, in this world, the same standing as those who preceded them in faith and righteous deeds, so they will be with them in the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them in excellence - Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [At-Tawbah: 100], and He said: ﴿And those who came after them say, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and put not in our hearts any resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful"﴾ [Al-Hashr: 10]. And in the hadith agreed upon (al-muttafaq 'alayh), rather mutawatir through sound chains, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "A man is with whom he loves" ("al-mar' ma'a man ahabb"). And in another hadith: "Whoever loves a people will be gathered with them" [[Narrated from the hadith of Abu Qarafa and Jabir. As for the hadith of Jabir, al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/19) through the route of Ziyad from 'Izza bint 'Iyad from Abu Qarafa, raised, with the wording: "Whoever loves a people, Allah will gather him in their company," and in its chain is one who is not known. Al-Khatib narrated it in his Tarikh (5/196) through the route of Isma'il ibn Yahya from Sufyan from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil from Jabir, raised, with the wording: "Whoever loves a people for their deeds will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in their company, and will be reckoned with their reckoning, even if he does not do their deeds," and Isma'il ibn Yahya is weak.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sharik, from 'Asim, from Abu Wa'il, from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Muhajirun and the Ansar are allies of one another, and the Tulaqa' of Quraysh and the 'Utaqa' of Thaqif are allies of one another until the Day of Resurrection." Sharik said: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Tamim ibn Salama, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hilal, from Jarir, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.

Ahmad alone narrated it through these two routes [[al-Musnad (4/343).]].

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Decree of Allah﴾, meaning: in the judgment of Allah. The intended meaning of ﴿blood relatives﴾ is not the specific category that the scholars of the obligatory shares (ulama' al-fara'id) apply to kinsmen who have no fixed share and are not 'asabah, but who are connected through an heir, such as the maternal aunt, the maternal uncle, the paternal aunt, children of daughters, children of sisters, and the like, as some of them claim and argue with the verse, and hold this view explicitly in the matter. Rather, the truth is that the verse is general, encompassing all kinds of kinship, as stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others, that it abrogated inheritance by alliance and brotherhood by which they used to inherit from one another or not. On this basis, it includes the dhawu al-arham by the specific term. And whoever does not grant them inheritance argues with evidence, the strongest of which is the hadith: "Indeed Allah has given every rightful person his right, so there is no bequest to an heir," and they said: If he were one with a right, he would have a named share in the Book of Allah; since he has none, he is not an heir. And Allah knows best.

End of the [commentary on] Surah "al-Anfal", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace, and in Him is trust and reliance, and He is our sufficiency and the best Disposer of affairs.
